docs.description: Deprecated: write each step as its own BottomSheet with isOpen, controlled by one state value that names the open step. Closing the top sheet and opening the next in the same update, from a control inside the open step, runs the same replace handoff (see BottomSheet, Replacing a sheet), with no sheetId and no switcher; a step changed from a control outside the flow (a page control, or code after focus left the step) closes and opens with ordinary push and pop motion. BottomSheetSwitcher keeps working until a future minor release removes it: a flow used on its own behaves as released (with three fixes: a toast raised from a step renders above the flow and can be pressed, under reduced motion its steps follow the reduced-motion rule, and a step with a hasAutoFocus field opens on that field in every browser), and a flow stacked with other sheets is one level of the stack (it recedes and is blocked when covered, shares the one scrim, and stands down from dismissal while covered). Modal and hasScrim={false} flows migrate the same way. Coordinates multiple BottomSheets as a mutually exclusive flow. One activeSheet ID selects the only interactive sheet; during a handoff, the new sheet enters above the inert previous sheet. If the new sheet is shorter, the previous sheet simultaneously moves down until their top edges align, then fades after both transforms complete. Each child sheet renders its own native <dialog>: a modal flow presents each sheet with showModal(), as a standalone modal sheet does, so the browser supplies modality (the page is inert and focus stays in the top-layer dialog, so both hold across a handoff) and the switcher holds the shared body scroll lock once for the whole modal flow. A no-scrim flow presents each sheet with show() inside the isolated flow wrapper of the switcher, which orders the step dialogs with local values; this differs from a standalone hasScrim={false} sheet, which is hosted in the top layer as a manual popover with no page-level z-index, and it is one reason to migrate. The switcher coordinates the rest: one scrim paints at a time, focus returns to the element that opened the flow, its ref, id, and data-testid resolve to the dialog hosting the active sheet, and its other dialog props and handlers apply to every sheet dialog.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref resolved to the native dialog hosting the flow: the active sheet's dialog, which changes to the next sheet's on a handoff; the exiting sheet's through its exit; and, while the flow is closed, the dialog that hosted it last (or the first mounted sheet's). It is never null while a sheet is mounted, from the first commit on. id and data-testid render on this dialog only: a flow that mounts open carries them on the active sheet's dialog in server markup too; a flow that mounts closed carries them from the first commit's synchronous re-render on, and its server markup carries them on no element. Other dialog props apply to every sheet dialog.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Called before the switcher handles a native cancel request (Escape or the platform close). Attached to every sheet dialog; the browser raises cancel on the dialog it is presenting, the active sheet's. Calling preventDefault() keeps the controlled flow open.

props.name: activeSheet
props.description: ID of the interactive BottomSheet, or null when the flow should close. Match a nested BottomSheet's unique sheetId; the previous sheet may remain visually present and inert while the new sheet enters, simultaneously align downward behind a shorter step, then fade away.

props.name: onActiveSheetChange
props.description: Called with null when the active sheet dismisses according to its purpose. Child BottomSheets may use purpose='form' or purpose='required' to limit implicit dismissal while flow controls can still use the same state setter to switch sheets or close the flow.

props.name: hasScrim
props.description: Whether the sheet dialogs are modal. true presents each sheet with showModal() for a native ::backdrop, native focus containment, one body scroll lock held for the whole flow, and click-to-dismiss when the active BottomSheet has purpose='info'; only one backdrop paints at a time. false uses show() with no backdrop and leaves the page interactive; avoid transformed, contained, or clipping ancestors because a non-modal dialog remains in its containing context.

props.name: children
props.description: BottomSheets identified by unique sheetId values.

anatomy.name: Sheet dialogs
anatomy.description: One native dialog per child sheet, presented and closed by the switcher; the dialog hosting the active sheet carries the flow's ref, id, modality, and dismissal.

anatomy.name: Sheet panels
anatomy.description: Direct BottomSheet children; exactly one is interactive while a previous panel may remain visible and inert during a handoff.

anatomy.name: Scrim
anatomy.description: Native dialog backdrop shown by the default scrim-backed modal presentation; one sheet dialog paints it at a time, so a handoff never dims the page twice.

usage.description:
Deprecated: write each step as its own BottomSheet with isOpen, controlled by one state value that names the open step. Closing the top sheet and opening the next in the same update, from a control inside the open step, runs the same replace handoff (see BottomSheet, Replacing a sheet), with no sheetId and no switcher; a step changed from a control outside the flow (a page control, or code after focus left the step) closes and opens with ordinary push and pop motion. BottomSheetSwitcher keeps working until a future minor release removes it: a flow used on its own behaves as released (with three fixes: a toast raised from a step renders above the flow and can be pressed, under reduced motion its steps follow the reduced-motion rule, and a step with a hasAutoFocus field opens on that field in every browser), and a flow stacked with other sheets is one level of the stack (it recedes and is blocked when covered, shares the one scrim, and stands down from dismissal while covered). Modal and hasScrim={false} flows migrate the same way. Set activeSheet to a nested BottomSheet's sheetId to open or switch steps, and to null to close.

Stacking. A scrim flow is one level in the stack of open sheets (see BottomSheet, Stacking). Open it while a standalone sheet is open and the flow sits on top of that sheet, which recedes and is blocked; open a standalone sheet while the flow is open, from a step's content or from anywhere else, and that sheet sits on top while the whole flow recedes as one. Switching the step in place never changes the flow's position. Escape, the scrim, a swipe, and a platform close request reach only the top level: the flow's onActiveSheetChange(null) when the flow is on top, the standalone sheet's onOpenChange(false) when that sheet is. A standalone sheet rendered inside a step's content is presented only while that step is the active one: it leaves when the flow switches step or closes, its isOpen stays yours, and it is presented again, on top, if the step returns while it is still open. Only the bottom level's backdrop dims the page. A no-scrim flow stays out of the stack.

bestPractices.description: Prefer one standalone BottomSheet per step with one state value naming the open step; the replace handoff is the same and nothing has to be nested under a switcher.

Migrate an existing flow in place: replace activeSheet / onActiveSheetChange with one step value, give each step isOpen={step === id} and a guarded onOpenChange (clear the step only if it is still the open one) in place of sheetId, remove the wrapper and move its hasScrim onto every step. Map the other switcher props: onCancel becomes a guarded onOpenChange on each step (ignore false while the flow must stay open) — a standalone sheet reports Escape, the platform close, the scrim tap and the swipe all as onOpenChange(false) with no reason, so the guard holds the step against all of them while it applies, and a veto of Escape alone has no equivalent; the only per-path lever is purpose (form keeps Escape and blocks the scrim tap and the swipe; required blocks all three and exposes the step as an alertdialog). A consumer aria-label or aria-labelledby becomes each step label, which names its dialog. ref, id, data-testid, className, style, xstyle and the other dialog props have no dialog-level equivalent: a standalone sheet sends its ref and base props to the panel div and its dialog is implementation, so a test or anchor that needs the dialog queries the panel closest("dialog"), and dialog-level styling is dropped.
Don't split information across sheets when people need to compare it; use a full-page layout that keeps the relevant content visible together instead.
Don't use a step flow when multiple panels must stay interactive or visible together; a flow intentionally selects one interactive step.

examples.label: Replacement: the same three-step flow as standalone sheets
examples.code:
const [step, setStep] = useState(null);

<>
  <Button label="Start" onClick={() => setStep('details')} />
  <BottomSheet isOpen={step === 'details'} onOpenChange={o => !o && setStep(c => (c === 'details' ? null : c))} label="Details" height="hug">
    <SetupDetails />
    <Button label="Continue" onClick={() => setStep('preferences')} />
  </BottomSheet>
  <BottomSheet isOpen={step === 'preferences'} onOpenChange={o => !o && setStep(c => (c === 'preferences' ? null : c))} label="Preferences" height="hug">
    <Preferences />
    <Button label="Back" onClick={() => setStep('details')} />
    <Button label="Continue" onClick={() => setStep('confirm')} />
  </BottomSheet>
  <BottomSheet isOpen={step === 'confirm'} onOpenChange={o => !o && setStep(c => (c === 'confirm' ? null : c))} label="Confirm" height="hug">
    <Confirmation />
    <Button label="Back" onClick={() => setStep('preferences')} />
    <Button label="Done" onClick={() => setStep(null)} />
  </BottomSheet>
</>

docs.name: Breadcrumbs

usage.description: Breadcrumbs show a trail of links from the root to the current page. Use them at the top of detail pages, settings panels, or anywhere the user needs to see where they are and navigate back up.

bestPractices.description: Place breadcrumbs above the page heading so the user sees their location before reading the content.
Keep labels short and match the page titles they link to: "Settings" not "Application Settings Page".
Use the supporting variant in dense UIs like admin panels or sidebars where the breadcrumb should be subtle.
Make the last item plain text, not a link; it represents the current page. The component does this automatically when you set isCurrent.

The component implements the WAI-ARIA APG Breadcrumb pattern: a labelled nav landmark wrapping an ordered list, with aria-current="page" on the current item. A crumb with a menu additionally implements the APG Menu Button pattern, opening on Enter, Space or ArrowDown and closing on Escape.
Give each trail its own label when a page renders more than one, so the nav landmarks stay distinguishable in a screen reader landmark list.
Use breadcrumbs as the primary navigation. They supplement a sidebar or top nav, not replace it.
Show breadcrumbs on top-level pages that have no parent; they add clutter without helping the user.
Let the trail grow beyond 5 levels. If you need more, consider simplifying the page hierarchy instead.
The built-in slash separator mirrors automatically in RTL. For a custom separator, leave Unicode-mirrored angle quotes such as › alone; mirror arrows and Icon separators once with rtlStyles.mirror.

Mirror a separator the bidi algorithm already mirrors. An angle-quote glyph such as › is Bidi_Mirrored, so it flips under RTL on its own and rtlStyles.mirror would flip it back. An arrow glyph such as → and any Icon separator are not, so those do need rtlStyles.mirror through xstyle.

usage.description: Button triggers an action when clicked. Use it for form submissions, confirmations, navigation, or any interaction that needs a clear call to action.

bestPractices.description: Reserve primary for the single most important action in the view. Use secondary or ghost for everything else based on emphasis.
Write labels that describe the action ("Save changes", "Delete account", "Send invite"), not vague labels like "OK" or "Click here".
Show a loading state for actions that take time, like saving or submitting, so the user knows it is working.
Always provide a label for icon-only buttons so screen readers can announce what the button does. Add a tooltip for sighted users.
For a dedicated icon-only button, use IconButton from '@astryxdesign/core/IconButton'. It is a separate component, not exported from '@astryxdesign/core/Button'.
Place more than one primary button in the same view; this dilutes the visual hierarchy.
Use the destructive variant without a confirmation step for irreversible actions like deleting data.
Use a button for navigation. If it only takes the user to another page, use a link instead. Buttons are for actions like saving, deleting, or submitting.

Restyle Button's `::before` (through `xstyle` or a `className` rule) and expect it to hold through a touch press: under a coarse primary pointer, while a press is on or fading, Button paints the press on that pseudo-element (`z-index: -1`, its opacity animated), so your styles merge into the press layer for that moment. At rest Button adds nothing there. Style a child element instead.

accessibility.name: Disabled appearance
accessibility.description: Disabled controls do not need to meet these contrast ratios.

components.name: ButtonGroup
components.description: Groups multiple buttons together with connected styling: shared borders, proper border-radius handling (only on outer edges), and horizontal or vertical orientation. Under the touch presentation a press tracks like a menu: press a button and slide across the others, and the highlight follows. The button you lift on runs, and lifting outside the group runs nothing. A mouse press acts as a native button's. With a finger, each button's target grows toward 44 px, up to half the gap to a neighbour, without the buttons growing. A menu trigger in the group keeps its own opening.

accessibility.name: Essential icon or spinner arc

bestPractices.description: Group buttons that perform related actions on the same object, like copy, cut, paste on selected text.
Use the same variant for all buttons in a group so they look like a single connected unit.
Keep groups small (2–4 buttons). For more actions, use a Toolbar or DropdownMenu instead.
Don't mix wildly different actions. A Save button next to a Delete button in the same group is confusing.
Don't use ButtonGroup for navigation. Use SegmentedControl or TabList for switching between views.
Don't nest ButtonGroups. If you need multiple groups, place them side by side with a gap.
Name the group for what its buttons act on. The label is the group's accessible name and a screen reader reads it before each member.

Keep the group a single Tab stop. Arrow keys move between members along the orientation, and Home/End jump to the ends. This is the WAI-ARIA APG roving tabindex technique: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_roving_tabindex
Don't disable the group to show that an action is in flight. Leave the group enabled and show progress on the button that started the work.

按钮组是单个 Tab 停靠点。方向键沿排列方向在成员间移动焦点，Home/End 跳到首尾，禁用成员会被跳过——即 WAI-ARIA APG 的 roving tabindex 技术。
不要用禁用整个按钮组来表示操作进行中。请保持按钮组可用，并在发起操作的按钮上显示进度。

usage.description: Calendar lets the user pick a date or date range from a month grid. Use it in booking flows, scheduling UIs, date filters, or anywhere the user needs to see surrounding dates for context.

bestPractices.description: Set min and max dates to limit selection to a valid window, like only future dates for a booking or the current quarter for a report.
Use range mode when the user needs to pick a start and end date, like a trip or a time-off request.
Use dateConstraints to disable specific dates like weekends or holidays, and explain why they are unavailable.
Show two months side by side when the user frequently selects dates that span a month boundary.

For a custom month view, use useCalendarNavigation and useCalendarDays from @astryxdesign/core/Calendar. To show another calendar system, pass the same calendar to both and feed visibleCalendarMonths into useCalendarDays. The hooks default to gregory and never read the InternationalizationProvider calendar.
Use a calendar for dates far in the past or future like a birth date. A text input is faster for open-ended entry.
Disable large blocks of dates without context. The user should understand why dates are unavailable.

anatomy.description: One day in the grid; the control a date is picked with.

anatomy.description: The currently selected date, highlighted. In range mode, the start and end dates plus the days between them.

anatomy.name: Today marker
anatomy.description: A subtle indicator on the current date for orientation.

props.description: Selection mode.

props.description: Controlled selected value. Use null for no selection; omit value or pass undefined for uncontrolled mode.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Uncontrolled default value.

props.description: Selection callback.

props.description: Number of months to display.

props.description: Minimum selectable date.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum selectable date.

props.name: dateConstraints
props.description: Custom constraint functions.

props.name: maxRangeSpan
props.description: Range mode: max days a range may span, both endpoints counted (7 = a 7-day window). Caps the window from the picked start; before a start is picked every day stays selectable.

props.name: minRangeSpan
props.description: Range mode: min days a range must span, both endpoints counted (2 forbids a single-day range). Clicking the start again commits a one-day range when allowed, or cancels the in-progress selection when the minimum is longer. Default 1.

props.description: Controlled visible month. Unset, the calendar opens on the selected date, else on today clamped into the min/max window.

props.name: hasWeekNumbers
props.description: Show ISO 8601 week numbers. They are ISO 8601 week numbers in every calendar system.

props.name: hasVariableRowCount
props.description: Give each month only the rows it needs. The default fixed 6-row grid keeps the same height from month to month; a variable row count trades that fixed height for a more compact grid.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: First day of week. Accepts a number (0=Sunday) or a three-letter day name (e.g. "mon").

props.name: calendar
props.description: Calendar system the grid shows, such as 'persian', 'hebrew', or 'islamic-umalqura'. It sets the months, their names, and month and year navigation. value, min, max, focusDate, and every callback stay Gregorian ISO dates. Calendars other than gregory, iso8601, buddhist, roc, and japanese need Temporal; where the runtime lacks it, load a polyfill such as temporal-polyfill/full/global on the server and in the browser, or the grid shows Gregorian months. Month starts in the Chinese and Dangi calendars come from the runtime's Temporal, and some polyfills start a few months one day apart from native Temporal; when server and browser markup must match, use one implementation on both sides, such as installImplementation() from temporal-polyfill/full/shim, which replaces a native Temporal.

params.name: options
params.description: Configuration for date bounds, range-span limits, and custom rules.

params.name: options.min
params.description: Earliest selectable date in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD). Dates strictly before this are disabled.

params.name: options.max
params.description: Latest selectable date in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD). Dates strictly after this are disabled.

params.name: options.dateConstraints
params.description: Custom date constraint predicates. Receives a native Date; if any returns false, the date is disabled.

params.name: options.maxRangeSpan
params.description: Maximum days a range may span, counting both endpoints (a value of 7 allows a 7-day window). Inactive until rangeAnchor is set.

params.name: options.minRangeSpan
params.description: Minimum days a range must span, counting both endpoints. Disables dates that would make the range shorter than minRangeSpan days (except rangeAnchor itself, which remains enabled so pickers forbidding single-day selections must refuse a second click on the anchor).

params.name: options.rangeAnchor
params.description: The in-progress range start date. Span constraints are measured from this date. Null when no selection is underway.

returns.name: isDateDisabled
returns.description: Predicate returning true when a PlainDate falls outside min/max bounds, is closer to rangeAnchor than minRangeSpan allows (except rangeAnchor itself), exceeds maxRangeSpan relative to rangeAnchor, or fails any dateConstraints predicate.

returns.name: minDate
returns.description: Parsed minimum date as a PlainDate object, or null if min was not provided.

returns.name: maxDate
returns.description: Parsed maximum date as a PlainDate object, or null if max was not provided.

usage.description: Provides date constraint validation for calendar views and custom range pickers. It combines boundary dates, span limits measured from an in-progress range start, and custom rules (such as weekly closures or blackout dates) into an isDateDisabled predicate. Calendar uses it internally to disable day buttons; use it directly when building bespoke scheduling interfaces or range pickers.

bestPractices.description: Pass rangeAnchor only after the user selects an initial range start, so all eligible start dates remain selectable before the first click.
Use dateConstraints for recurring or dynamic rules, such as disabling closed weekdays, past holidays, or sold-out dates.
Perform slow network calls or heavy calculations inside dateConstraints predicates, because isDateDisabled is evaluated synchronously for each day rendered in the grid.

docsDense.description: Provides date constraint validation combining min/max bounds, range-span caps relative to rangeAnchor, and custom rule functions into isDateDisabled.

paramDescriptions.options.dateConstraints: Array of predicates returning false for disabled dates.
paramDescriptions.options.maxRangeSpan: Max days in range counting endpoints, measured from rangeAnchor.
paramDescriptions.options.minRangeSpan: Min days in range counting endpoints, measured from rangeAnchor.
paramDescriptions.options.rangeAnchor: Active range start PlainDate for span constraints.

returnDescriptions.isDateDisabled: Function returning true if PlainDate violates any constraint.

usage.description: Combines bounds, spans, and predicates into isDateDisabled for calendar and date-picker layouts.

bestPractices.description: Set rangeAnchor only while actively picking a range end.
Use dateConstraints for recurring blackout dates or closures.
Run expensive computation inside dateConstraints.

params.name: options
params.description: The month to lay out and how.

params.name: options.year
params.description: Year of the month to lay out, as options.calendar numbers it.

params.name: options.month
params.description: The month's position in its year under options.calendar, 1-based. In the Gregorian calendar 1 is January and 12 is December; other calendars number months as Temporal.PlainDate does, so a Hebrew leap year runs from 1 to 13.

params.name: options.weekStartsOn
params.description: First day of the week, from 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday). It sets the first column of both the grid and dayNames.

params.name: options.hasVariableRowCount
params.description: Use only as many week rows as the month needs instead of a fixed 6-row grid. That is 4 to 6 for a Gregorian month, and 1 or 2 for the short thirteenth month of the Coptic and Ethiopic calendars.

params.name: options.calendar
params.description: The calendar system that numbers year, month and each day's dayNumber. Every day keeps its Gregorian date and iso. The hook never reads the InternationalizationProvider calendar. Calendars other than gregory, iso8601, buddhist, roc and japanese need Temporal; without it the hook uses Gregorian numbers and warns once in development.

returns.name: days
returns.description: Every cell of the grid in order, including the days from the previous and next months that fill the first and last weeks. Each day has date (a PlainDate), iso (YYYY-MM-DD), isOutside (true for a day outside the month) and dayNumber (its day of the calendar month).

returns.name: weeks
returns.description: The same days grouped into rows of seven.

returns.name: dayNames
returns.description: Weekday header names for the current locale (from InternationalizationProvider), starting at weekStartsOn. Abbreviated where every name fits the column, otherwise the locale's narrow names.

returns.name: totalCells
returns.description: Number of cells in the grid: 42 for the fixed grid, otherwise rows times seven.

usage.description: Builds the day grid for one month: every date to show, including the previous and next months' days that fill the first and last weeks, grouped into weeks, plus localized weekday header names that start on weekStartsOn. It is the layout Calendar uses, for a custom month view such as a compact availability grid or a mini calendar. It returns data only: rendering, selection, keyboard navigation and the grid's accessibility semantics are the caller's.

bestPractices.description: Render dayNames as the header row so the header follows weekStartsOn and the locale together with the grid.
Style days with isOutside differently, for example dimmed, so the filler days read as part of the next or previous month.
Use it to build a date picker that people choose from; use Calendar, which adds selection, keyboard navigation and grid semantics.

docsDense.description: Builds one month's day grid: every date incl. previous/next month filler days, grouped into weeks, + localized weekday names starting at weekStartsOn. Calendar's layout, for custom month views. Data only: rendering, selection, keyboard nav, a11y semantics are the caller's.

paramDescriptions.options.year: year of the month, numbered by options.calendar.
paramDescriptions.options.month: month's position in its options.calendar year, 1-based (gregory 1 = January; Hebrew leap year 1-13).

usage.description: Card is a bordered, elevated container for discrete, self-contained items: things you could reorder, remove, or interact with independently. Cards are NOT the default layout tool. Most content groups don't need a container at all; spacing and alignment create visual grouping naturally. Only reach for a Card when items need clear interaction boundaries or visual comparison in a grid.

bestPractices.description: Ask "could I reorder or remove this independently?" If yes, it's a card. If no, it's just a section of the page: use a heading + Stack or Section.
Use cards for discrete items: a single user profile, a single notification, a single metric, a product in a grid. Each card represents one "thing" with clear interaction boundaries.
Spacing and alignment alone create visual grouping. Not everything needs a container; try removing the card and see if the grouping is still clear from whitespace and typography.
Keep padding consistent across sibling cards so they align visually in a grid or list.
Pair a card with Layout when you need a structured header, scrollable content, and footer with actions.

Let cards share a row or grid on a phone: a card shrinks to fit its track and clips content that cannot wrap at its edge. Truncate long IDs, hashes, and URLs with Text maxLines={1} (the full value shows in a tooltip), and give wide content its own scroll region: Table scrolls by itself; put code or other wide content in a ScrollableArea.
Default to cards for visual grouping. A heading + Stack with proper spacing creates hierarchy without adding borders everywhere. Cards should be the exception, not the default.
Wrap page sections in cards. "General Settings", "Notification Preferences", form groups: these are page regions, use Section or heading + stack.
Create identical card grids (icon + heading + text, repeated). Vary the layout or question whether cards are needed at all.
Nest cards inside other cards; flatten the hierarchy or use spacing and dividers instead.
Use color variants for status; use Banner or Badge for that. Color cards are for categorization.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.description: Any children rendered inside the card. Often a stack of heading, text, and actions.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the card (number = pixels, string = used as-is). In a flex row or grid track this is the preferred width: the card shrinks below it when the row is narrower. To hold the width in a flex row, wrap the card in StackItem (static by default) and let the row wrap or scroll. In Grid, set a consumer minWidth on the Card and size the track accordingly.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the card (number = pixels, string = used as-is).

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum width of the card.

props.name: minHeight
props.description: Minimum height of the card.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render inside the card.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding using the spacing scale. Omit it and the card takes the theme's card padding rather than a step, so passing a step is a decision to override the theme, not a way to restate the default.
props.default: the theme's card padding (spacing step 4 with no theme)

props.name: variant
props.description: Background color variant. `default` uses the standard card background. `transparent` drops the background entirely. `muted` uses the muted background for de-emphasised cards. The non-semantic variants use the corresponding `--color-background-<name>` token.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth. `none` is flat; `low`/`med`/`high` map to the shadow token scale. Raise a card only when it needs to float above surrounding content.

Use cards for discrete items: a single user profile, a single notification, a single metric, a product in a grid. Each card represents one "thing" with clear interaction boundaries.
Spacing and alignment alone create visual grouping. Not everything needs a container; try removing the card and see if the grouping is still clear from whitespace and typography.
Keep padding consistent across sibling cards so they align visually in a grid or list.
Pair a card with Layout when you need a structured header, scrollable content, and footer with actions.

Let cards share a row or grid on a phone: a card shrinks to fit its track and clips content that cannot wrap at its edge. Truncate long IDs, hashes, and URLs with Text maxLines={1} (the full value shows in a tooltip), and give wide content its own scroll region: Table scrolls by itself; put code or other wide content in a ScrollableArea.
Default to cards for visual grouping. A heading + Stack with proper spacing creates hierarchy without adding borders everywhere. Cards should be the exception, not the default.
Wrap page sections in cards. "General Settings", "Notification Preferences", form groups: these are page regions, use Section or heading + stack.
Create identical card grids (icon + heading + text, repeated). Vary the layout or question whether cards are needed at all.
Nest cards inside other cards; flatten the hierarchy or use spacing and dividers instead.
Use color variants for status; use Banner or Badge for that. Color cards are for categorization.

usage.description: Carousel scrolls a row of items horizontally when they overflow the available width. Use it for card grids, image galleries, product lists, or any set of items that should be browsable without taking up the full page.

bestPractices.description: Enable scroll-snap when each item should land precisely at the start edge, like a gallery or product list.

For iOS paging under a finger and on a trackpad swipe, pass hasSnap={useSnapPaging()} from @astryxdesign/core/SnapPaging. A flick moves one view, or one item with useSnapPaging({pages: 'item'}). A mouse wheel keeps native snapping. Only a carousel given it loads the paging code.
Reach for hasLoop on small, cyclable sets like a photo gallery, where wrapping past the last item back to the first feels natural.
Always provide an aria-label that describes what the carousel contains, like "Featured products" or "Team members".

Carousel implements the WAI-ARIA APG carousel pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/) without auto-rotation: the region is labelled and carries aria-roledescription="carousel", each item is a group named "Slide N of M", and the scroll container is a tab stop while its content overflows, so keyboard users can pan it with the arrow keys; while everything fits it stays out of the tab order.
Use a consistent gap and item width so the carousel looks intentional, not like content overflowing by accident.
Trust the built-in navigation: trackpad users can swipe horizontally, and mouse users can hold Shift while scrolling the wheel to move through items.
Use a carousel for content every user must see. Not everyone scrolls horizontally, so put critical content above the fold.
Auto-advance items. Let the user scroll at their own pace.
Nest carousels. A carousel inside a carousel is confusing and breaks keyboard navigation.

usage.description: Carousel 在项目超出可用宽度时将一行项目水平滚动。适用于卡片网格、图片画廊、产品列表，或任何希望无需占据整页即可浏览的项目集合。

bestPractices.description: 当每个项目应精确对齐到起始边缘时启用滚动吸附，例如画廊或产品列表。
在小型可循环的集合（如照片画廊）上使用 hasLoop，此时从最后一项绕回第一项的滚动更自然。
始终提供描述轮播内容的 aria-label，例如"精选产品"或"团队成员"。
Carousel 实现不含自动轮播的 WAI-ARIA APG carousel 模式（https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/）：区域带有标签和 aria-roledescription="carousel"，每个项目是名为“第 N 张，共 M 张”的 group，滚动容器可获得焦点，键盘用户可用方向键平移。
使用一致的间距和项目宽度，让轮播看起来是有意为之，而不是内容意外溢出。
信任内置导航：触控板用户可水平滑动，鼠标用户可按住 Shift 滚动滚轮来浏览项目。
将每位用户都必须看到的内容放入轮播。并非所有人都会水平滚动，关键内容应放在首屏。
自动轮播项目。让用户按自己的节奏滚动。
嵌套轮播。轮播中嵌套轮播会造成困惑并破坏键盘导航。

propDescriptions.gap: 使用间距令牌比例的项目间距。

propDescriptions.hasLoop: 环绕滚动：在末尾按"下一个"回到开头，在开头按"上一个"跳到末尾。按钮在两端始终可见。仅在内容溢出时生效。
propDescriptions.hasSnap: 使每个子元素吸附到起始边缘。hasSnap 使用原生 CSS 滚动吸附。hasSnap={useSnapPaging()} 在相同吸附点上增加手指和触控板轻扫下的 iOS 分页：一次轻扫移动一屏，或用 useSnapPaging({pages: 'item'}) 移动一项。只有该值会加载分页代码。

propDescriptions.handleRef: 命令式句柄，暴露 scrollNext()、scrollPrev()、scrollTo(index)、canScrollNext() 和 canScrollPrev() 以进行编程式滚动控制。

usage.description: Center aligns content to the middle of its container. Use it for empty states, loading screens, login forms, or any content that should sit in the center of the available space.

bestPractices.description: Use a single-axis value only in horizontal writing, or after verifying the active writing mode. In vertical writing, the current implementation follows flex main/cross axes rather than the physical prop names.
In horizontal writing, give Center height when using axis="vertical"; centering needs available space on the selected flex axis.
Use isInline to center small elements like icons or badges within a line of text without breaking the text flow.
Keep semantic structure and accessible names on the content. Center is a layout-only container and does not add a role or label.
Wrap large page sections in Center. Use Layout or AppShell for page-level structure.
Use Center for horizontal lists of items. Use Stack with hAlign="center" instead.

usage.description: ChatComposer is the message-entry shell for a chat surface. It coordinates a controlled or uncontrolled draft, provides a default token-capable input and send/stop action, and arranges optional drawer, header, footer, and status content. Custom inputs and send controls can join the same value, submission, disabled, stop, and focus contract through useChatComposerContext().

docs.name: ChatComposerInput
docs.description: Rich text input for the chat composer. Supports trigger menus (type @ or / to open a typeahead), inline tokens rendered as badges, message history recall with ArrowUp/Down, paste/drop file handling, and a 16px iOS font-size floor to prevent input zoom. Pass it to ChatComposer's input slot when you need more than a plain textarea.

usage.description: Pass ChatComposerInput to ChatComposer's input slot when the draft needs trigger menus, inline tokens, history recall, dictation insertion, or file intake.

bestPractices.description: Use handleRef for programmatic text or token insertion; inserted text follows the same onChange pipeline as typing.
Use onFiles for files pasted or dropped onto the editor, and keep file validation and upload progress in the product layer.
Use custom token rendering for ordinary mentions or commands; prefer the structured badge form so tokens remain predictable and themeable.

props.description: Paste-as-token behavior. By default, plain-text pastes over 200 characters become expandable tokens. Pass false to keep every text paste inline, or provide useChatPasteAsToken() to customize the conversion.

props.description: Called when files are pasted or dropped onto the input. Use to handle attachments.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Called when the user presses Enter without Shift. The serialized value includes token placeholders.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Key-down handler invoked before the built-in Enter/history behavior (after any open trigger menu). The seam for platform-specific keys: call event.preventDefault() to suppress the default submit (e.g. newline on a touch keyboard), or act on the event yourself to add behavior (e.g. submit on Cmd/Ctrl+Enter). IME composition is always respected; Enter never submits mid-composition.

usage.description: ChatDictationButton is a toggle button that starts and stops voice dictation inside a chat composer. It pairs with useChatDictation to show a microphone icon when idle and animated frequency bars when listening. Place it in the sendActions slot of ChatComposer.

bestPractices.description: Place the dictation button in the sendActions slot of ChatComposer so it sits next to the send button where users expect voice input controls.
Pass an inputRef to useChatDictation so interim transcripts appear as ghost text in the composer input while the user speaks.
Enable hasSounds on useChatDictation to give users audio feedback when dictation starts and stops. This is especially helpful when the button's visual change is subtle.
Don't use the dictation button outside a chat composer context. It's designed for the composer's send-action layout, not as a standalone recording control.
Don't forget to handle the unsupported case. The button hides itself by default when the browser lacks SpeechRecognition, but you should still design the composer to work without it.

usage.description: Chat is a family of composable primitives for building AI and human chat experiences. Combine ChatLayout, ChatMessageList, ChatMessage, bubbles, system messages, tool calls, tokenized text, and ChatComposer to assemble complete conversations without reimplementing sender-aware layout, density, scrolling, or composer behavior.

bestPractices.description: Compose messages using MessageList > Message > Bubble for consistent sender-aware styling and density.
Set the density prop to control spacing globally: compact for sidebars, balanced for most views, spacious for long-form reading. Individual messages can override.
Use gap when top-level rows are independent (for example, LLM tool events or streamed blocks) and list spacing needs to be tuned separately from density.
Use the group prop on bubbles (first, middle, last) when a single sender sends multiple consecutive messages; it tightens corner radius to visually connect them.
Use ChatSystemMessage with variant="divider" for date separators and default for inline status notices like joins, leaves, or topic changes.
Put name on the first bubble and metadata on the last bubble in a message so they align with the bubble's inline padding.

Wrap custom in-message content (cards, attachments, citations) in a ghost bubble so it aligns with the bubble text column; add width="100%" when it should span the full message column instead of the default bubble width cap.
Provide an emptyState prop so new users see a clear prompt to start a conversation instead of a blank screen.
Use the ghost bubble variant for AI-style responses that show rich content like code blocks or markdown without a visible boundary.
Don't use ChatSystemMessage for sender content; it has no avatar, alignment, or bubble. Use ChatMessage with a sender role instead.
Don't put long or multi-line content in a system message; keep it to a single short sentence. If you need more, use a bubble or a card.
Don't nest ChatMessage inside another ChatMessage; each message is a standalone article element with its own sender context.
Don't apply a fixed height directly on the message list; wrap it in a sized container and let the list fill with flex: 1.
Don't mix filled and ghost bubble variants within the same sender's messages; pick one style per side and use it consistently.
Don't place metadata or names on both the bubble and the message wrapper; pick one based on whether the content has a bubble boundary.

usage.description: Chat 是一组用于构建 AI 和人工聊天体验的可组合基础组件。组合 ChatLayout、ChatMessageList、ChatMessage、气泡、系统消息、工具调用、标记文本和 ChatComposer，可构建完整对话，而无需重新实现发送者感知布局、密度、滚动或编写器行为。

bestPractices.description: 使用 MessageList > Message > Bubble 组合来获得一致的发送者感知样式和密度。
设置 density 属性来全局控制间距：compact 用于侧边栏，balanced 用于大多数视图，spacious 用于长篇阅读。
当同一发送者发送多条连续消息时，使用气泡的 group 属性（first、middle、last）来视觉上连接相关消息。
使用 ChatSystemMessage 的 variant="divider" 作为日期分隔线，使用 default 作为内联状态通知。
将 name 放在第一个气泡上，metadata 放在最后一个气泡上，使其与气泡的内边距对齐。
将自定义消息内容（卡片、附件、引用）包裹在 ghost 变体的气泡中，使其与气泡文本列对齐；需要占满消息列宽度时设置 width="100%"。
提供 emptyState 属性，让新用户看到开始对话的提示，而不是空白屏幕。
使用 ghost 气泡变体显示代码块或 Markdown 等富内容，无需可见边界。
不要将 ChatSystemMessage 用于发送者内容，它没有头像、对齐或气泡。请使用带有发送者角色的 ChatMessage。
不要在系统消息中放置冗长或多行内容，保持一句简短的话。如需更多内容，请使用气泡或卡片。
不要将 ChatMessage 嵌套在另一个 ChatMessage 内，每条消息都是独立的 article 元素。
不要直接在消息列表上应用固定高度，将其包裹在有尺寸的容器中，让列表以 flex: 1 填充。
不要在同一发送者的消息中混用 filled 和 ghost 气泡变体，每一侧选择一种样式并保持一致。
不要同时在气泡和消息包装器上放置 metadata 或 name，根据内容是否有气泡边界来选择。

docs.name: ChatLayout
docs.description: Layout shell for full chat interfaces. Messages flow in normal page flow, composer is fixed to the bottom with a frosted glass dock. Set density (compact/balanced/spacious) to control spacing, message max-width, and blur layer sizing. Includes built-in auto-scroll, a "New messages" scroll-to-bottom button, and a frosted glass blur layer behind the composer. By default the layout root is the scroll container; pass scrollRef to delegate scrolling to a parent element or the document body. Where the visual viewport shrinks for the software keyboard, the composer stays on top of the keyboard, and a conversation at its newest message stays there. In Chrome on Android the composer rides Gboard’s slides in step with them. In Safari on iOS (in the browser and as a home-screen app) and in Firefox for Android, it moves above the keyboard once the browser reports it. On a touch screen, in a top-level page, every way into the composer’s text (a tap, the keyboard’s previous and next buttons, Tab, the input’s focus()) focuses it without scrolling the page; under a mouse or inside an iframe the browser’s own focus applies. Where your page sets interactive-widget=resizes-content, Chrome on Android shrinks the page for the keyboard itself and the composer stays above it without moving (see the browser-support guide).

props.name: scrollRef
props.description: External scroll container ref. When provided, auto-scroll and scroll-to-bottom target this element instead of the layout root. Use when the chat is embedded in a page where a parent element or the document body scrolls.

props.name: density
props.description: Visual density: controls dock padding, message-area max-width and inline padding, and the height of the frosted glass blur layer.

usage.description: ChatLayout is the layout shell for full-page chat interfaces. It renders messages in normal page flow and docks the composer to the bottom with a frosted glass blur layer. Set the density prop to control spacing; it defaults to balanced. Use it to wrap ChatMessageList and ChatComposer for a complete chat experience with built-in auto-scroll and a scroll-to-bottom button.

bestPractices.description: Pass ChatMessageList as children and ChatComposer as the composer prop for a complete chat interface.
Provide an emptyState so new conversations show a prompt instead of a blank screen.
Use scrollRef when the chat is embedded in a page where a parent element handles scrolling.

Give a full-page ChatLayout a container 100dvh tall, not 100vh: where a phone browser's toolbar collapses, 100vh is the viewport with the toolbar hidden, so the composer would start below the screen's edge.
Don't apply a fixed height on the layout; let it fill its container with flex: 1.
Don't render multiple ChatLayout instances in the same scroll container; each expects to own its scroll context.

anatomy.name: Message area
anatomy.description: Scrollable region for messages. Renders children (typically ChatMessageList) in a flex column that pushes content to the bottom when the list is short.

anatomy.name: Frosted glass dock
anatomy.description: Sticky or fixed container at the bottom with a backdrop-blur layer. Houses the scroll button and composer. While a software keyboard is up it sits on top of the keyboard, and the message area gets room to scroll above it.

anatomy.name: Scroll-to-bottom button
anatomy.description: Appears when the user scrolls up or new messages arrive. Defaults to ChatLayoutScrollButton; pass null to hide or a custom element to override.

anatomy.name: Composer
anatomy.description: The input area for sending messages, typically ChatComposer. Docked at the bottom inside the frosted glass layer. In a top-level page on a touch screen, its wrapper (without the scroll button) is a group with no name. When the keyboard’s Done ends typing, focus rests on that group (it is no tab stop), so the next tap or Tab starts from the composer. It shows the focus ring after keyboard input only. Under a mouse or inside an iframe, the wrapper is a plain container.

anatomy.name: Empty state
anatomy.description: Centered placeholder shown when no messages exist. Use EmptyState for a consistent look.

docs.name: ChatMessageBubble
docs.description: Styled content container for the chat "bubble." Reads sender from parent ChatMessage context to auto-style the background. Use filled for standard messages and ghost when content needs alignment without a visible boundary. Supports name/metadata slots aligned with bubble padding, and multi-bubble grouping via the group prop for consecutive messages from the same sender.

props.name: children
props.description: Bubble content: text, Markdown, or any ReactNode.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant. 'filled' renders sender-colored background (default). 'ghost' renders transparent background but keeps padding for alignment.

props.name: name
props.description: Sender name rendered above the bubble, aligned with bubble text padding. Use on the first bubble in a message. Non-rendering scalar values (null, undefined, booleans, and the empty string) omit the aligned wrapper; numeric 0 remains aligned. If the first content is raw (no bubble), use ChatMessage's `name` prop instead.

props.name: metadata
props.description: Metadata content rendered below the bubble, aligned with bubble text padding. Use on the last bubble in a message. Non-rendering scalar values (null, undefined, booleans, and the empty string) omit the aligned wrapper; numeric 0 remains aligned. If the last content is raw (no bubble), use ChatMessage's `metadata` prop instead.

props.name: group
props.description: Position within a multi-bubble group. Controls corner radius reduction on the sender side. Leave unset for standalone bubbles (full radius).

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the bubble (number = pixels, string = used as-is). When set, replaces the default max(80%, 280px) width cap. Combine with variant="ghost" to let custom content (an artifact card, attachments) span the full message column.

docs.name: ChatTokenizedText
docs.description: Renders a text string with token patterns replaced by inline token content. Wrap any message body inside ChatMessageBubble to turn raw @mentions, #tags, or /commands into styled content. When no non-empty token matches or none are provided, the text renders as-is, so you can use ChatTokenizedText unconditionally on every message.

props.name: children
props.description: The plain text message containing serialized token values. Patterns matching a token's value are replaced with inline token content.

props.name: tokens
props.description: Token definitions using the same type as composer input. Each non-empty value is matched literally. Empty values are ignored. Structured tokens render a Badge, while custom tokens render caller content.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the root text wrapper. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

usage.description: Use ChatTokenizedText inside a chat message when stored plain text contains serialized token values that should be projected as inline badges or caller-rendered token content. Unmatched text is preserved exactly and empty token values are ignored so rendering always finishes.

bestPractices.description: Reuse the same token definitions for composer insertion and message rendering so serialized values and visible labels stay aligned.
Use non-empty, stable serialized values so every definition identifies real message text.
Use token labels as a substitute for the surrounding message text; the complete message must remain understandable in reading order.
Put component-owned interaction or accessibility behavior inside a custom token renderer; custom token content remains caller owned.

usage.description: ChatToolCalls displays tool or function call invocations from an LLM response. Pass an array of calls and the component handles the rest: a single call renders inline, while multiple calls collapse into a summary with the latest call visible at the surface. Use it anywhere an AI agent shows what actions it took.

bestPractices.description: Include a target string on every call so the user can see what the tool acted on: a file path, a shell command, or a search query.
Show a duration on completed calls so users can judge which tools are slow and understand why a response took time.
Provide a group label when the automatic count does not explain what the calls represent.
Provide resultDetail with a code block for calls that produce output (diffs for edits, terminal output for shell commands) so users can inspect results inline.
Set a unique key on each call item when streaming so React can animate additions without re-mounting completed rows.
Don't omit the status field. Without it the call defaults to complete, which is misleading for calls that are still running or have failed.
Don't display tool calls outside a chat message context; they are designed to sit inside an assistant message, not as standalone UI.
Don't use custom wrappers around individual calls; the component handles single vs. grouped layout automatically based on the array length.

anatomy.name: Status icon
anatomy.description: A themed semantic success/error icon, or a spinner while the call is pending or running.

anatomy.name: Tool name
anatomy.description: The function or tool name displayed in monospace: bash, edit, read, web_search, etc.

anatomy.name: Node badge
anatomy.description: A neutral pill badge showing which sandbox or environment ran the tool, like cli:remote-server or workspace.

anatomy.name: Target label
anatomy.description: The target of the action (a file path, command, or search query) shown after the tool name.

anatomy.name: Diff stats
anatomy.description: Green additions and red deletions counts for edit operations, displayed inline after the target.

anatomy.name: Duration
anatomy.description: Execution time shown on the trailing edge for completed calls.

anatomy.name: Group header
anatomy.description: A wrench icon with a call count, shown when multiple calls are present. Clicking toggles between the summary and the full list.

props.name: calls
props.description: Array of tool call data. Each item has name, status, target, duration, node, additions, deletions, stats, errorMessage, resultDetail, key, and data. status is one of 'pending', 'running', 'complete', or 'error' (defaults to 'complete').

props.name: label
props.description: Custom summary label shown for an expanded group. The translated call count is used when omitted.

props.name: isExpanded
props.description: Controlled expanded state for the group.

props.name: defaultIsExpanded
props.description: Default expanded state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Callback fired when the expanded state changes.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.description: The size of the checkbox. sm for compact layouts, md for default. Under a coarse pointer a labelled checkbox’s target grows toward 44 px through an invisible hit area. It never shrinks below the row and stops at half the gap to a closer neighbour; nothing changes size.

accessibility.name: Checkbox box
accessibility.description: The box edge (unchecked) and fill (checked) must have at least 3:1 contrast with the surface behind them. For Hover and Pointer down, measure the final colors after the tint and the pressed overlay are applied.

usage.description: CheckboxInput toggles a single on/off value. Use it for settings like "Enable notifications", terms acceptance, or opt-in choices. For multiple checkboxes in a group, use CheckboxList instead.

bestPractices.description: Always provide a visible label so the user knows what they are toggling. Use isLabelHidden only when surrounding context makes it obvious.
Add a description for choices that need extra context, like explaining what "Share usage data" actually shares.
Use the indeterminate state for "select all" checkboxes when only some items in a group are selected.
Use a checkbox for mutually exclusive choices; use RadioList when only one option can be selected.
Use a checkbox for actions that take effect immediately; use a toggle switch or button instead.
Wrap a disabled checkbox in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

usage.description: CheckboxList shows a small group of checkboxes so users can turn several options on or off at once. Place it in settings pages, filter panels, or forms where every choice should be visible without scrolling. For a single standalone checkbox (like "I agree to the terms"), use CheckboxInput instead. If only one option can be picked, use RadioList. If the list is long enough to need searching or scrolling, use MultiSelector instead.

bestPractices.description: Keep the list short: three to seven options is the sweet spot. Beyond that, switch to MultiSelector which adds search and scrolling.
Turn on dividers (hasDividers) when items have helper text underneath; without them the labels and descriptions blur together.
Write a group label that says what the choices represent: "Export formats" tells users more than "Options".
Show a CheckboxList when the user can only pick one thing; that is what RadioList is for.
Put buttons or links inside the trailing slot (endContent); the whole row is already tappable, so a nested button creates two competing click targets.
Wrap a disabled CheckboxList in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

vars.name: --_checkbox-row-press-paint
vars.description: The touch press paint a row that owns its checkbox's press hands that checkbox's box: none at rest, and the press paint at the press's strength while the touch press controller presses that row under a coarse pointer. Set on the row by its own press arms; the box reads its nearest row's value, so a list placed in a row's content keeps its own rows' paint.

docs.name: CheckboxListItem
docs.description: Individual checkbox item with label, description, and end content slot. Works in collection mode (inside a CheckboxList with a value array) or standalone mode (inside List, or inside a CheckboxList without value, such as a select-all item). On a touch screen (a coarse primary pointer), a toggleable row is one press target: a touch on the label, the description or the box itself shows the pressed state on the row and its checkbox together. Where the primary pointer is fine, the box keeps its own press.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary text label for the item. Rich labels may contain links or buttons, which keep their own behavior without toggling the item. A ReactNode label names the checkbox from its visible text; pass aria-label only when that text is absent, or include all visible label words in the override.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Plain-text accessible name for the checkbox, replacing the one derived from label. Applied to the checkbox control. Use it when a rich label has no visible text; otherwise the value must retain every visible label word.

props.name: value
props.description: Identity key. Required when the parent CheckboxList has a value array; the item throws without it there.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary content below the label. String or ReactNode. Exposed as the checkbox's accessible description through aria-describedby, so assistive technology can tell it is the explanation for that choice.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label area.

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment of the start and end content against the label, passed through to Item unchanged. `first-line` keeps a small mark (a checkbox) level with the first line of a wrapped label. See Item.align.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether this individual item is disabled.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether this item is loading. Shows a spinner inside the checkbox and blocks interaction on this item. In collection mode, the toggled item also shows this automatically while the parent changeAction is pending.

props.name: isChecked

docs.description: Fenced code block with syntax highlighting. Use for multi-line code snippets.

props.name: code
props.description: The code string to display.

props.name: language
props.description: Language for syntax highlighting. A string selects a built-in: ts, js, tsx, jsx, json, html, xml, svg, css, scss, less, python, bash/sh/zsh/shell, php, hack, yaml, markdown, c, cpp (c++, cc, cxx, hpp, hh), sql, rust, kotlin, swift, go. Any other language is a value you import on its own and pass here: graphql, java, thrift, objectiveC, toml, powershell, ruby, lua, dockerfile from @astryxdesign/core/CodeBlock/languages/<path> (e.g. languages/graphql, languages/objective-c), or your own made with createCodeLanguage({name, identifiers, tokenize}). A value labels with its name and reflects its first identifier as data-language. Use "plaintext" to disable.

props.name: title
props.description: Filename or label shown in the header bar.

props.name: hasLanguageLabel
props.description: Show the language name in the header bar. Hidden when language is "plaintext".

props.name: hasLineNumbers
props.description: Show a line number gutter.

props.name: startLineNumber
props.description: First line number shown in the gutter. The gutter shows file coordinates (startLineNumber + index) so a code excerpt reads with its real line numbers. highlightLines uses the same file coordinates. Values below 1 clamp to 1.

props.name: highlightLines
props.description: 1-indexed line numbers to highlight, in the same file coordinates as the gutter (see startLineNumber). Out-of-range entries render no highlight.

props.name: isDiff
props.description: Render the code as a unified diff over `language`: lines starting with + are added, - removed, @@ is a hunk header (a `--- `/`+++ ` file-header pair directly before one is a header too), anything else is context. The language label reads `diff` or `<language> diff`. The glyph sits in its own column and the rest of each line keeps syntax highlighting; copy returns the exact source. Markdown ```diff and ```diff-<lang> fences set this.

props.name: hasCopyButton
props.description: Show a copy-to-clipboard button.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Callback after the code is copied.

props.name: onCopyError
props.description: Called once with the rejection when the clipboard write fails. The copy button shows a cross and is named and announced as "Failed to copy value to clipboard."; the error is not shown.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Your own controls, shown just before Copy: in the header when the block has one, otherwise beside the code in the top inline-end corner, never over it. It never creates a header and never collapses the block. Ghost sm IconButtons match Copy’s size and variant.

props.name: isWrapped
props.description: Wrap long lines instead of enabling horizontal scroll.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Max height before the block scrolls vertically.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size variant.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the code block. Any CSS width value. 'fit-content' (default) shrinks to longest line. '100%' fills parent width.

props.name: container
props.description: Container presentation style. 'card' (default): border and radius with the muted syntax background for a standalone card look. 'section': no border or radius and a transparent background so the block blends into the card or panel it's embedded in.

props.name: tokenizer
props.type: (code: string, language: string) => Array<{type: string; start: number; end: number}>
props.description: Deprecated: pass language={createCodeLanguage({name, identifiers, tokenize})} with this same function instead. Still works exactly as released and wins over the language; astryx upgrade rewrites static uses.

props.description: Per-instance syntax theme override. Shorthand for wrapping the block in <SyntaxTheme theme={...}>. Accepts a preset from @astryxdesign/core/theme/syntax or a theme created with defineSyntaxTheme(). Defaults to the nearest SyntaxTheme ancestor or the theme-level syntax colors.

props.name: highlightMode
props.description: Syntax highlighting rendering mode.

props.name: isCollapsible
props.description: Allow collapsing the code body into just the header bar. Starts expanded; a visible header becomes clickable when the code exceeds collapsibleThreshold lines. Headerless blocks never collapse, and removing the header expands a previously collapsed block.

props.description: Minimum number of lines before the collapse toggle appears. Below this threshold the code block renders normally even when isCollapsible is true.

props.description: Ref forwarded to the root code-block element.

props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles. Prefer xstyle for StyleX-optimized styling.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

vars.description: Width of the line-number gutter, computed from the digit count of the last line so the code column starts at a stable offset.

componentIcons.fallback: `copy`; `check` while copied; `close` while a failed copy shows

state.description: True while the copied feedback shows after a successful copy. False while a failed copy shows, so a theme that maps the slot draws its rest glyph then; the button is still named and announced as the failure.

usage.description: CodeBlock renders syntax-highlighted code with line numbers, a copy button, and optional collapsible sections. Use CodeBlock for multi-line snippets like source files, terminal commands, and configuration examples. Use Code for inline references to function names, variables, or CLI flags within body text.

usage.description: Collapsible hides and reveals content behind a trigger button. Use it in settings panels, FAQ pages, or detail views to keep the page scannable while letting users drill into sections they care about. Wrap multiple collapsibles in CollapsibleGroup for accordion behavior. For custom collapsible components, use the `useCollapsible` hook directly (`astryx hook useCollapsible`).

bestPractices.description: Give every trigger a meaningful accessible name. Visible text usually supplies it; custom trigger content should include VisuallyHidden text when its visuals do not.
Use hasDividers on CollapsibleGroup for FAQ-style lists: built-in row hairlines with themed border tokens, no hand-rolled borders.
Wrap each Collapsible in an Card for visual separation in accordion layouts, or use CollapsibleGroup's hasDividers for flat lists; don't combine both.
Use CollapsibleGroup with type="single" for settings or FAQ pages where only one section should be open at a time.
Use type="multiple" when users need to compare content across sections, like feature lists or pricing tiers.
Start sections open (defaultIsOpen) when the content is likely needed on first view; don't make users click to see essential info.
Hide critical or required content behind a collapsible; users may not discover it.
Nest collapsibles more than two levels deep; it makes content hard to find and navigate.
Use a collapsible for a single short paragraph; just show the text directly instead.

usage.description: CommandPalette is a searchable dialog for quick access to commands, navigation, and actions. Use it as a keyboard-driven launcher powered by SearchSource for filtering and selection.

bestPractices.description: Provide a searchSource with bootstrap results so users see useful options before typing.
Use auxiliaryData.group on items to automatically organize results into labeled sections.
Provide a specific label when more than one command palette can appear in the same product surface.
Keep renderItem content non-interactive; each rendered row is one option, so buttons and links cannot be nested inside it.
Intercept query-field keyboard events without preserving active IME composition and native Home/End caret movement.
Use CommandPalette for simple dropdowns or menus; use Menu or Selector for inline selections.
Add too many groups or items; curate results to keep the palette fast and scannable.

docs.name: CommandPaletteItem
docs.description: One option in a command palette result list. CommandPalette context supplies selection, highlight, identity, and close behavior.

usage.description: Use CommandPaletteItem for one non-interactive result row inside CommandPaletteList or CommandPaletteGroup. CommandPalette owns the composite keyboard model; standalone items expose only their explicit visual state and pointer activation.

bestPractices.description: Keep each value unique within the result list so highlight, active-descendant identity, and selection resolve to the same item.

Inside CommandPalette, each item is an option in the listbox popup of the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern: keyboard focus stays in the query field, arrow keys move the highlight through aria-activedescendant, and Enter selects the highlighted item.

Nest buttons, links, or other interactive controls inside an item. Option semantics make descendants presentational, so use non-interactive content such as icons, descriptions, and shortcut hints, and activate the option itself.
Treat isHighlighted as selection. Highlight is the active keyboard result; isSelected represents the chosen value.

usage.description: Use ComplexSelector when a selection needs richer custom content than a Selector option row. It is intentionally one component: ComplexSelector owns the field, trigger, popover, focus restore, and changeAction flow, while the content render prop owns the selector-specific accessible structure.

bestPractices.description: Use variant="secondary" beside secondary buttons, or variant="ghost" beside ghost buttons; add a startIcon when it helps identify the trigger. Use alignment="end" when a wide surface should align its end edge to the trigger.
For staged editors, keep draft state in the composed content and call the provided onChange helper only from Apply. Cancel or dismiss without committing.

Compose the dialog content from the appropriate accessible structure for the job: RadioList for a simple choice, Calendar/date inputs for date picking, TreeList or a searchable list for hierarchy, or a custom grid when two-dimensional arrow navigation is useful.
Use the provided onChange helper from children; it already calls both onChange and changeAction and updates optimistic busy state.
Call close() from custom content when a selection should dismiss the popup. Keep it open for multi-step content or freeform entry flows.
Use Astryx focus hooks for custom content: useGridFocus for two-dimensional grids, useTreeFocus through TreeList for hierarchies, and useListFocus for custom linear collections.

Evaluate custom content against WCAG 2.2: keyboard operation, focus visible/not obscured, names and roles, labels/instructions, target size, and contrast/non-text contrast are especially relevant for selector popovers.
Do not rebuild trigger ARIA, popover focus management, or changeAction handling in product code.
Do not use ComplexSelector for a plain single-column text list; use Selector instead.

usage.description: A right-click context menu that appears at the cursor position. Use to provide contextual actions for specific elements or regions without cluttering the UI with visible buttons.

bestPractices.description: Keep menu items concise and action-oriented; users expect quick access to contextual actions.
Use sections and dividers to group related actions when the menu has many items.
Use `presentation="adaptive"` when right-click should remain cursor-positioned on desktop while long-press opens a reachable BottomSheet on compact touch devices.
Ensure all context menu actions are also accessible via other UI elements for keyboard-only users.
Keep a visible MoreMenu or equivalent trigger for important mobile actions; long-press must not be the only route.
Use a ContextMenu as the only way to access important actions; not all users know to right-click.
Place more than 10–12 items in a single menu without grouping them into sections.

props.description: First day of week in Astryx calendar surfaces. A number (0 = Sunday to 6 = Saturday) or a three-letter day name; native pickers remain browser/OS-owned.

props.name: format
props.description: How the committed date value is displayed. Named values are reused from Timestamp's format vocabulary: 'date' shows 'Mar 21, 2026', 'date_long' shows 'March 21, 2026', 'date_weekday' shows 'Wed, Mar 21, 2026', 'system_date' shows '2026-03-21'. 'date', 'date_long', and 'date_weekday' write the date in the field's calendar; 'system_date' stays the Gregorian ISO date. A function receives the ISO value and returns a custom string; the field cannot re-commit text it cannot read back. Applies only to the committed value, never to text being typed.

props.name: calendar
props.description: The calendar the text field reads and writes dates in, and the calendar its popover and bottom sheet show. value, onChange, min, and max stay Gregorian ISO dates. People type a date the way the locale writes it in this calendar, in any decimal digits; the field reports a date only once it is complete, and names a date the calendar does not have. Years are years of this calendar: a Buddhist field reads 2026 as Buddhist year 2026, so set min and max on Buddhist and Minguo calendar fields to catch a Gregorian year typed by mistake. Calendars other than gregory, iso8601, buddhist, roc, and japanese need Temporal, native or a polyfill the application loads; without it the field shows Gregorian dates. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, a presentation that would show the native date control shows the popover on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer, because the native control is Gregorian; the bottom sheet shows the months, leap months, and era years of the calendar. A year in which the era changes is labeled with the era of the shown month, such as 平成31 in January 2019 and 令和元 in July.

props.name: presentation
props.description: Which surface draws the date picker. 'adaptive-native' (the default) uses Astryx's calendar popover on a fine pointer and the browser/OS picker (input type=date) on a coarse pointer, keeping Astryx fallbacks where a native control cannot express the value; 'native' always uses the browser/OS picker with no fallback; 'adaptive-bottom-sheet' uses the popover on a fine pointer and Astryx's bottom-sheet picker on a coarse pointer; 'popover' and 'bottom-sheet' force that Astryx surface on every pointer. Every value opens a picker; a typed-only field is TimeInput's alone. Use a non-native presentation for a field that needs weekStartsOn, numberOfMonths or dateConstraints, none of which a native picker can express. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, 'native' and 'adaptive-native' use the popover on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer, and an explicit 'native' warns in development.

props.name: nativePicker
props.description: Deprecated: use presentation ('touch' = 'adaptive-native', 'always' = 'native', 'never' = 'adaptive-bottom-sheet'). Still works exactly as released; presentation wins when both are set. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, 'touch' and 'always' use the popover on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer.

props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

usage.description: DateInput lets the user type or pick a date from a calendar popover. Use it for scheduling, deadlines, booking dates, or any form field that needs a specific calendar date.

bestPractices.description: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the date input, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after DateInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.
Provide clear labels and descriptions so users understand what date is expected.
Use min, max, and dateConstraints to restrict selectable dates to valid ranges.
Set min and max on a Buddhist or Minguo calendar field, so a Gregorian year typed by mistake shows an error instead of a date centuries away.
Use hasClear when the date is optional so the user can reset it.
Show a loading state with changeAction when the date triggers a server-side save.

On a fine pointer the field follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with a dialog popup, as in the APG date picker combobox: ArrowDown or Alt+ArrowDown opens the calendar, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the field.
Use DateInput inside InputGroup when adding a short static prefix or suffix, such as a due-date hint.
Use a DateInput for free-form text that does not represent a calendar date.
Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the field purpose obvious.
Rely on the calendar alone; the text input lets users type dates directly, which is faster for known dates.
Wrap a disabled DateInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.
