props.description: 说明输入框为何被禁用。与 isDisabled 一起使用时，在悬停/键盘聚焦时显示提示（仍阻止输入和激活）。请使用此属性，而不是用 Tooltip 包裹已禁用的 DateInput。

props.name: value
props.description: 选中的日期，YYYY-MM-DD 格式。

props.name: onChange
props.description: 选中日期变更时调用的回调。

props.name: changeAction
props.description: 在 onChange 之后触发的异步操作。通过 useTransition 驱动乐观更新。

props.name: isLoading
props.description: 输入框是否处于加载状态。字段仍可聚焦，并通过 `aria-busy` 和加载指示器表示忙碌；加载结束前不能输入、选择或清除日期。

props.name: min
props.description: 可选择的最早日期（YYYY-MM-DD）。

props.name: max
props.description: 可选择的最晚日期（YYYY-MM-DD）。

props.name: dateConstraints
props.description: 自定义约束函数数组，用于禁用特定日期。

props.name: placeholder
props.description: 文本输入框中显示的占位符文本。调用方提供的占位符会替代日历格式提示。

props.name: size
props.description: 输入控件的尺寸。

props.name: status
props.description: 错误、警告或成功状态的状态指示对象，附带消息。

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: 状态消息相对于输入框的放置方式。attached 直接叠加在输入框下方（带边框处理）；detached 作为独立元素浮于下方并留有间距；tooltip 隐藏消息框，并在状态图标上以提示气泡形式显示。

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: 通过标签末尾的信息图标显示的提示文本。

props.name: hasClear
props.description: 有日期值时显示清除按钮。点击后清除日期。

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: 日历弹出层中同时显示的月份数量。

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: Astryx 日历表面中每周的起始日。可为数字（0=周日……6=周六）或三字母星期缩写；原生选择器仍由浏览器或操作系统控制。

props.name: format
props.description: 已选日期的显示格式。命名值复用 Timestamp 的格式词汇：'date' 显示 'Mar 21, 2026'，'date_long' 显示 'March 21, 2026'，'date_weekday' 显示 'Wed, Mar 21, 2026'，'system_date' 显示 '2026-03-21'。'date'、'date_long' 与 'date_weekday' 按字段的历法书写日期；'system_date' 始终为公历 ISO 日期。函数接收 ISO 值并返回自定义字符串；字段无法读回的文本在编辑后不能重新提交。仅作用于已提交的值，不影响正在输入的文本。

props.name: calendar
props.description: 文本字段读写日期所用的历法，也是其弹出日历和底部选择器显示的历法。value、onChange、min 和 max 始终为公历 ISO 日期。用户按当前语言区域在该历法中的写法输入日期，可使用任意十进制数字；只有输入完整时字段才会报告日期，并会指出该历法中不存在的日期。年份是该历法的年份：佛历字段把 2026 读作佛历 2026 年，因此请为佛历和民国纪年字段设置 min 和 max，以发现误输入的公历年份。gregory、iso8601、buddhist、roc 和 japanese 以外的历法需要 Temporal（原生或由应用加载的 polyfill）；没有 Temporal 时字段显示公历日期。使用 gregory 或 iso8601 以外的历法时，原本显示原生日期控件的呈现会在精细指针上显示弹出层、在粗指针上显示底部选择器，因为原生控件只显示公历；底部选择器显示该历法的月份、闰月和带纪元的年份。年号更替的年份按所显示月份的年号标注，如 2019 年 1 月为“平成31”，7 月为“令和元”。

props.name: presentation
props.description: 由哪个界面绘制日期选择器。'adaptive-native'（默认）在精细指针上使用 Astryx 日历弹出层、在粗指针上使用浏览器/操作系统选择器（input type=date），且原生控件无法表达值时保留 Astryx 回退；'native' 始终使用浏览器/操作系统选择器且不回退；'adaptive-bottom-sheet' 在精细指针上用弹出层、在粗指针上用 Astryx 底部选择器；'popover' 与 'bottom-sheet' 在任何指针上强制使用对应 Astryx 界面。每个值都会打开选择器；仅输入字段的呈现只属于 TimeInput。需要 weekStartsOn、numberOfMonths 或 dateConstraints 的字段应使用非原生呈现，原生选择器无法表达这些。使用 gregory 或 iso8601 以外的历法时，'native' 与 'adaptive-native' 在精细指针上使用弹出层、在粗指针上使用底部选择器，显式的 'native' 会在开发环境中发出警告。

props.name: nativePicker
props.description: 已弃用：请使用 presentation（'touch'='adaptive-native'、'always'='native'、'never'='adaptive-bottom-sheet'）。仍按已发布行为工作；同时设置时以 presentation 为准。使用 gregory 或 iso8601 以外的历法时，'touch' 与 'always' 在精细指针上使用弹出层、在粗指针上使用底部选择器。

props.name: width
props.description: 字段宽度（数字按像素处理，字符串按原样使用，例如 “100%”）。统一调整标签、控件和状态消息的宽度。

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: 作用于包含标签、控件和状态的 Field 容器的 StyleX 样式；containerClassName 与 containerStyle 以类名和内联样式作用于同一容器。没有 Field 容器时（InputGroup 内或 horizontal-labels FormLayout 中）不生效，并在开发环境发出警告。

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Field 容器的类名，作用目标同 containerXstyle。

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Field 容器的内联样式，作用目标同 containerXstyle。

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: 作用于可见控件框（带边框、包含文本、图标和末端控件的元素，而非原生 input）的 StyleX 样式；controlClassName 与 controlStyle 以类名和内联样式作用于同一元素。本组件不接受根级 xstyle、className 和 style。

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: 可见控件框的类名，作用目标同 controlXstyle。

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: 可见控件框的内联样式，作用目标同 controlXstyle。

props.description: Show an "(optional)" indicator.

props.description: Mark the field as required.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disable the trigger and picker. The trigger stays focusable and exposes `aria-disabled`; opening is blocked.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and describes the trigger (activation stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled DateRangeInput in Tooltip.

props.name: value
props.description: Selected date range or null. Import the `DateRange` type from `@astryxdesign/core/DateRangeInput`; it is `{start: ISODateString, end: ISODateString}`. Do NOT redeclare your own DateRange type; use the exported one so TypeScript structurally matches.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback when the range changes. Called with null on clear.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Drives optimistic UI updates via useTransition.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the input is in a loading state. Disables interaction and shows a spinner.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum selectable date. `ISODateString` is a template literal type (`\`${number}${number}${number}${number}-${number}${number}-${number}${number}\``). Pass a string literal like `"2026-01-28"`, not a runtime string variable. Import it from `@astryxdesign/core/Calendar` or use `as ISODateString` if computing the value dynamically.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum selectable date. Same template literal type as `min`: use a YYYY-MM-DD string literal or cast with `as ISODateString`.

props.name: dateConstraints
props.description: Custom constraint functions to disable specific dates.

props.name: maxRangeSpan
props.description: Maximum days a selected range may span, counting both endpoints (`7` = a 7-day window, start + 6). Once a start is picked, days beyond this distance are disabled so the range cannot stretch past the cap. Rolling window relative to the start; for fixed calendar bounds use `min`/`max`. Constrains selection only; it never rewrites a `value` already wider than the cap (flag that with `status`).

props.name: minRangeSpan
props.description: Minimum days a selected range must span, counting both endpoints (`2` forbids a single-day range). Once a start is picked, days closer than this are disabled. Clicking the start again commits a one-day range when allowed, or cancels the in-progress selection when the minimum is longer. Defaults to 1 (same-day start and end allowed).

props.name: presets
props.description: Preset ranges shown as quick-select options beside the calendar, or above it when the two do not fit side by side. A preset is disabled when either endpoint violates min, max, or dateConstraints, or when its span violates minRangeSpan or maxRangeSpan.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear button when a range is selected.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text when no range is selected.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the trigger.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator for error, warning, or success states.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text via info icon at label end.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: Number of months in the calendar.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: First day of week in the calendar. A number (0 = Sunday to 6 = Saturday) or a three-letter day name.

props.name: calendar
props.description: The calendar the trigger text and the popover calendar show, such as persian, hebrew, or buddhist. value, onChange, min, max, and presets stay Gregorian ISO dates. The field has no typed entry. Calendars other than gregory, iso8601, buddhist, roc, and japanese need Temporal, native or a polyfill the application loads; without it the field shows Gregorian dates and warns in development. Month starts in the Chinese and Dangi calendars come from the runtime's Temporal; when you render on the server, load the same Temporal implementation on the server and in the browser.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the Field box around the label, control, and status. containerClassName and containerStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. No effect (development warning) where no Field box renders: inside InputGroup (style the group) and in a horizontal-labels FormLayout.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the bordered element that holds the text, icons, and end controls, never the native input. controlClassName and controlStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. Replaces root xstyle, className, and style, which this component does not accept.

usage.description: DateRangeInput lets users select a start and end date from a dual-month calendar popover. Use it for filtering data by time period, report generation, analytics dashboards, and booking flows.

bestPractices.description: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the range trigger, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after DateRangeInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.
Use presets for common ranges like "Last 7 days" to speed up selection.
Use min/max to constrain selectable dates to valid ranges.
Keep hasClear enabled (default) so users can reset the filter.
Provide clear labels and descriptions so users understand what the range controls.
Use DateRangeInput when only a single date is needed; use DateInput instead.
Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the purpose obvious.
Wrap a disabled DateRangeInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

props.name: value
props.description: Selected datetime in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback invoked when the selected datetime changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Drives optimistic UI updates via useTransition.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the input is in a loading state. Disables interaction and shows a spinner.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum selectable datetime. Constrains both date and time selection.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum selectable datetime. Constrains both date and time selection.

props.name: dateConstraints
props.description: Array of custom constraint functions that disable specific dates.

props.name: hasSeconds
props.description: Include seconds in the time portion. Keeps Astryx's time field even when nativePicker selects native surfaces, because iOS has no seconds wheel.

props.name: hourFormat
props.description: Hour display format. '12h' shows the locale's day period; '24h' uses 24-hour notation. When unset, follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle (en-US 12-hour, en-GB 24-hour); a person's own preference rides on the locale tag (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23').

props.name: timeIncrement
props.description: Minute step for arrow keys in Astryx's typed time field. A non-default value keeps the Astryx time field in nativePicker modes because iOS treats native step as validation, not picker cadence. Ignored by the Astryx touch sheet, which uses wheels.

props.name: timeOptionInterval
props.description: Minute cadence for the preset-time combobox on Astryx's fine-pointer time field. Setting it keeps that Astryx time field even in nativePicker modes because the OS picker has no equivalent preset list. The Astryx touch sheet uses wheels.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear button when a datetime value is set.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown in the date portion when no date is selected. A caller placeholder replaces the calendar format hint.

props.name: calendar
props.description: The calendar the date segment reads and writes typed dates in, and the calendar its popover and bottom sheet show. value, onChange, min, and max stay Gregorian ISO datetimes. People type a date the way the locale writes it in this calendar, in any decimal digits; the field reports a date only once it is complete, and names a date the calendar does not have. Years are years of this calendar, so set min and max on Buddhist and Minguo calendar fields to catch a Gregorian year typed by mistake. Calendars other than gregory, iso8601, buddhist, roc, and japanese need Temporal, native or a polyfill the application loads; without it the field shows Gregorian dates. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, a presentation that would show native controls shows the popovers on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer, because the native date control is Gregorian; the Date panel of the bottom sheet shows the months, leap months, and era years of the calendar. A year in which the era changes is labeled with the era of the shown month, such as 平成31 in January 2019 and 令和元 in July.

props.name: timePlaceholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown in the time portion when no time is selected. On touch, this appears in the closed time segment before a time is chosen.

props.name: timeLabel
props.description: Accessible label for the time portion. Defaults to "{label} time" so it is tied to the field label and localizable.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the input control.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator object for error, warning, or success states with a message.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed via an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: Number of months displayed simultaneously in Astryx's pointer calendar popover. Ignored by native date controls and the mobile touch sheet, whose Date panel always shows one swipe-paged month at a time.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: First day of week in Astryx calendars. A number (0 = Sunday to 6 = Saturday) or a three-letter day name. Ignored by native date controls.

props.name: presentation
props.description: Which surfaces draw the date and time pickers. 'adaptive-native' (the default) uses Astryx's typed fields and popovers on a fine pointer and browser/OS controls on a coarse pointer — with per-segment Astryx fallbacks: hasSeconds, non-default timeIncrement, or timeOptionInterval retain Astryx's time field because iOS cannot express them faithfully; 'native' always uses both browser/OS controls with no fallback; 'adaptive-bottom-sheet' uses popovers on a fine pointer and Astryx's coordinated bottom sheet on a coarse pointer; 'popover' and 'bottom-sheet' force that Astryx surface on every pointer. Every value opens pickers; typed-only fields are TimeInput's alone. Use a non-native presentation when numberOfMonths, weekStartsOn, or visible dateConstraints behavior matters. Constraints are enforced on commit; min/max are forwarded as hints. hourFormat formats the closed time, while the OS picker follows the user's locale. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, 'native' and 'adaptive-native' use the popovers on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer, and an explicit 'native' warns in development.

props.name: nativePicker
props.description: Deprecated: use presentation ('touch' = 'adaptive-native', 'always' = 'native', 'never' = 'adaptive-bottom-sheet'). Still works exactly as released; presentation wins when both are set. With a calendar other than gregory or iso8601, 'touch' and 'always' use the popovers on a fine pointer and the bottom sheet on a coarse pointer.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the Field box around the label, control, and status. containerClassName and containerStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. No effect (development warning) where no Field box renders: inside InputGroup (style the group) and in a horizontal-labels FormLayout.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the row that holds the bordered date and time segments with their icons and end controls, never a native input. controlClassName and controlStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. Replaces root xstyle, className, and style, which this component does not accept.

usage.description: DateTimeInput combines date and time selection in one field. With presentation="adaptive-native" (the default), mouse/trackpad devices use Astryx typed fields and popovers, while coarse-pointer devices use browser/OS date and time controls in the same two-segment field. presentation="native" uses both native controls on every pointer; presentation="adaptive-bottom-sheet" keeps Astryx's own surfaces — pointer fields on fine pointers and the coordinated Date/Time bottom sheet on coarse pointers; "popover" and "bottom-sheet" force one Astryx surface on every pointer. The closed segments stay side by side when at least 400px is available and wrap into full-width rows below 400px, independent of viewport width. Use it for scheduling, event creation, deadline setting, or any form field that needs a specific datetime.

bestPractices.description: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the date input, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after DateTimeInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.
Provide clear labels and descriptions so users understand what datetime is expected.
Use min and max to restrict selectable datetimes to valid ranges.
Set min and max on a Buddhist or Minguo calendar field, so a Gregorian year typed by mistake shows an error instead of a date centuries away.
Use hasClear when the datetime is optional so the user can reset it.

Leave hourFormat unset so the field follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle (12-hour in en-US, 24-hour in en-GB or de-DE). Set it only when the field itself needs a fixed format, and carry a person's own 12/24-hour preference on the provider locale (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23') rather than on each field.
Use DateTimeInput when only a date is needed; use DateInput instead.
Use DateTimeInput when only a time is needed; use TimeInput instead.
Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the field purpose obvious.
Wrap a disabled DateTimeInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

usage.description: DateTimeInput combines date and time selection. presentation="adaptive-native" (default) uses browser/OS date+time controls on coarse pointers and Astryx pointer fields on fine pointers; "native" uses both native controls everywhere; "adaptive-bottom-sheet" uses Astryx's coordinated bottom sheet on coarse pointers and pointer fields on fine pointers; "popover"/"bottom-sheet" force one Astryx surface everywhere. Closed segments stay side by side when at least 400px is available and wrap below 400px.

bestPractices.description: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the date input, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after DateTimeInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.
Provide clear labels + descriptions so users understand what datetime is expected.
Use min and max to restrict selectable datetimes to valid ranges.
Set min and max on a Buddhist or Minguo calendar field, so a Gregorian year typed by mistake shows an error instead of a date centuries away.
Use hasClear when the datetime is optional so the user can reset it.

Leave hourFormat unset so the field follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle (12-hour in en-US, 24-hour in en-GB or de-DE). Set it only when the field itself needs a fixed format, and carry a person's own 12/24-hour preference on the provider locale (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23') rather than on each field.
Use DateTimeInput when only a date is needed; use DateInput instead.
Use DateTimeInput when only a time is needed; use TimeInput instead.
Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the field purpose obvious.
Wrap a disabled DateTimeInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

propDescriptions.label: label text
propDescriptions.isLabelHidden: visually hide label
propDescriptions.disabledMessage: reason shown in a tooltip on hover/focus when disabled; describes the fields
propDescriptions.changeAction: async action after onChange; drives optimistic UI
propDescriptions.isLoading: loading state; disables interaction, shows spinner
propDescriptions.dateConstraints: custom constraint fns to disable specific dates
propDescriptions.hasSeconds: include seconds; retains Astryx time field because iOS native picker has no seconds wheel
propDescriptions.hourFormat: display format. '12h' shows the locale's day period; '24h' uses 24-hour. Unset follows the provider locale's hour cycle (a -u-hc- tag carries a user preference)
propDescriptions.timeIncrement: minute step for Astryx typed field; non-default retains Astryx time field in native modes because iOS native step is validation-only
propDescriptions.timeOptionInterval: preset-time combobox cadence; setting it retains Astryx time field because native pickers have no equivalent list
propDescriptions.hasClear: Shows clear button when datetime is set
propDescriptions.calendar: calendar for typed + committed date text, the popover, and the sheet's Date panel (months, leap months, era years; an era-change year follows the shown month, e.g. 平成31 in Jan 2019, 令和元 in Jul) (default: provider's, else 'gregory'); values stay Gregorian ISO; years are the calendar's, so set min/max on buddhist/roc fields; non-Gregorian-aligned calendars need Temporal (native or app-loaded polyfill), else Gregorian; non-gregory/iso8601 never shows native controls: popovers fine / sheet coarse
propDescriptions.timePlaceholder: time-portion placeholder when empty; shown on touch closed time segment
propDescriptions.timeLabel: accessible label for the time input; defaults to "{label} time"
propDescriptions.status: error/warning/success status w/ message
propDescriptions.labelTooltip: tooltip text via info icon at label end
propDescriptions.numberOfMonths: Astryx pointer-calendar months shown simultaneously; ignored by native date controls and the mobile touch sheet
propDescriptions.weekStartsOn: first day of week in Astryx calendars (0=Sunday, or name e.g. "mon"); ignored by native date controls
propDescriptions.presentation: date+time surfaces: 'adaptive-native' (default) = Astryx popovers fine / browser/OS coarse w/ per-segment fallbacks (seconds/timeIncrement/timeOptionInterval); 'native' = browser/OS always, no fallback; 'adaptive-bottom-sheet' = popovers fine / coordinated sheet coarse; 'popover'/'bottom-sheet' force Astryx. every value opens pickers (no typed-only value; that is TimeInput's). non-gregory/iso8601 calendar: native + adaptive-native become popovers fine / sheet coarse; explicit 'native' warns in dev.
propDescriptions.nativePicker: deprecated, use presentation: 'touch'='adaptive-native', 'always'='native', 'never'='adaptive-bottom-sheet'. still works as released, except that a calendar other than gregory or iso8601 never shows the native control; presentation wins if both set.
propDescriptions.containerXstyle: Field box (label+control+status); also containerClassName/containerStyle. no effect in InputGroup or horizontal-labels FormLayout
propDescriptions.controlXstyle: visual control box = the row holding the date and time segments, never a native input; also controlClassName/controlStyle. no root xstyle/className/style

usage.description: DateTimeInput combines date and time selection in one field. With presentation="adaptive-native" (the default), mouse/trackpad devices use Astryx typed fields and popovers, while coarse-pointer devices use browser/OS date and time controls in the same two-segment field. presentation="native" uses both native controls on every pointer; presentation="adaptive-bottom-sheet" keeps Astryx's own surfaces — pointer fields on fine pointers and the coordinated Date/Time bottom sheet on coarse pointers; "popover" and "bottom-sheet" force one Astryx surface on every pointer. The closed segments stay side by side when at least 400px is available and wrap into full-width rows below 400px, independent of viewport width. Use it for scheduling, event creation, deadline setting, or any form field that needs a specific datetime.

bestPractices.description: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the date input, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after DateTimeInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.
Provide clear labels and descriptions so users understand what datetime is expected.
Use min and max to restrict selectable datetimes to valid ranges.
Set min and max on a Buddhist or Minguo calendar field, so a Gregorian year typed by mistake shows an error instead of a date centuries away.
Use hasClear when the datetime is optional so the user can reset it.

Leave hourFormat unset so the field follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle (12-hour in en-US, 24-hour in en-GB or de-DE). Set it only when the field itself needs a fixed format, and carry a person's own 12/24-hour preference on the provider locale (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23') rather than on each field.
Use DateTimeInput when only a date is needed; use DateInput instead.
Use DateTimeInput when only a time is needed; use TimeInput instead.
Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the field purpose obvious.
Wrap a disabled DateTimeInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

props.name: label
props.description: 标签文本。

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: 视觉隐藏标签。

props.name: description
props.description: 显示在标签下方的辅助文本。

props.name: isOptional
props.description: 在标签旁显示"(optional)"指示器。

props.name: isRequired
props.description: 将字段标记为必填。

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: 禁用输入框和选择器。字段仍可聚焦并暴露 `aria-disabled`，但不能输入或打开选择器。

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: 说明输入框为何被禁用。与 isDisabled 一起使用时，在悬停/键盘聚焦时显示提示，并描述日期和时间字段（仍阻止输入和激活）。请使用此属性，而不是用 Tooltip 包裹已禁用的 DateTimeInput。

props.name: value
props.description: 选中的日期时间，ISO 8601 格式。

props.name: onChange
props.description: 选中日期时间变更时调用的回调。

props.name: changeAction
props.description: 在 onChange 之后触发的异步操作。通过 useTransition 驱动乐观更新。

props.name: isLoading
props.description: 输入框是否处于加载状态。禁用交互并显示加载指示器。

props.name: min
props.description: 可选择的最早日期时间。同时约束日期和时间选择。

props.name: max
props.description: 可选择的最晚日期时间。同时约束日期和时间选择。

props.name: dateConstraints
props.description: 自定义约束函数数组，用于禁用特定日期。

props.name: hasSeconds
props.description: 在时间部分包含秒。即使 nativePicker 选择原生界面，也会保留 Astryx 时间字段，因为 iOS 没有秒滚轮。

props.name: hourFormat
props.description: 控制显示格式。'12h' 使用区域设置的上午/下午用语；'24h' 使用 24 小时制。未设置时遵循 InternationalizationProvider 区域设置的小时制（en-US 为 12 小时制，en-GB 为 24 小时制）；用户自己的偏好可通过区域标签传入（例如 'en-US-u-hc-h23'）。

props.name: timeIncrement
props.description: Astryx 可输入时间字段中箭头键的分钟步长。非默认值会在 nativePicker 模式下保留 Astryx 时间字段，因为 iOS 将原生 step 视为验证规则，而不是选择器步长。Astryx 触摸面板使用滚轮。

props.name: hasClear
props.description: 当有值时显示清除按钮。

props.name: placeholder
props.description: 日期部分未选择日期时显示的占位符文本。调用方提供的占位符会替代日历格式提示。

props.name: calendar
props.description: 日期部分读写输入日期所用的历法，也是其弹出日历和底部面板显示的历法。value、onChange、min 和 max 始终为公历 ISO 日期时间。用户按当前语言区域在该历法中的写法输入日期，可使用任意十进制数字；只有输入完整时字段才会报告日期，并会指出该历法中不存在的日期。年份是该历法的年份，因此请为佛历和民国纪年字段设置 min 和 max，以发现误输入的公历年份。gregory、iso8601、buddhist、roc 和 japanese 以外的历法需要 Temporal（原生或由应用加载的 polyfill）；没有 Temporal 时字段显示公历日期。使用 gregory 或 iso8601 以外的历法时，原本显示原生控件的呈现会在精细指针上显示弹出层、在粗指针上显示底部面板，因为原生日期控件只显示公历；底部面板的日期页显示该历法的月份、闰月和带纪元的年份。年号更替的年份按所显示月份的年号标注，如 2019 年 1 月为“平成31”，7 月为“令和元”。

props.name: timePlaceholder
props.description: 时间部分未选择时间时显示的占位符文本。在触摸设备上，这会显示在未选择时间的闭合时间段中。

props.name: timeLabel
props.description: 时间部分的无障碍标签。默认为“{label} time”，与字段标签关联且可本地化。

props.name: size
props.description: 输入控件的尺寸。

props.name: status
props.description: 错误、警告或成功状态的状态指示对象，附带消息。

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: 通过标签末尾的信息图标显示的提示文本。

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: Astryx 指针日历弹出层中同时显示的月份数量。原生日期控件和移动触摸面板会忽略此属性；触摸面板的日期部分一次显示一个可滑动月份。

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: Astryx 日历中每周的起始日。可为数字（0=周日……6=周六）或三字母星期缩写。原生日期控件会忽略此属性。

props.name: presentation
props.description: 选择由哪些界面绘制日期和时间选择器。'adaptive-native'（默认）在精细指针上使用 Astryx 文本字段与弹出层、在粗指针上使用浏览器/操作系统控件，并按段回退：hasSeconds、非默认 timeIncrement 或 timeOptionInterval 会保留 Astryx 时间字段；'native' 始终使用两个原生控件且不回退；'adaptive-bottom-sheet' 在精细指针上用弹出层、在粗指针上用 Astryx 协调底部面板；'popover' 与 'bottom-sheet' 在任何指针上强制使用对应 Astryx 界面。每个值都会打开选择器；仅文本字段的呈现只属于 TimeInput。需要 numberOfMonths、weekStartsOn 或可见 dateConstraints 行为时请使用非原生呈现。约束会在提交时执行，min/max 作为提示传给原生控件。hourFormat 格式化关闭状态的时间，而操作系统选择器遵循用户区域设置。使用 gregory 或 iso8601 以外的历法时，'native' 与 'adaptive-native' 在精细指针上使用弹出层、在粗指针上使用底部面板，显式的 'native' 会在开发环境中发出警告。

props.name: nativePicker
props.description: 已弃用：请使用 presentation（'touch'='adaptive-native'、'always'='native'、'never'='adaptive-bottom-sheet'）。仍按已发布行为工作；同时设置时以 presentation 为准。使用 gregory 或 iso8601 以外的历法时，'touch' 与 'always' 在精细指针上使用弹出层、在粗指针上使用底部面板。

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: 作用于包含标签、控件和状态的 Field 容器的 StyleX 样式；containerClassName 与 containerStyle 以类名和内联样式作用于同一容器。没有 Field 容器时（InputGroup 内或 horizontal-labels FormLayout 中）不生效，并在开发环境发出警告。

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: 作用于可见控件框（容纳带边框的日期与时间分段及其图标和末端控件的行，而非原生 input）的 StyleX 样式；controlClassName 与 controlStyle 以类名和内联样式作用于同一元素。本组件不接受根级 xstyle、className 和 style。

docs.description: Modal dialog using the native <dialog> element. Modal and inline content starts with theme body text defaults. Ancestor surface/group membership ends as a whole, including group-owned state. Explicit props and unrelated contexts remain unchanged. Place intentional groups and complete required providers inside the dialog. With reduced motion the dialog never slides or scales in: on a touch screen it fades in, in 200 ms or less, and with a mouse it appears at once. On a phone or tablet (a coarse primary pointer), a tap or a drag that lands while the dialog is still entering reaches nothing, and the dialog finishes entering; keys and assistive technology stay live, and a mouse or a trackpad still clicks: at once when it was the last pointer used, otherwise once it moves.

usage.description:
Dialog displays a modal overlay that blocks interaction with the page until the user responds. Use it for delete confirmations, edit forms, terms acceptance, or any decision that should not be skipped.

For cases where you want to show a dialog without managing open state, use the `useImperativeDialog` hook: call `dialog.show(content)` and render `dialog.element` in your tree.

bestPractices.description: Choose the right purpose: info for dismissable content, form to prevent accidental backdrop dismissal, required when the user must respond.
Include a clear title in the header so users immediately understand what the dialog is asking.
Use purpose="form" for dialogs with inputs so the user can't accidentally lose data by clicking the backdrop.
Keep dialogs focused on a single task; if the content grows beyond what fits, consider a full page instead.
Use a dialog for simple messages that could be shown inline or as a toast notification.
Nest dialogs inside other dialogs; restructure the flow into steps within a single dialog instead.
Use the fullscreen variant for simple confirmations; it is meant for complex content like editors or long forms.

params.name: element
params.description: The element a drag moves. It moves along `axis` only, by translation, so lay it out at its resting position as usual.

params.name: options.axis
params.description: The axis the element moves along.

params.name: options.snapPoints
params.description: Offsets in px along `axis` from the element's resting position, such as `[0, 240, 480]`, sorted before use (`onSettle` and `settleTo` count in that order); an empty list makes the drag do nothing. Unlike BottomSheet's `snapPoints`, they are not fractions of the viewport.

params.name: options.flickThreshold
params.description: A release faster than this, in px/s, carries to the next snap point in its direction. The default is the flick speed measured for UIKit's sheet.

params.name: options.onSettle
params.description: Called with the snap point's index once the element settles on it, after a drag or `settleTo`. A settle that a new drag interrupts calls nothing.

returns.name: settleTo
returns.description: Settles the element on the snap point at `index` without a drag, then calls `onSettle`. Wire it to keys and buttons: it is the keyboard path. An index outside the snap points does nothing and warns in development.

returns.name: destroy
returns.description: Removes every listener and stops the element where it is. Call it when you remove the element.

usage.description: Lets a drag move an element along one axis and settles it on snap points when the finger lifts, the way an iOS sheet settles on its detents: on the nearest snap point to where it is, on the next one in its direction after a quick flick, and back where it started when the finger was moving back. The settle continues the release's velocity. For a bottom sheet, use BottomSheet's `snapPoints`; for a scrolling row, Carousel's `hasSnap`. Use the `useDragToSnapPoints` hook in React.

bestPractices.description: Offer the same positions without a drag: buttons or keys that call `settleTo`.
Keep the snap points few and far apart, so a release clearly picks one.
Use it for a sheet or a carousel: their own props already settle the way people expect.

accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology
accessibility.description: A drag is one way in, never the only one. Give each snap point a control a keyboard and a screen reader can reach, such as Expand and Collapse buttons, and call `settleTo` from it. When a position changes what the element shows, announce the change.

accessibility.name: Reduce Motion
accessibility.description: When the person asks for reduced motion, the settle after a touch drag becomes a short cross-fade into the snap point, as does any settle on a device whose primary pointer is coarse, such as a tablet; after a mouse or pen drag elsewhere it lands at once. `settleTo` fades on such a device and lands at once with a fine primary pointer. While the finger is down, the element still follows it.

docs.name: Drawer

children.children: Adjust the properties below, then open the preview.

docs.description: Side panel that floats above page content, using the native <dialog> element. Slides in from the inline start or end edge; full height, never reflows the layout underneath. Like Dialog, it is a container: set padding (or a theme's drawer padding) and a lone Section child or bleed children such as Table and Divider align against that inset. The default inset is --spacing-4 (16px), as in Dialog.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the drawer is open. Fully controlled; pair with onOpenChange.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the drawer requests an open-state change. Escape and a scrim click call it with false as purpose allows; a DrawerHeader given the same callback calls it from its close button. The caller owns the open state. With sibling drawers open, Escape only closes the last-opened one.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the drawer. Required; the drawer has no built-in heading to derive a name from.

props.name: children
props.description: Drawer content, rendered inside a full-height scrollable area. Compose your own header/body/footer; an element with data-autofocus is focused on open. Children stay mounted during the exit animation; keep the last-selected item rendered instead of nulling content on close.

props.name: side
props.description: Edge the drawer slides from: 'end' is right in LTR (the inspector convention), 'start' is left. Inline axis only; for a bottom sheet use BottomSheet.

props.name: width
props.description: Desktop width budget. A number is pixels; a string is any CSS length ('50%', '32rem'). Below the 640px mobile breakpoint this remains the maximum while the drawer preserves a 56px reveal of the page behind.

props.name: experimental
props.description: Experimental options: anything in this object may change or be removed in a patch release, and omitting it keeps the stable behavior. isFullWidthOnMobile (default false) covers the full viewport width below the 640px mobile breakpoint instead of preserving the default 56px reveal of the page behind, which makes the drawer read as an overlay, not a navigation.

props.name: hasScrim
props.description: Modal scrim behind the drawer. true uses showModal() (top layer, focus trap, scroll lock; clicking the scrim closes unless purpose prevents it; modal only); false uses the manual Popover API for a non-modal top-layer overlay that does NOT trap focus and keeps the page behind interactive.

props.name: purpose
props.description: Configures implicit dismissal, matching Dialog. info: Escape and a scrim click close. form: Escape closes, a scrim click does not. required: neither closes (Escape is consumed) and a modal drawer is exposed as an alertdialog, so give its content a way out. A non-modal drawer has no scrim, so form and info behave the same.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding of the drawer content using the spacing scale, matching Dialog. When omitted, uses the theme default for drawers: --spacing-4 (16px) unless the theme sets padding on drawer. Pass 0 for a full-bleed content area. A lone Section child escapes the padding, bleed children such as Table and Divider compensate against it, and a Layout picks it up for its regions. The content area's block-end edge adds the home-indicator safe area on top in every mode.

usage.description:
A side panel that floats above page content for inspectors and detail views: the "click a table row, see its details" pattern. Unlike a docked panel it overlays the layout instead of reflowing it. Works on desktop and touch: the width budget applies on desktop and the panel preserves a 56px page reveal below 640px without exceeding the width budget. Escape closes the drawer (unless purpose is required) and focus returns to the element that opened it. Entry/exit slide animation respects prefers-reduced-motion. On a phone or tablet (a coarse primary pointer), a tap or a drag that lands while the drawer is still sliding in reaches nothing (for a drawer without a scrim, only one on the panel: the page stays live), and the drawer finishes sliding in; keys and assistive technology stay live, and a mouse or a trackpad still clicks: at once when it was the last pointer used, otherwise once it moves. Stacking contract: sibling drawers stack last-opened on top, Escape closes only the topmost, and closing peels innermost-first; render them as siblings, never nested.

Like Dialog, the drawer is a container: its content area is inset by --spacing-4 (16px) by default, by the padding prop, or by a theme's padding on drawer. Compose the header, body, and footer the way Dialog does, with a Layout: DrawerHeader in the header slot (it shows a close button when you pass it onOpenChange, like DialogHeader), the body in LayoutContent, and actions in LayoutFooter. The Layout redistributes the inset to those regions so they line up on one content line, and the header is not inset twice. A lone Section child also escapes the inset. Drawer renders no close button of its own, so give every drawer a visible way to close, especially a non-modal one, which has no scrim to click. Put data-autofocus on the control that should receive focus on open.

Choosing a surface: use Dialog for a centered decision or short form, Drawer for full-height side detail that keeps the page in sight, BottomSheet for block-axis sheets on touch, and a docked panel (a layout column) when content should reflow the page instead of floating over it.

Theming: the panel is the single stable target (astryx-drawer, with data-side reflecting side), and the scrim is the panel's native ::backdrop. DrawerHeader exposes astryx-drawer-header targets for its row, slots, and close icon.

bestPractices.description: Use for contextual detail views (row inspectors, entity details) where the user should keep the underlying list in sight.
Keep the caller as the source of truth: derive isOpen from selection state and clear the selection in onOpenChange.
Use hasScrim={false} for master-detail flows; non-modal drawers do not trap focus and the page behind stays interactive.
Keep the last-selected item rendered on close: children stay mounted during the exit animation, so nulling content mid-close blanks the panel while it slides out.
Give every drawer a visible close action, usually DrawerHeader with onOpenChange; a non-modal drawer has no scrim to click.
Use purpose="form" when a stray scrim click would discard unsaved input.
Use a Drawer for short confirmations or small forms; use Dialog or AlertDialog instead.
Reach for a Drawer when the content should push the page aside; a Drawer floats over content, so use a docked panel or layout column instead.
Use a Drawer as a bottom or top sheet; it is inline-axis only, so use BottomSheet for block-axis sheets.
Nest a Drawer inside another Drawer; render drawers as siblings; the last-opened stacks on top and Escape closes it first.

anatomy.description: 模态抽屉（hasScrim，默认开启）背后调暗并阻止页面交互的背景层；非模态抽屉没有。

usage.description:
浮在页面内容之上的侧边面板，用于检查器和详情视图——"点击表格行查看详情"的模式。与停靠面板不同，它覆盖在布局之上，不会挤压页面。桌面端按 width 设定宽度，宽度小于 640px 时保留 56px 的底层页面，并且不超过 width 上限。按 Escape 关闭抽屉（purpose 为 required 时除外），焦点返回到打开它的元素。滑入/滑出动画遵循 prefers-reduced-motion。堆叠约定：同级抽屉后开的在上层，Escape 只关闭最上层的，关闭顺序由内向外——请以同级方式渲染，切勿嵌套。

与 Dialog 一样，Drawer 是一个容器：内容区域默认带有 --spacing-4（16px）的内边距，也可以由 padding 属性或主题中 drawer 的 padding 设置。像 Dialog 一样用 Layout 组合页眉、正文和页脚：DrawerHeader 放在 header 插槽（传入 onOpenChange 时显示关闭按钮，与 DialogHeader 相同），正文放在 LayoutContent，操作放在 LayoutFooter。Layout 会把内边距分配给这些区域，使它们对齐在同一条内容线上，页眉也不会被重复缩进。作为唯一子元素的 Section 同样会越出该内边距。Drawer 本身不渲染关闭按钮，所以每个抽屉都要提供可见的关闭方式，非模态抽屉尤其如此，因为它没有可点击的遮罩。在打开时应获得焦点的控件上加 data-autofocus。

如何选择：居中的决定或短表单用 Dialog；保持页面可见的全高侧边详情用 Drawer；触屏上的块轴面板用 BottomSheet；内容应当把页面挤开重排时用停靠面板（布局分栏），而不是浮层。

主题化：面板是唯一的稳定目标（astryx-drawer，data-side 反映 side 值），遮罩是面板的原生 ::backdrop。DrawerHeader 为其标题行、插槽和关闭图标提供 astryx-drawer-header 系列目标。

bestPractices.description: 用于上下文详情视图（行检查器、实体详情），让用户保持对底层列表的可见性。
让调用方作为唯一数据源：从选中状态派生 isOpen，并在 onOpenChange 中清除选中。
在主从流程中使用 hasScrim={false}——非模态抽屉不捕获焦点，抽屉后面的页面保持可交互。
关闭时保留最后选中的内容：退出动画期间子内容仍然挂载，中途置空会让面板在滑出时变为空白。
为每个抽屉提供可见的关闭操作，通常是带 onOpenChange 的 DrawerHeader；非模态抽屉没有可点击的遮罩。
误点遮罩会丢失未保存的输入时，使用 purpose="form"。
用 Drawer 做简短确认或小表单——请改用 Dialog 或 AlertDialog。
需要把页面内容挤开时不要用 Drawer——它浮在内容之上，请改用停靠面板或布局分栏。
不要把 Drawer 当作底部/顶部面板使用——它只支持行内轴，块轴面板请用 BottomSheet。
在 Drawer 中嵌套另一个 Drawer；应以同级方式渲染——后开的堆叠在上层，Escape 先关闭它。

docs.description: Action menu with a trigger button and anchored, bottom-sheet, or adaptive presentation.

props.name: button
props.description: Props for the trigger button (Button props except onClick). Mutually exclusive with `renderTrigger`.

props.name: renderTrigger
props.description: Render the control the menu hangs off — an IconButton, a chip, an avatar, a list row — instead of the built-in Button. Spread the given props onto it: they carry the press model (a mouse opens on press-down, a held finger opens with the finger down), the keyboard opens, the toggle click, and `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`/`id`; the menu is then named by that control through `aria-labelledby`. Mutually exclusive with `button`.

props.name: items
props.description: Array of menu entries. Each entry is one of: an action item `{label, onClick?, href?, target?, rel?, icon?, description?, endContent?, isDisabled?, variant?, hasCloseOnSelect?, id?}` (`href` makes the row a real link, so a modified click keeps the browser's meaning; variant `"destructive"` renders it in the error color; `endContent` holds trailing content such as a keyboard-shortcut hint; `id` is the row's stable React key, needed only when the array reorders or filters), a divider `{type: "divider"}`, or a section `{type: "section", title?, id?, items: [...action items]}`.

props.name: presentation
props.description: Presentation surface for data-driven items. 'popover' stays anchored, 'bottom-sheet' always renders the actions in a modal BottomSheet, and 'adaptive' uses a BottomSheet on compact coarse-pointer layouts while remaining anchored elsewhere. Compound children currently support popover only. Omitted, the menu is anchored, and under a finger, on every device, the finger that opened it picks a row only after moving 10 px. Pass 'popover' to keep the pointer behavior on every device, the settle rule included.

props.name: isMenuOpen
props.description: Controlled open state for the menu. Mounting with true renders the menu open without moving focus into it; focus moves to the first item only when the menu opens after mount.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when the open state changes.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Minimum width for the popover presentation. Length values may grow for content; intrinsic and CSS-wide keywords select the preferred inline size. Every form is capped to the available viewport space. Defaults to matching the trigger width up to that cap.

props.name: menuMaxHeight
props.description: Maximum height in pixels for the popover presentation, for a menu that must fit its rows. Lifts the default 300px cap; the viewport still bounds it.

props.name: header
props.description: Content above the rows and outside the menu itself — a filter field, a toggle. A menu holds only its rows, so a control that is not a row goes here or in `footer`, never among the rows. It keeps its own keys and presses. With a header or footer the popover is a modal dialog around the menu: Tab and Shift+Tab move through the header, the menu and the footer and wrap at either end, and Escape closes. The bottom sheet shows it above the actions.

props.name: footer
props.description: Content below the rows and outside the menu itself — a "Create" button. Tab from the menu moves into it, and Tab past its last control wraps to the start of the dialog (see `header`). The bottom sheet shows it below the actions.

props.name: placement
props.description: Popover placement relative to the trigger. Ignored by the bottom-sheet presentation. Logical: start/end resolve against the menu's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors).

props.name: alignment
props.description: Popover alignment along the placement axis. Ignored by the bottom-sheet presentation. Logical: start/end follow the menu's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors).

props.name: onClick
props.description: Callback fired for accepted trigger activation. The trailing click from the same press that light-dismissed the menu is ignored.

props.name: hasChevron
props.description: Whether to show a chevron icon on the trigger button. Set to false for icon-only triggers.

props.name: children
props.description: Compound-mode menu content: DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuDivider, DropdownMenuSubMenu (a flyout on a laptop, a drilled-in view with a Back row on a phone), and the selectable items. Mutually exclusive with `items`.

usage.description: A dropdown menu that displays a list of actionable items in a popup triggered by a button. Use to present action options as a next step in a process, or to offer contextual actions without cluttering the interface. Like the menus of macOS and iOS, the row under the pointer when it is released is the row that acts, the highlight follows a held mouse or finger, a mouse opens it on press and can drag straight into it, and a finger held on the trigger opens it with the finger down.

bestPractices.description: Keep menu items concise and action-oriented so users can scan options quickly.
Use sections and dividers to group related actions when the menu has many items.
For a short, flat action set, use presentation="bottom-sheet" when product policy calls for a modal touch surface.
Use presentation="adaptive" when the same short action set should remain anchored on pointer layouts and become a BottomSheet on compact coarse-pointer layouts.
For a hierarchy that cannot fit as adjacent flyouts on a compact touch surface, a product may explicitly use a drill-in interaction with a Back action.
Choose presentation explicitly in product code. A compact, coarse-pointer, hover-free media query is one useful policy, but DropdownMenu does not impose a universal device breakpoint.
When the content is no longer a short list of immediate actions, reevaluate the interaction and choose a component that matches the actual task; content traits alone do not determine the component.
Use a DropdownMenu for navigation; use a navigation component instead.
Place more than 10–12 items in a single menu without grouping them into sections.

docs.name: DropdownMenuGroup
docs.description: A group of rows in a compound menu. A visible title names role="group" through aria-labelledby; an omitted title leaves the group unnamed. The heading is not a menuitem, so arrow keys and typeahead skip it. Keep title content non-interactive and place controls in DropdownMenu header or footer. The data-driven equivalent is the `{type: "section", title, items}` entry in `items`; both forms share the heading treatment and theme target. Host attributes and DOM handlers (id, data-*, aria-*) reach the group element; its role, and its name while it has a title, stay component-owned.

usage.description: Use DropdownMenuGroup to give related compound-menu rows one visible and programmatic name. Use an untitled group only when a separate name would not help people understand the rows.

bestPractices.description: Use short, descriptive title content that explains what the grouped rows have in common.
Keep the title non-interactive so every available action remains in the menu arrow-key order.
Place buttons, links, fields, or other controls in title. Put them in DropdownMenu header or footer instead.
Wrap rows that do not form a meaningful set; a group adds structure only when its relationship helps users.

docs.name: DropdownMenuSubMenu
docs.description: A single menu row that reveals a nested flyout of its own items. The row adopts DropdownMenuItem semantics (label / icon / description / isDisabled); its children become the flyout content. Opens inline-end with viewport auto-flip; Right/Enter/Space opens and focuses the first item, Left/Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger (Right/Left swap in RTL). On a phone (a coarse pointer, decided when the menu opened) the row drills in instead: its rows replace the menu's rows in the same box, led by a Back row named "Back to <parent>", and Back, Escape or ArrowLeft return to the row. Host attributes and DOM event handlers (aria-*, data-*, id) reach the trigger row, the element carrying role="menuitem" and aria-haspopup="menu"; a caller's handlers run after the row's own, except for the keys that open the flyout (the open arrow, Enter, Space) and a click on a disabled row. For data-driven menus, give a menu item a nested `items` array instead of using this component directly.

props.description: Primary label text for the trigger row.

props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: children
props.description: The flyout menu items: the same components used at the top level (DropdownMenuItem, nested DropdownMenuSubMenu, selectable items).

props.description: A disabled submenu renders its trigger row but never opens the flyout.

props.name: hasSpinner
props.description: Show a spinner in place of the caret, e.g. while a lazy submenu's children are loading.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Minimum flyout width. The flyout may grow for its content, but it is capped to the available viewport space. Defaults to intrinsic sizing (min 160px).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the flyout opens or closes.

props.name: presentation
props.description: How the sub-menu shows its rows. 'flyout' opens them beside the row; 'drill-in' replaces the menu's rows with them and a Back row, in the same box; 'adaptive' drills in when a finger opened the menu (a coarse pointer, decided when the menu opened) and flies out otherwise.

props.name: delay
props.description: How long a hovering pointer waits before the flyout opens, in milliseconds. Keyboard focus and touch never wait.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: How long the flyout stays open after the pointer leaves, in milliseconds.

props.name: header
props.description: Content above the sub-menu's rows and outside its menu, a field that filters them, say. It keeps its own keys and presses. With a header or footer the sub-menu's surface (the flyout, or the drilled-in view on a phone) is a modal dialog named by the row, beside the menu rather than inside it: the row says aria-haspopup="dialog", Tab and Shift+Tab move through the header, the rows and the footer and wrap, Escape returns to the row, and a pointer leaving the flyout closes it only once focus leaves too. A ContextMenu does not show it.

props.name: footer
props.description: Content below the sub-menu's rows and outside its menu, a door to where the options are managed, say. Same rules as header.

props.name: menuDataTestId
props.description: Test id for the sub-menu's own role="menu" element: the flyout, or the drilled-in list on a phone. The trigger row takes data-testid.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the trigger row. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the trigger row, the element carrying role="menuitem" and aria-haspopup="menu" ("dialog" with a header or footer).

usage.description: Field is a low-level wrapper for custom, native, or third-party controls that do not already provide field label, description, and status UI. Use it when you need the Field shell around a control you own; use styled Astryx inputs like TextInput, Typeahead, and Select directly when they already expose label, description, and validation props.

bestPractices.description: Wrap custom controls, native inputs, or third-party widgets that need labeling, helper text, optional/required indicators, or validation status.
Always provide a label for accessibility, even if visually hidden with isLabelHidden.
Use inputID and descriptionID to connect the label and description to the inner control with htmlFor and aria-describedby.
Nest Field around styled inputs such as TextInput, Typeahead, Select, DateInput, or TextArea; those components already render their own Field shell.
Use attached status only when the wrapped control is opaque, bordered, and fixed-height; use detached for custom, tall, translucent, or non-bordered controls.
Set both isOptional and isRequired on the same field.
Hide the label without providing an alternative way for the user to understand the field purpose.

docs.description: Status message component for form field validation feedback. Messages are announced to screen readers through persistent live regions (assertive for errors, polite otherwise), so conditional mounting is safe.

usage.description: FieldStatus renders validation feedback for fields and field-like controls. Use it directly for custom controls that need the same error, warning, or success presentation as Field.

bestPractices.description: Use attached status below bordered inputs when the message belongs to that input.
Use detached status for controls like checkboxes, switches, and custom controls where overlap would be visually awkward.
Use FieldStatus for general alerts or page-level notices; use Banner or Toast instead.

A field's status is announced when it first appears and when its message or type changes, not again when a repeated submit fails with the same errors. On such a repeated submit, with the errors unchanged, announce it once from the form with useAnnounce, for example announce(`${errors.length} errors. ${errors[0]}`, 'assertive'), and move focus to the first invalid field. On a first failed submit the fields announce their own errors, so the form adds no announcement.

bestPractices.description: Use attached status below bordered inputs when message belongs to that input.
Use detached status for checkboxes, switches, and custom controls where overlap is visually awkward.
Use FieldStatus for general alerts or page-level notices; use Banner or Toast instead.

props.name: label

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected file(s). Controlled component.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when files are selected or removed.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async change action (React 19 transitions pattern). Use for immediate upload on file selection.

props.name: accept
props.description: Accepted file types. Uses the HTML accept attribute format (e.g. "image/*", ".pdf,.doc").

props.name: isMultiple
props.description: Whether multiple files can be selected. When true, value and onChange use File[] instead of File.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: Maximum file size in bytes. Files exceeding this are rejected with an error status.

props.name: maxFiles
props.description: Maximum number of files (only applies when isMultiple is true).

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Displays an "Optional" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Displays a "Required" indicator next to the label and adds a screen-reader-only "Required" description to the trigger (assistive tech does not reliably announce aria-required on the trigger). Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input, preventing interaction and dimming the element.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the trigger focusable via aria-disabled (opening the file picker stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled FileInput in Tooltip; disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the input in a loading state, showing a spinner and setting aria-busy.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no file is selected.

props.name: mode
props.description: Visual mode. 'input' is a compact inline style; 'dropzone' is a larger area with drag-and-drop support.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status: applies a colored border. If message is provided, displays a floating message below the input. Error type also sets aria-invalid.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon. Dropzone mode does not support attached: use detached or tooltip. From the next minor release, a dropzone resolves attached to detached and defaults to it.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

usage.description: FileInput provides file upload with optional drag-and-drop support. Use it for single or multiple file selection with built-in validation for file type, size, and count. Pair with validation status for upload feedback.

bestPractices.description: Always specify an accept prop to guide users toward valid file types.
Use maxSize and maxFiles to prevent oversized uploads; the component handles validation and error display automatically.
Add a description to communicate constraints like file size limits or accepted formats.
Use changeAction for immediate upload workflows that benefit from optimistic UI.
Don't use FileInput for directory or folder uploads; that is not supported in v1.
Don't avoid dropzone mode unless space is constrained; drag-and-drop is the expected interaction for file uploads.
Don't wrap a disabled FileInput in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: direction
props.description: Controls field arrangement. Vertical stacks top-to-bottom, horizontal uses one fractional grid track per field in logical inline order, and horizontal-labels uses CSS Grid with labels beside inputs on the inline-start side (collapsing to vertical when the viewport is <=480px).

props.name: defaultOptionality
props.description: The state the form treats as its default, so only the exception shows an optional/required indicator. With "optional", only fields marked isRequired show an indicator; with "required", only fields marked isOptional do. A field that restates the default shows nothing. Under "required" the unmarked fields also expose aria-required so screen readers match the visual default; aria-required only, never the native required attribute. CheckboxInput, Switch and CheckboxList are the exception: an unchecked box, an off switch or an empty group is an answer, so they take no required state from the default. A CheckboxInput or Switch is required only through its own isRequired. Leave unset for today's per-field behavior.

props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

usage.description: A layout container that arranges form fields with consistent spacing and direction. FormLayout handles where fields go, not state or submission. Wrap it in a native <form> for that; <form> has no Astryx replacement, so it stays a plain element. Supports vertical (default), horizontal, and horizontal-labels directions, and can be nested to mix them.

bestPractices.description: Stack fields vertically for most forms. It's the easiest to scan top to bottom.
Nest a horizontal FormLayout inside a vertical one when fields naturally pair up, like First Name + Last Name or City + State + ZIP.
Use horizontal-labels for settings pages where labels sit beside their inputs.
Use FormLayout for form state or submission. It's just layout. Wrap it in a native <form> for that.
Put unrelated fields side by side in a horizontal layout. Save it for fields that belong together.
Nest horizontal-labels inside another FormLayout. It uses CSS Grid and needs to be the outermost container.

params.name: element
params.description: The element to drag. The pan writes the `touch-action` its axis needs on it and nothing else; it moves nothing itself.

params.name: options
params.description: Configuration object.

params.name: options.axis
params.description: Limits the drag to one axis. A drag along the other axis is not reported, and that component of every value reads 0, so a scroll across it stays the page’s. Omit it to report both axes; a finger’s scroll that starts on the element then moves the element instead of the page. A trackpad scroll still scrolls the page.

params.name: options.onPan
params.description: Called with `{state, translation, velocity}` as the drag begins, changes, ends at the release, or is cancelled. `state` is 'began', 'changed', 'ended' or 'cancelled'. `translation` is the movement since the drag began, in pixels, without the travel the drag needed to begin, so an element that follows it does not jump. `velocity` is in pixels per second; at 'ended' it is the release velocity, 0 when the finger rested before lifting, and at 'cancelled' it is 0.

returns.name: destroy
returns.description: Removes every listener the pan added and its `touch-action`. A drag in progress is cancelled: `onPan` hears `cancelled`.

usage.description: Reports a drag on an element as values, without React, for a surface the product moves itself: a card that follows the finger, a drawer pulled by its handle. A finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it. A mouse or pen drag that starts on selectable text selects that text, and the pan reports nothing. Give that text `user-select: none`. The drag claims its touch at UIKit’s 10 pt, as `UIPanGestureRecognizer` does, so a tap stays a tap and a press or a long press is never reported as a pan. Use the `usePanGesture` hook in React. Where a component already offers the behavior, use its prop instead: BottomSheet's `snapPoints`, Carousel's `hasSnap`. Its example is on the usePanGesture page: one draggable box, made once with the hook and once with createPanGesture.

bestPractices.description: Move the element from `translation` added to where it was when the drag began, so it moves with the finger from the moment the drag claims it.
At `ended`, hand `velocity` to the animation that settles the element, so a flick carries on at the speed it was released.
Call `destroy` when the element leaves the page, so no listener outlives it.
Read the element’s layout on every `changed` event to place it; `translation` already says where the finger is.

accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology
accessibility.description: A drag has no keyboard or assistive-technology path of its own: whatever the drag does needs another way to do it, such as buttons, arrow keys or a menu.

accessibility.name: Reduce Motion
accessibility.description: The pan moves nothing itself, so Reduce Motion applies to the motion you drive from it: a settle or a throw goes to its end without travel when the person asks for reduced motion.

docsDense.description: Reports a drag on an element as values ({state, translation, velocity}), without React; a finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it, though a mouse or pen drag on selectable text selects it instead (give that text user-select: none). Returns {destroy}.

paramDescriptions.element: element to drag; the pan writes only its touch-action.
paramDescriptions.options.axis: 'x' | 'y': limit to one axis; the other is never reported and reads 0.
paramDescriptions.options.onPan: ({state, translation, velocity}): state 'began' | 'changed' | 'ended' | 'cancelled'; translation px since the drag began (no jump); velocity px/s, release velocity at 'ended', 0 at 'cancelled'.

returnDescriptions.destroy: () => void; removes every listener and the touch-action, cancels a drag in progress.

usage.description: Drag as values without React, for a surface you move. Claims at UIKit’s 10 pt. No keyboard path of its own (WCAG 2.5.7); Reduce Motion applies to what you animate. Prefer component props (BottomSheet snapPoints, Carousel hasSnap); in React, usePanGesture.

bestPractices.description: Move from translation + the offset at began, so the element moves with the finger from the claim.
Hand the ended velocity to the settling animation.
Call destroy when the element leaves the page.
Read layout on every changed event; use translation.

anatomy.description: Optional GridSpan wrapper that changes one item's column or row participation.

usage.description: A CSS grid layout container for arranging children in rows and columns. Use Grid for card galleries, dashboards, and any multi-column layout. For columns that reflow on small screens, use `columns={{minWidth, max}}`; a numeric `columns` is exactly N columns at every width and never reflows.

bestPractices.description: Default to responsive columns for anything that must survive a phone: `columns={{minWidth: 240, max: 4}}` renders at most 4 columns, each at least 240px, and drops to one full-width column when narrow.
Use `columns={4}` for a row that must work on small screens; a number never reflows and renders four narrow tracks on a phone. Reserve numbers for rows that must stay fixed, such as a 7-day week.
Always pair `minWidth` with `max`: `max` caps the count on wide screens and lets the last column shrink to a narrow container; `{minWidth}` alone overflows a phone narrower than `minWidth`.
Use `repeat: 'fill'` (the default) for consistent item widths. Use `'fit'` when items should stretch to fill leftover space.
Write manual CSS grid; Grid handles spacing and responsive behavior for you.
Use `HStack` with wrapping for grids; use Grid instead.
Track templates use CSS-variable indirection (not raw inline styles), so `xstyle` overrides of `gridTemplateColumns` (including inside `@media` queries) take effect.

docs.description: Grid container with fixed or responsive columns; `{minWidth, max}` reflows, a number never does.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column configuration. A number creates exactly N `1fr` tracks at every width and never reflows (e.g. `columns={3}`); a child's minimum content may widen its track. For columns that reflow on small screens, use `{minWidth, max}`. Use an object for responsive columns: `minWidth` sets the minimum column width in px, `repeat` controls track behavior (`"fill"` preserves empty tracks for consistent widths, `"fit"` collapses empty tracks so items stretch; defaults to `"fill"`), and `max` caps the maximum number of columns.

usage.description: A CSS grid layout container for arranging children in rows and columns. Use Grid for card galleries, dashboards, and any multi-column layout. For columns that reflow on small screens, use `columns={{minWidth, max}}`; a numeric `columns` is exactly N columns at every width and never reflows.

bestPractices.description: Default to responsive columns for anything that must survive a phone: columns={{minWidth: 240, max: 4}} = at most 4 columns, each >= 240px, one full-width column when narrow.
Use columns={4} for rows that must work on small screens; a number never reflows (4 narrow tracks on a phone). Numbers only for rows that must stay fixed, e.g. a 7-day week.
Always pair minWidth with max: max caps the count on wide screens and lets the last column shrink to a narrow container; {minWidth} alone overflows a phone narrower than minWidth.
Use repeat: 'fill' (the default) for consistent item widths. Use 'fit' when items should stretch to fill leftover space.
Write manual CSS grid; Grid handles spacing and responsive behavior for you.
Use HStack with wrapping for grids; use Grid instead.
track templates use CSS-var indirection, not inline styles, so xstyle/@media overrides of gridTemplateColumns work.

usage.description: Returns a handle to pass to a component whose size changes, such as TreeList or Collapsible. When that component changes size, it and the content after it inside `containerRef` animate together on one shared motion role. Fixed and stuck sticky elements stay put, the glide never scrolls the area, and Reduce Motion is respected. It applies under every pointer, a mouse included. Without the handle a component keeps its jump: content after it takes its place at once. Content after the change may mix Astryx components and your own elements; none of it opts in.

bestPractices.description: Create one handle per scroll container or panel and pass the same handle to every component in it whose size changes.
Pass the ref you already give ScrollableArea as containerRef; ScrollableArea does not register itself.
Wrap the content after a disclosure in an extra element to make it move; everything after the change inside the container moves on its own.
Animate height yourself alongside it; the glide moves content with a compositor translate and never animates height.
