params.name: ref
params.description: The ref of the one element to animate, the same ref you pass to the element: another hook, such as a gesture hook, can take it too, so a drag and an animation share one element. After every render the animator follows the element behind it. When the element unmounts its motion stops and its values return to rest, so a remount starts at rest, and so does a node that replaces it. Before the element mounts, and while it is unmounted, every call does nothing and `animate` and `decay` resolve at once.

returns.name: animator
returns.description: The element's animator, the same object on every render: `animate(target, {velocity?})` springs channels to a target on the state-change motion Astryx's components use, `decay(velocity)` coasts them from a release velocity, `set(values)` jumps them, `get()` and `getVelocity()` read them, and `stop()` halts them. The channels are `x` and `y` (px), `scale` (1 at the element's size), `rotate` (degrees) and `opacity` (0 to 1). `animate` and `decay` return a promise that resolves when the motion ends. Calling it never re-renders the component. Calls before the ref attaches do nothing and resolve at once.

usage.description: Animates one element with the motion Astryx's own components use. Call `animator.animate` to spring an element to new values on the state-change motion, `animator.decay` to fling it with the momentum of a released scroll view, and `animator.set` to move it directly, so a card can follow a finger, snap back and be thrown away. To animate an area's layout as its items change, use `useAnimatedLayout`; for what a component already animates, such as a sheet's detents or a carousel's snapping, use the component's own props. Outside React, use `createAnimator`.

bestPractices.description: Call the animator from event handlers and effects: it lives outside render, so animating never re-renders the component.
Start every `animate` that follows a drag with the release velocity, so the element carries on as it was thrown.
Reach every state an animation shows without the animation too: a key, a button or a menu item that calls the same code.
Keep the animated values in React state: read them with `animator.get()` when you need them.

accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology
accessibility.description: An animator moves an element; it adds no way to act. Give every action an animation stands for a control a keyboard and a screen reader can reach, such as a button that discards a card, and have it call `animate`, which Reduce Motion turns into a fade in place. Keep `decay` for a throw the person made: Reduce Motion keeps the momentum of a coast, as it continues that throw. Keep focus on an element that stays on screen: move it before you fling its element away.

accessibility.name: Reduce Motion
accessibility.description: When the person asks for reduced motion, every call is planned for them. On a touch screen a move or a scale becomes a short opacity cross-fade: the element fades out where it was and fades back in where it lands. With a mouse it lands at once. A decay of `x` and `y` keeps its momentum, as it continues the throw the person made; a decay of `scale`, `rotate` or `opacity` is planned like a move. No option turns this off.

docsDense.description: Animates the element behind ref (x, y, scale, rotate, opacity) with Astryx's motion; returns the animator.

paramDescriptions.ref: The element ref; share it with a gesture hook to drag and animate one element.

returnDescriptions.animator: animate(target, {velocity?}), decay(velocity), set, get, getVelocity, stop; stable, never re-renders.

usage.description: Spring with animate, fling with decay, follow a finger with set. Reduce Motion: a cross-fade on touch, at once with a mouse; decay keeps its momentum.

bestPractices.description: Pass the release velocity to animate after a drag.
Keep animated values in state; read animator.get().

params.name: options
params.description: Configuration object.

params.name: options.hasReplace
params.description: The instance states one current state, such as a search's result count: each message it writes withdraws the instance's previous message while that one has not been spoken yet, whatever their politeness, and is spoken at its own politeness. A message already spoken stays. Messages from other instances, and from instances without hasReplace, still join. Give each state a component reports its own instance, for example one for the result count and one for selection changes.

returns.name: announce
returns.description: Speaks a message through the live region the caller can be heard from: the shared one on the page body, or, when the calling component is rendered inside an open Astryx modal (Dialog, modal BottomSheet, modal Drawer, Lightbox, MobileNav, CommandPalette), a persistent region inside that modal, since a native modal hides the page-body region from assistive technology. Politeness defaults to "polite"; messages announced in the same frame are joined, in order, into one announcement, and an identical repeat is kept once, except that each message from a hasReplace instance replaces the previous message of that instance not yet spoken. An empty message clears any lingering status, including joined messages not yet spoken, instead of announcing.

usage.description: Imperatively announces a message to screen readers through a visually-hidden live region. Use it for state that is only conveyed visually; search result counts, "no results", loading and saved confirmations, validation errors (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages). The polite and assertive regions are created empty on first use and stay mounted, which is what makes announcements reliable: most screen readers ignore a live region that is inserted together with its content. Each message is cleared a couple of seconds after it is announced so stale status does not linger in the accessibility tree. A message is delivered where its caller is: from inside an open Astryx modal it goes to a region inside that modal and is heard there with no change to the calling code; a message sent just as the modal is dismissed is delivered through whatever is exposed afterwards rather than lost. A call made outside the modal, even by the component that renders it, uses the page-body region.

bestPractices.description: Reach for this instead of hand-rolling an aria-live div; a region rendered with its content usually does not announce at all.
Keep "polite" for status and result counts; reserve "assertive" for errors and time-sensitive alerts, since it interrupts whatever the screen reader is saying.
Announce the outcome, not the interaction; "12 results" rather than "search ran".
Send a value that keeps changing, such as a result count as the user types, through its own useAnnounce({hasReplace: true}) instance, so input faster than a frame says only the latest count.
Announce content that is already visible and correctly labeled in the DOM; that doubles up for screen reader users.

docsDense.description: Imperative screen-reader announcements via a visually-hidden live region: the page-body one, or one inside the open Astryx modal the caller is rendered in (a native modal hides the body region). Polite + assertive regions created empty on first use + kept mounted, so announcements are reliable (most AT ignore a live region inserted together w/ its content). Messages auto-clear after ~2s.

paramDescriptions.options.hasReplace: instance states one current state (e.g. a search's result count): each message withdraws the instance's previous one not yet spoken, whatever politeness, spoken at its own; spoken messages stay; other instances + instances w/o hasReplace still join. Default false.

returnDescriptions.announce: speaks message through the live region the caller is heard from: page body, or inside the open Astryx modal (Dialog, modal BottomSheet/Drawer, Lightbox, MobileNav, CommandPalette) the calling component is rendered in. politeness defaults "polite"; same-frame messages join in order, identical repeat kept once, except a hasReplace instance replaces its own not-yet-spoken message; empty message clears lingering + not-yet-spoken status.

usage.description: Announces visual-only state to screen readers: result counts, "no results", loading / saved confirmations, validation errors (WCAG 4.1.3). Regions mounted empty up front, so updates announce; text auto-clears so stale status does not linger in a11y tree.

bestPractices.description: Use instead of hand-rolled aria-live div; region rendered w/ its content usually does not announce.
"polite" for status / counts; "assertive" only for errors + time-sensitive alerts (it interrupts).
Announce outcome, not interaction; "12 results", not "search ran".
Changing value (result count while typing): own useAnnounce({hasReplace: true}) instance, so faster-than-a-frame input says only the latest.
Announce content already visible + labeled in DOM; doubles up for AT users.

returns.description: Writes text to the clipboard. On success flips isCopied to true, announces the configured message, restarts the reset timer, and resolves true. A clipboard rejection is a silent no-op that leaves the copied state unchanged and resolves false.

usage.description: Copy-to-clipboard behavior: the clipboard write, a transient isCopied flag with its own reset timer, and an optional polite screen-reader announcement. Extracted so every copy affordance is a thin control over one implementation instead of re-deriving the timer and announcement. Rapid re-copies restart the reset timer so the confirmation always lasts the full duration, and the timer is cleaned up on unmount. CodeBlock and Timestamp build their built-in copy buttons on it; reach for it directly when building a copy affordance that is not a plain icon button (a menu item, a labeled text button, a copy-on-click value chip).

params.name: options
params.description: Configuration object for the reveal container. Optional.

params.name: options.isEnabled
params.description: When false the hook is inert: the container gets no styles and content getters return no styles, so content is always shown. Read on every render, so a component can flip it after mount (e.g. revealOn === "hover").

returns.name: getContainerProps
returns.description: Spread onto the container whose hover/focus-within drives the reveal. Accepts hoverDelay (ms the pointer must dwell before the reveal starts: a hover-intent gate like Tooltip's and HoverCard's delay, so a cursor sweeping across a list leaves nothing painted behind it) and forceState ("active" | "inactive") to pin the trigger state when a caller owns it: a motion gate, a scroll, or a row whose menu is open. "inactive" still yields to keyboard focus and coarse pointers.

returns.name: getContentRevealProps
returns.description: Spread onto each revealed / concealed child. Accepts isRevealInverted to conceal-on-hover instead of reveal-on-hover, isLayoutPreserved to reserve the layout box while hidden (opacity-only) and avoid layout shift, and forceVisibility ("shown" | "hidden") to pin this one element's appearance whatever the container is doing. "hidden" yields to focus.

usage.description: A headless hover/focus reveal primitive. Gives a container a scoped trigger that reveals (or conceals) content inside it when the container is hovered or receives keyboard focus: the classic "row actions appear on hover" pattern. The reveal is CSS-only: no hover state lives in React and hovering never triggers a re-render. The caller authors no StyleX for the reveal itself; the hook hands out the container and content styles, and a nested container shadows its ancestor, so nested containers never leak hover/focus into one another. Accessible by construction: revealed content is visually hidden at rest with position and opacity (never display:none), so it stays mounted, keeps its place in the tab order, and is announced to assistive technology; it reveals on :focus-within so keyboard users see it when tabbing in, stays visible on touch (never gated behind hover on coarse pointers), and honors prefers-reduced-motion.

bestPractices.description: Destructure getContainerProps and getContentRevealProps; spread getContainerProps() on the container (via mergeProps with your own stylex.props) and getContentRevealProps() on the content to reveal.
Use for secondary affordances: reveal-on-hover row actions (edit/copy/remove on list or table rows) and overlay controls on a card or media tile (e.g. Thumbnail's remove button).
Gate the reveal with isEnabled when a consumer prop decides whether content is revealed on hover or always shown; it can change at any time.
Pass isLayoutPreserved for absolutely-positioned or overlay content to reserve its box and avoid layout shift when it appears.
Set a hoverDelay (100-250ms) on rows in a long list, so a cursor travelling across the list does not light up every row it passes; keyboard and touch still reveal immediately.

Reach for forceState when something other than the pointer owns the interaction (a drag, a scroll or motion gate, an open row menu), and forceVisibility when just one element should ignore the container.
Reach past the API into the hook's private custom properties (--_reveal-opacity and friends) to suppress a reveal; use forceState / forceVisibility, which survive a rename.
Use it to hide content that must always be discoverable; keep essential actions visible instead of gating them behind hover.

params.description: The axis the element moves along. A new one creates the drag again, starting where the element is.

params.name: options.snapPoints
params.description: Offsets in px along `axis` from the element's resting position, such as `[0, 240, 480]`, sorted before use (`onSettle` and `settleTo` count in that order); an empty list makes the drag do nothing. Unlike BottomSheet's `snapPoints`, they are not fractions of the viewport. New ones create the drag again and nothing more: the element stays where it is, a settle in flight included, and the next drag or `settleTo` starts there.

params.name: options.flickThreshold
params.description: A release faster than this, in px/s, carries to the next snap point in its direction. The default is the flick speed measured for UIKit's sheet. A new one creates the drag again, as new snap points do.

params.name: options.onSettle
params.description: Called with the snap point's index once the element settles on it. The latest function is the one called, so it may be new on every render.

returns.name: settleTo
returns.description: Settles the element on the snap point at `index` without a drag: the keyboard path. The same function on every render.

usage.description: Lets a drag move an element along one axis and settles it on snap points when the finger lifts, the way an iOS sheet settles on its detents: on the nearest snap point to where it is, on the next one in its direction after a quick flick, and back where it started when the finger was moving back. The settle continues the release's velocity. For a bottom sheet, use BottomSheet's `snapPoints`; for a scrolling row, Carousel's `hasSnap`. Outside React, use `createDragToSnapPoints`.

bestPractices.description: Offer the same positions without a drag: buttons or keys that call `settleTo`.
Keep the settled index in state from `onSettle`, and render what the position means from it.
Use it for a sheet or a carousel: their own props already settle the way people expect.

accessibility.name: Keyboard and assistive technology
accessibility.description: A drag is one way in, never the only one. Give each snap point a control a keyboard and a screen reader can reach, such as Expand and Collapse buttons, and call `settleTo` from it. When a position changes what the element shows, announce the change.

accessibility.name: Reduce Motion
accessibility.description: When the person asks for reduced motion, the settle after a touch drag becomes a short cross-fade into the snap point, as does any settle on a device whose primary pointer is coarse, such as a tablet; after a mouse or pen drag elsewhere it lands at once. `settleTo` fades on such a device and lands at once with a fine primary pointer. While the finger is down, the element still follows it.

docsDense.description: A drag that settles the element at ref on snap points (px offsets): {settleTo}.

paramDescriptions.options.flickThreshold: px/s past which a release carries one snap point; 1008.

usage.description: Traps focus within a container element following the WAI-ARIA dialog focus trap pattern. Listens to focus events on the document and redirects focus back into the container if a Tab from inside it moves focus out. Handles both Tab and Shift+Tab wrapping. A Tab pressed while focus is outside the container is left to the page, so an open non-modal surface never takes over the focus order of the page. When the trap deactivates or unmounts, focus is restored to the element that was focused before activation, unless focus was already moved elsewhere or never entered the trap (so popups that keep focus on their trigger, like comboboxes, are unaffected). Mouse clicks outside the container are not intercepted; use a light-dismiss handler for that.

bestPractices.description: Call focusFirst() when opening a dialog/modal to move focus into the trapped region.
Provide an onEscape callback to close the dialog when Escape is pressed.
Rely on the built-in focus restoration on close; only add your own onHide focus handling when you need to send focus somewhere other than the previously-focused element.
Use on non-modal content like tooltips or dropdowns; those need light-dismiss, not focus trapping.

params.name: options
params.description: Configuration object for grid focus behavior.

params.name: options.columns
params.description: Number of columns in the grid. Used for up/down navigation (moves by this many cells).

params.name: options.onNavigateAfter
params.description: Callback when navigation would go after the last cell. Receives the column index and offset.

params.name: options.onPageUp
params.description: Callback for Page Up key (e.g., navigate to previous month in calendars). Receives the key event, so `event.shiftKey` can select a larger step, such as a year.

params.name: options.onPageDown
params.description: Callback for Page Down key (e.g., navigate to next month in calendars). Receives the key event, so `event.shiftKey` can select a larger step, such as a year.

params.description: Own a single roving tab stop across the grid: one focusable cell (its resolved focus target) carries tabindex="0", the rest -1. Stamped/repaired on render and moved with arrow navigation. Attach the returned handleFocus to the container onFocus.

returns.name: handleKeyDown
returns.description: Key down handler to attach to the grid container.

usage.description: Manages keyboard navigation within a 2D grid following the WAI-ARIA grid pattern. Supports arrow keys for cell-to-cell navigation, Home/End for row boundaries, Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End for grid boundaries, and Page Up/Down for custom callbacks (e.g., month navigation in calendars). Boundary navigation callbacks allow cross-grid navigation.

usage.description: Draws the standard focus ring on the indicator of a control whose real input is visually hidden; a checkbox or radio focuses an opacity-0 input, so the ring has to appear on the picture beside it. The ring is painted imperatively on the indicator's own element, which is the only element whose border-radius can shape it, and only on :focus-visible, so pointer clicks stay quiet. Owning it here means a theme-supplied indicator cannot ship a control with no visible focus (WCAG 2.4.7) by ignoring a prop.

params.description: Configuration object for the keyboard hint.

params.description: Which arrow-key axis the composite navigates, controlling which arrow icons the hint shows (← → for horizontal, ↑ ↓ for vertical, all four for both).

params.description: Milliseconds before the hint auto-dismisses after appearing.

params.description: Whether the hint is enabled. Set to false to suppress it for a specific instance (e.g. a disabled or read-only widget).

returns.description: The popover hint element to render inside the composite container (as the last child). Portals to the top layer via popover="manual", renders arrow keys with Kbd, and manages its own visibility; render it unconditionally.

returns.name: onFocus
returns.description: Attach to the container onFocus. Shows the hint on the first keyboard-focus (:focus-visible) entry from outside the composite.

returns.name: onBlur
returns.description: Attach to the container onBlur. Hides the hint when focus leaves the composite entirely, and re-anchors when focus moves within.

returns.name: onKeyDown
returns.description: Attach to the container onKeyDown. Dismisses the hint on the first arrow press (the user has discovered the interaction). Never prevents default or stops propagation.

usage.description: Shows an ephemeral "← → to navigate" hint anchored to the focused item the first time a roving-tabindex composite (Toolbar, TabList, SegmentedControl, etc.) receives keyboard focus. It teaches sighted keyboard users that arrow keys move within the group. The hint renders arrow keys with Kbd in the top layer (popover="manual") and is CSS-anchor-positioned to the focused element, so overflow containers never clip it. It auto-dismisses on the first arrow press, on timeout, or on blur, and does not re-show for that instance. Toolbar, TabList, and SegmentedControl wire this in automatically; reach for the hook directly only when building a custom roving-tabindex widget.

params.name: ref
params.description: The element to drag. The hook creates one pan for the element behind the ref, creates a new one when the ref moves to another node or `axis` changes, and destroys it at unmount; a drag in progress then ends without a `cancelled` event, since an effect never calls `onPan`.

params.name: options
params.description: Configuration object.

params.name: options.axis
params.description: Limits the drag to one axis. A drag along the other axis is not reported, and that component of every value reads 0. Omit it to report both axes.

params.name: options.onPan
params.description: Called with `{state, translation, velocity}` as the drag begins, changes, ends at the release, or is cancelled. `state` is 'began', 'changed', 'ended' or 'cancelled'. `translation` is the movement since the drag began, in pixels: the travel the drag needed to begin is not part of it, so an element that follows it does not jump. `velocity` is in pixels per second; at 'ended' it is the release velocity (0 when the finger rested before lifting), and at 'cancelled' it is 0. Read through a ref: a new function each render re-creates nothing.

returns.name: void
returns.description: Nothing: the hook hands out no recognizer. Without React, `createPanGesture(element, options)` takes the same options and returns `{destroy}`, which removes every listener it added and cancels a drag in progress.

usage.description: Reports a drag on an element as values, for a surface the product moves itself: a card that follows the finger, a drawer pulled by its handle. A finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it. A mouse or pen drag that starts on selectable text selects that text, and the pan reports nothing. Give that text `user-select: none`. The drag claims its touch at UIKit’s 10 pt, as `UIPanGestureRecognizer` does, so a tap stays a tap, and a press or a long press is never reported as a pan. With `axis`, a scroll across that axis that starts on the element stays the page’s; without it, the pan takes a drag in any direction, so a finger’s scroll that starts on the element moves the element instead of the page. A trackpad scroll still scrolls the page. The hook is a thin layer over `createPanGesture`, the same API for code without React. A drag has no keyboard or assistive-technology path of its own: whatever the drag does needs another way to do it, such as buttons or arrow keys (WCAG 2.5.7). The pan moves nothing itself, so Reduce Motion applies to the motion you drive from it: honor the user’s reduced-motion setting in the animation that moves the element. Where a component already offers the behavior, use its prop instead: BottomSheet’s `snapPoints`, Carousel’s `hasSnap`.

Hold the drag offset in a large component’s state: each `changed` event renders the component that holds it.
Recognize taps or long presses with it; `useLongPress` and the components’ own press handling own those.

returns.description: The marker attribute to spread on the element that paints the press. Compose one of `interactionOverlayStyles` (from `@astryxdesign/core/utils`) on the same element — `backgroundColor` or `backgroundImage` for a surface whose hover and press are the system's overlays, `pressedBackgroundColor` for one whose hover is its own — and it paints the pressed token on the first frame of a press and fades it over the release, keeping `:active` for a mouse on a desktop. On a phone or tablet, where the stylesheet drops `:active`, the controller also paints a mouse, trackpad or Space-key press: at once, held while the button or key is down, faded at the release. A press is themed through `--color-overlay-pressed`.

usage.description: The touch press model every Astryx pressable uses, for a local component that paints its own press. Under a finger, CSS `:active` paints on the touch itself and can outlive the start of a scroll; the press model instead tracks the touch the way UIKit tracks a control: it highlights as the finger lands (after the content-touch delay inside a scroller, where a flick paints nothing), a quick tap answers at the lift, and a scroll that takes the touch cancels it with no fade. One document-level controller does this for every marked element (installed by the first pressable to mount, removed by the last to unmount), so calling the hook adds no listener or state to your element. On a desktop a mouse press is still your `:active` rule: keep it, and drop it under `@media (pointer: coarse)` the way the built-in components do. That query reads the primary pointer, so on a phone or tablet it also drops `:active` for a connected mouse, trackpad or keyboard; the controller paints those presses there (at once, faded at the release), so nothing goes unanswered.

params.name: isLocked
params.description: whether page scroll should be locked.

usage.description: Locks page scroll while active and keeps the page where it is. The page gets overflow: hidden (on the root, or on body when its own overflow is the one the viewport uses), which stops wheel, keyboard and scrollbar scrolling, and overscroll-behavior-y: none on the root and body, which stops the overscroll bounce while the lock holds. Where the primary pointer is coarse (phones and tablets), a one-finger pan that would scroll the page is cancelled, because iOS Safari scrolls an overflow: hidden page under a finger; pans that a scroller inside the overlay can take, drags on a native range input, pinch-zoom, and one-finger drags on a pinch-zoomed page (which pan the zoomed view) still work. The scroll offset never changes, so nothing jumps when the lock starts or ends, and iOS Safari keeps its toolbar as it was. Where the hidden scrollbar takes layout space (desktop), the hook holds its gutter open with scrollbar-gutter: stable, so the page, including any position: fixed chrome, does not shift sideways.

bestPractices.description: Use when opening full-screen modals or dialogs to prevent background content from scrolling.
Pass the same boolean that controls dialog visibility (e.g., isOpen) as the isLocked parameter.
Use for non-modal overlays like popovers or tooltips; users should be able to scroll away from those.

Offset never changes: no jump, iOS toolbar unchanged. Holds the hidden scrollbar's gutter open (scrollbar-gutter: stable) so the page (incl. position: fixed chrome) does not shift sideways.

params.type: (item: HTMLElement, id: string | undefined) => boolean | void
params.description: Called when Enter/Space activates a treeitem. Return true when handled; return false/undefined to let the hook fall back to toggling expansion.

params.name: options.onActiveChange
params.description: Notified when the hook moves focus to a treeitem. Consumers use this to move a single roving tab stop.

params.name: options.hasRovingTabIndex
params.description: When true, the hook owns a single roving tab stop across the visible treeitems (stamps tabindex 0/-1, repairs on mount, moves with navigation). Preserves an existing tabindex="0" seed on mount. Attach the returned `handleFocus` to keep the stop in sync after clicks.

params.name: options.typeahead
params.description: Whether typeahead (jump to next item whose text starts with the typed characters, ignoring case, accents, the stroked letters đ ł ø ħ ŧ ƀ and Turkish ı/İ in every locale) is enabled.

returns.name: handleFocus
returns.description: Focus handler to attach to the container's onFocus. Keeps the roving tab stop in sync when hasRovingTabIndex is enabled; a no-op otherwise, so always safe to attach.

returns.name: focusLast

components.name: HoverCard
components.description: Component wrapper for hover card display: a richer, larger overlay triggered on hover or focus.

props.name: children
props.description: The trigger. Text children, a string or number or text written around an expression such as `Edited {when}`, are wrapped in a focusable inline span; holes such as `false` and `null` are ignored. With element children, HoverCard wires the first element, so that element does not need to accept a ref.

props.name: content
props.description: Hover card content.

props.name: placement
props.description: Position relative to the anchor element. Logical: start/end resolve against the popover's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors in pure CSS).

props.name: alignment
props.description: Alignment along the placement axis. Logical: start/end resolve against the popover's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors in pure CSS).

props.name: delay
props.description: Show delay in milliseconds.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: Hide delay in milliseconds.

props.name: focusTrigger
props.description: When focus should open the hover card. auto opens when the trigger itself takes focus, or focus lands inside a trigger that is focusable at that moment, so a roving-tabindex member opens when the arrow keys reach it.

props.name: touchTrigger
props.description: What a tap does where there is no hover. auto opens on tap unless the trigger performs an action of its own (a button, link, or form control), whose tap belongs to the control; an aria-disabled control performs none, so a tap on it opens its reason. tap always opens. none never opens on touch. A tap-opened card is dismissed by a tap outside it.

props.name: isEnabled
props.description: Enables or disables the hover and focus triggers.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the hover card popup. When provided, the popup is exposed as a named role="dialog"; when omitted, it falls back to role="group" (a group may validly be unnamed).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when hover card visibility changes. Called with true when shown and false when hidden.

props.name: hasHoverIndication
props.description: Shows a dashed underline on a text trigger. auto shows it when children is text: strings and numbers, such as `Edited {when}`, with holes such as `false` and `null` ignored. It has no effect on an element trigger, which keeps its own styling.

props.name: isDefaultOpen
props.description: Whether the hover card should be shown on mount. Still dismissible.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. true holds the card open. false holds it closed against hover and focus. A controlled card answers Escape by calling onOpenChange(false) without closing; it closes when you set isOpen to false, and focus inside the card then returns to the trigger.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the card surface, the element that carries the hover-card theme target.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name added to the card surface, beside the hover-card target class.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the card surface.

usage.description: HoverCard shows additional information when the user hovers or focuses a trigger element. Use it for profile cards, link summaries, or inline definitions where the user needs more context without navigating away.

bestPractices.description: Keep content supplementary; hover cards should enhance understanding without blocking the primary workflow.
Provide a dashed underline on text triggers so users know the element is hoverable.
Use the hook API (useHoverCard) when you need more control over timing or placement.
Leave touchTrigger on auto so a tap opens the card on triggers that do nothing else, and stays out of the way on triggers that perform an action.
Place critical actions or required information inside a hover card; users may miss content that only appears on hover.
Use a hover card when a simple Tooltip or Popover would suffice.
Use a HoverCard for content the user must interact with; it disappears when the cursor leaves.

Prefer placing HoverCard in a block context rather than directly in a

, heading, or link. Those placements are supported when necessary through a corrective portal, but the DOM and tab order may differ.

props.description: 在没有悬停的触摸设备上，轻点的行为。auto：轻点即打开，除非触发元素本身会执行操作（按钮、链接、表单控件），此时轻点归该控件所有；设置了 aria-disabled 的控件不执行操作，因此轻点它会显示其原因。tap：始终轻点打开。none：触摸永不打开。轻点打开的卡片可通过点击卡片外部关闭。

props.name: isEnabled
props.description: 启用或禁用悬停和聚焦触发器。

props.name: label

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: 悬浮卡片可见性变化时触发的回调。显示时传入 true，隐藏时传入 false。

props.name: hasHoverIndication
props.description: 在文本触发元素上显示虚线下划线。auto：当 children 是文本（字符串和数字，例如 `Edited {when}`，忽略 `false`、`null` 等空位）时显示。对元素触发器无效，元素保留自身样式。

props.name: isDefaultOpen
props.description: 是否在挂载时显示悬浮卡片。仍然可以关闭。

props.name: isOpen
props.description: 受控的打开状态。true 保持卡片打开。false 使悬停和焦点都无法打开卡片。受控卡片响应 Escape 时调用 onOpenChange(false) 而不关闭；将 isOpen 设为 false 时关闭，此时卡片内的焦点返回触发元素。

props.name: className
props.description: 添加到卡片表面的类名，与 hover-card 目标类名并列。

usage.description: HoverCard shows additional information when the user hovers or focuses a trigger element. Use it for profile cards, link summaries, or inline definitions where the user needs more context without navigating away.

bestPractices.description: Keep content supplementary; hover cards should enhance understanding without blocking the primary workflow.
Provide a dashed underline on text triggers so users know the element is hoverable.
Use the hook API (useHoverCard) when you need more control over timing or placement.
Leave touchTrigger on auto so a tap opens the card on triggers that do nothing else, and stays out of the way on triggers that perform an action.
Place critical actions or required information inside a hover card; users may miss content that only appears on hover.
Use a hover card when a simple Tooltip or Popover would suffice.
Use a HoverCard for content the user must interact with; it disappears when the cursor leaves.

Prefer placing HoverCard in a block context rather than directly in a

, heading, or link. Those placements are supported when necessary through a corrective portal, but the DOM and tab order may differ.

params.name: placement
params.description: Position relative to the trigger. Logical: start/end resolve against the popover's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors in pure CSS).

params.name: alignment
params.description: Alignment along the placement axis. Logical: start/end resolve against the popover's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors in pure CSS).

params.name: delay
params.description: Delay before showing the hover card on hover, in milliseconds.

params.name: hideDelay
params.description: Delay before hiding after mouse or focus leaves, in milliseconds.

params.name: focusTrigger
params.description: When focus should open the hover card. auto opens when the trigger itself takes focus, or focus lands inside a trigger that is focusable at that moment, so a roving-tabindex member opens when the arrow keys reach it.

params.name: touchTrigger
params.description: What a tap does where there is no hover. auto opens on tap unless the trigger performs an action of its own (an aria-disabled control performs none); tap always opens; none never opens on touch.

params.name: isEnabled
params.description: Whether hover and focus triggers are enabled.

params.name: label
params.description: Accessible name for the hover card popup. When provided, the popup is exposed as a named role="dialog"; when omitted, it falls back to role="group" (a group may validly be unnamed).

params.name: isOpen
params.description: Controlled open state. true force-shows, false force-hides, undefined lets hover/focus manage visibility.

params.name: isDefaultOpen
params.description: Whether the hover card should be shown on mount.

params.name: onShow
params.description: Callback fired when the hover card becomes visible.

params.name: onHide
params.description: Callback fired when the hover card is hidden.

returns.name: ref
returns.description: Combined ref that sets both position and interaction on the same trigger element.

returns.name: positionRef
returns.description: Ref for the positioning anchor element. Use when position and interaction live on different elements.

returns.name: interactionRef
returns.description: Ref for the hover/focus interaction element. Use with positionRef for split trigger patterns.

returns.name: anchorId
returns.description: CSS anchor name for advanced positioning cases.

returns.name: describedBy
returns.description: ID to compose into aria-describedby on the trigger.

returns.name: renderHoverCard
returns.description: Render function for the anchor-positioned hover card content. The positioning opt-out is excluded: the hover card always derives its position from placement/alignment.

returns.name: show
returns.description: Imperatively show the hover card immediately.

returns.name: hide
returns.description: Imperatively hide the hover card immediately.

Prefer the HoverCard component for standard trigger-content pairs; use the hook for custom trigger patterns.
Use for simple text hints: use Tooltip or useTooltip instead.

usage.description: Wraps your app to set the active locale and (optionally) merge additional translation catalogs + per-locale overrides. Astryx components inside the subtree resolve their strings against this context. If no provider is present, components fall back to the shipped English defaults.

anatomy.name: Provider boundary
anatomy.description: A nonvisual context boundary that supplies locale, message catalogs, overrides, and direction to descendant Astryx components, and a calendar system to `Calendar`. It renders no DOM element.

bestPractices.description: Use shipped Astryx locale catalogs from `@astryxdesign/core/locales/*` when one exists for your target locale.
Use a same-shape local catalog only when Astryx has not shipped that locale yet or you are testing in-progress translations.
Use real BCP 47 tags such as `fr-FR`, `pt-BR`, or `ar-SA`; regional locales fall back to their base language before English.

Set the `dir` attribute on `<html>` (or a wrapping element) yourself; the provider does not set it. Astryx components mirror layout and directional icons from the DOM `dir`, so an RTL locale won't visually mirror without it. Use `getLocaleDirection(locale)` to derive the value for both the provider and the DOM.

Set `calendar` to show `Calendar`, `DateInput`, `DateRangeInput`, and `DateTimeInput` in another calendar system and write Timestamp, PowerSearch, and Schedule dates in it. A locale never selects the calendar: `fa-IR` shows Gregorian dates until you set `calendar="persian"`, and a `-u-ca-` keyword in `locale`, as in `th-TH-u-ca-buddhist`, keeps Gregorian dates too. Date values stay Gregorian ISO strings.
Cast custom catalog maps to `any`; the i18n package exports `ProviderMessagesByLocale`, `MessagesByLocale`, `Catalog`, and `RuntimeCatalog` for local catalog typing.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 language tag for the active locale (e.g. "en", "pt", "pt-BR", "zh-Hans"). Regional tags fall back to their base language, then to the shipped "en" catalog.

props.name: messages
props.description: Optional map of BCP 47 tag to a rich or generated runtime catalog. Import compact shipped catalogs from `@astryxdesign/core/locales/*.generated.js`; the shipped "en" catalog is always available and does not need to be listed here.

props.name: overrides
props.description: Sparse per-locale key overrides applied on top of shipped defaults. Overrides are locale-keyed so a runtime locale swap picks up the correct set.

props.name: dir
props.description: Explicit text-direction override for the context. When omitted, direction is derived from `locale` via `Intl.Locale.getTextInfo()`. This sets the direction Astryx reads, but it does NOT set the DOM `dir` attribute; you must set `dir` on `<html>` (or a wrapping element) yourself, since Astryx components mirror layout and directional icons from the DOM `dir`, not from this prop. Set both to the same value and keep them in sync.

props.name: calendar
props.description: Calendar system of the subtree, such as 'persian', 'hebrew', or 'buddhist'. `Calendar`, `DateInput`, `DateRangeInput`, and `DateTimeInput` show it, and Timestamp, PowerSearch, and Lab's Schedule write their dates in it. When omitted, the calendar is Gregorian: a locale never selects it, neither by its default calendar nor by a `-u-ca-` keyword. A component's own `calendar` prop takes precedence. Values stay Gregorian ISO dates. Calendars other than gregory, iso8601, buddhist, roc, and japanese need `Temporal`; the context keeps the requested calendar, and where the runtime lacks `Temporal`, these components show Gregorian dates and warn in development. Load a polyfill such as `temporal-polyfill/full/global` on the server and in the browser.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render with the internationalization provider.

props.name: icon
props.description: Semantic icon name or SVG component. Valid semantic names: close, chevronDown, chevronLeft, chevronRight, chevronsLeft, chevronsRight, check, success, error, warning, info, calendar, clock, externalLink, menu, moreHorizontal, search, upload, arrowUp, arrowDown, arrowsUpDown, funnel, eyeSlash, viewColumns, copy, checkDouble, wrench, stop, microphone. A namespaced key such as `richtext:bold` names a glyph that one component or library registers, and a theme can replace it by key; a namespaced key that nothing registers renders nothing. For any icon not in this list, pass an SVG component directly (e.g. import from lucide-react or @heroicons/react). Note: this prop is called `icon`, not `name`.

props.name: color
props.description: Color variant mapped to Astryx icon color tokens. Semantic values (primary through warning) follow the role, and inherit uses the surrounding text color. On the web, Icon also accepts the palette values blue, red, green, gray, cyan, teal, yellow, orange, pink, and purple, which pick a non-semantic hue.

props.name: size
props.description: Icon size. xsm, sm, md, and lg are 12, 16, 20, and 24px at a 16px root and scale with the root font size; a theme sets a size's glyph dimension with width and height, in px or rem, on components.icon['size:sm'] (and the other sizes). An explicit value wins. When omitted, Icon uses the nearest default supplied by an owning Astryx component for its icon slot, then falls back to md when no contextual default exists.

props.name: variant
props.description: Requests the active theme's alternate artwork for a semantic icon name, such as 'filled'. Names come from IconVariantMap, which an application augments from @astryxdesign/core/Icon; Astryx defines none. The theme's icon entry receives the variant only when the active theme lists it in iconVariants (and, for an entry the theme inherited, the theme that defined the entry lists it too); otherwise it draws its normal artwork. Ignored by an icon component passed directly. Selects artwork only: it is not written to the DOM and has no theming selector.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for a MEANINGFUL, standalone icon (a status glyph or icon-only indicator with no adjacent text). Setting it exposes the icon to screen readers as role="img" with this text as the accessible name (aria-label) and removes the default aria-hidden. Omit it (default) for decorative icons and the icon stays hidden from assistive tech (aria-hidden="true"). This is the accessible-name / alt-text prop for icons: one prop instead of manually setting aria-label + role + aria-hidden. An empty string is treated as decorative. Do not set it when an interactive parent (Button, IconButton, link) already names the control.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for customization (color, size, opacity). Folded into the icon's own stylex.props() call so it composes with the base color/size styles. Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name added to the rendered glyph, beside the astryx-icon target class.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles merged onto the rendered glyph after Icon's own size and color styles.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the rendered SVG element, for an icon component and for a semantic or namespaced name. For a name, it is the <svg> inside the wrapper, or null when the resolved glyph has no <svg>.

usage.description: Icons are small visual symbols that represent actions, objects, or concepts. They improve scannability and reinforce meaning alongside text. Supports both direct SVG components and semantic icon names that adapt to the active theme.

bestPractices.description: Use semantic icon names when available; they adapt to theme changes automatically.
Pair icons with text labels for accessibility; icon-only elements need an accessible label.
Use color tokens for icon colors, not hardcoded hex values.
Be mindful of context; decorative icons in compact components can distract rather than help.
Use icons as the sole means of conveying meaning; always provide a text alternative.
Resize icons with arbitrary pixel values; use the provided size props.
Mix icon styles (e.g. outline and filled) within the same context.
Render raw SVG elements; always wrap in Icon for consistent sizing and color.
Pass a `name` prop; Icon uses `icon` (not `name`) to specify which icon to render.

params.name: name
params.description: Semantic icon name, such as 'success', 'warning' or 'close', or a namespaced extension key such as 'richtext:bold'. Both resolve through the same registry.

returns.name: icon
returns.description: The icon for that name from the nearest Theme's icons (or, outside any Theme, from the registered theme the document root names), else from registerIcons() overrides, else the built-in default. A function entry is read at {size: 'md'}.

usage.description: Resolves a semantic icon name to a React node through the nearest Theme, so a custom component draws the same success, warning or error icon that Astryx components draw and follows a theme that overrides it. Resolution reads the nearest Theme's icons (outside any Theme, the registered theme the document root names), then registerIcons() overrides, then the built-in default. The node is returned as is, with no size or color wrapper: the built-in icons are 1em squares in currentColor, so they follow the surrounding text. A function entry is read at {size: 'md'}. Render <Icon icon={name} /> instead when the icon needs another size, a color or a label.

bestPractices.description: Use it in a custom component that places a semantic icon itself, so a Theme that overrides the icon changes the component too.
Render <Icon icon={name} /> when the icon needs a size other than md, a color, or an accessible label.
Import a specific icon library glyph for a semantic purpose that a theme should control, such as a success or error state.

docs.description: Decorative control visuals: the mark on a chosen option, the box a checkbox draws, the circle a radio draws. Rendered by Selector, CheckboxInput, RadioList, and menu selection rows. Replace one by name through defineTheme({indicators}) and every component drawing it follows.

components.name: CheckboxIndicator
components.description: The checkbox visual: a square box with a checkmark or an indeterminate bar. Decorative (aria-hidden); the owning control keeps the input, role, accessible name, focus, and keyboard behavior.

props.name: state
props.description: Which state to draw. An indicator draws in EVERY state: the unchecked box is an empty box, not nothing.

props.name: size
props.description: Control size: 20px or 24px.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the owning control is disabled. Purely visual; the owner keeps the real disabled semantics.

props.name: children
props.description: Rendered inside the chrome INSTEAD of the state mark when the shallow `isRenderable(children)` check accepts the value. The helper excludes `null`, `undefined`, booleans, and the empty string; React elements and containers take the replacement path even when their descendants render nothing. CheckboxInput passes its loading Spinner through as `children={isBusy && <Spinner/>}`, so replacements should use the same helper rather than a nullish check.

components.name: CheckIndicator
components.description: The mark on a chosen option: a checkmark by default, and nothing at all when unchosen, so a listbox shows no empty box beside every row. This is the indicator to replace to change what "chosen" looks like: mapping it to RadioIndicator gives every single-selection mark radio visuals, including an empty circle on unchosen rows. Unlike the checkbox and radio visuals it renders no chrome of its own (it IS the glyph), so a host's theme target lands on the same element as astryx-icon.

props.description: Which state to draw. The default renders nothing when unchecked; a replacement may draw in both states.

props.name: size
props.description: Control size, matching the other indicators.

props.name: isDisabled

props.name: children
props.description: Rendered INSTEAD of the mark, in every state: a host showing a pending Spinner passes it through whether or not the row is chosen.

components.name: RadioIndicator
components.description: The radio visual: a circle with a filled inner dot when selected. Draws in both states; an unselected radio is an empty circle, which is what lets it stand in for a checkmark in a selection slot.

props.description: Which state to draw. Radio belongs to the singleSelection family, which has no partial state.

usage.description: Indicators are the componentized selection visuals shared by CheckboxInput, RadioList, and menu selection rows. They are decorative: the owning component keeps the input, role, accessible name, focus, and keyboard behavior, while the indicator turns state into a picture. That split is what makes them themeable: restyle one through its class targets, or replace the component outright.

bestPractices.description: Reach for the canonical `components['checkbox-indicator']` override first. Replacing the component is the heavier path, for when the shape itself is wrong.

Match the shipped replacement-content branch with `isRenderable(children)`, not `children != null` or `children ?? mark`. The helper is deliberately shallow: it excludes nullish values, booleans, and the empty string, while React elements and containers take the replacement path even when their descendants render nothing. The owning control passes `children={isBusy && <Spinner/>}`, so a nullish check deletes the state mark whenever that value is `false` (#4893).
A replacement must set aria-hidden. The owning control provides the role and accessible name; a visible indicator would be announced twice.
Use theme tokens for every color, radius, and border width in a replacement. Run `astryx docs tokens` for the set.

Render a single root ELEMENT, and let it keep the border-radius you want the focus ring to follow. A control whose real input is visually hidden cannot show focus on that input, so the owner paints the standard ring onto the indicator element itself at focus time (useIndicatorFocusRing), and `outline` then picks up that element's radius. A replacement needs no cooperation and can forget nothing: the ring is never missing (WCAG 2.4.7), it is only the wrong shape if the root has no radius of its own. Do not draw a focus ring yourself; the owner already did.
Thread hover or pressed state in as props. Interaction state reaches an indicator through the owner's CSS ancestor marker, so hovering the row tints the control with no props involved.

Assume you are only mounted when selected. The host renders its indicator unconditionally and passes `state`, in every state; that is what lets a replacement draw where the default draws nothing (a radio's empty circle on an unchosen row). Drawing nothing in a state is a decision the indicator makes, not one the host makes for it.

usage.description: An info icon that reveals help: a small "i" button. Hover and keyboard focus preview the help, and a click, tap, Enter, or Space pins it open until Escape, a second press, a press outside, or focus leaving. Use it next to labels, values, and metrics for permission notes, metric definitions, and field help. Its value over hand-composing Icon inside Tooltip is the pre-wired accessible trigger: a real button with an aria-label, Tab-reachable, tooltip on hover AND focus AND tap, and Escape dismissal. It follows the toggletip pattern: the button reports `aria-expanded="true"` while the help is pinned, and a screen reader hears the help once when it pins.

bestPractices.description: Keep tooltip content concise, plain, and non-interactive; use Popover or HoverCard for links and buttons.
Override label when "More information" is too generic, e.g. "About this metric".

Rely on InfoTip rather than a hand-rolled info button on touch: it pins its help on a press, so a tap, a click, Enter, or Space pins the tooltip even though the trigger is a button, and a tap outside dismisses it.
Hand-compose Icon inside Tooltip for info affordances; the bare Icon is aria-hidden and unfocusable, so keyboard and screen-reader users never see it.
Use InfoTip for essential information users must see to complete a task; put that text inline instead.

usage.description: InputGroup connects an input with prefix/suffix addons in a single visual unit. Use it for URL fields, currency inputs, search fields with action buttons, or any input that needs contextual decorations.

bestPractices.description: Use text addons to show units, prefixes, or suffixes that clarify the input format (e.g., "$", "kg", "https://").
Use InputGroupText for static prefixes/suffixes like "$", "kg", or "https://".
Use Button for an action attached to the input; InputGroup connects its corners automatically.
Use InputGroup with compatible single-line inputs: TextInput, NumberInput, TimeInput, DateInput, Typeahead, Selector, and MultiSelector.
Keep each inner input's label specific; grouped inputs automatically combine the group label with their own label and inherit the group description/status context.
Don't put multiple text inputs in one group; use separate fields instead.
Don't use InputGroup for unrelated inputs; it's for a single input with decorations.
Don't use InputGroup with TextArea, Slider, Switch, CheckboxInput, or RadioList.

components.name: Item
components.description: A universal item primitive that unifies the "start content + label + description + end content" layout pattern. Use as a building block for list items, menu items, contact rows, notifications, and more.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary text identifying this item. Accepts string (auto-truncated) or ReactNode (for rich content).

props.name: marker
props.description: Marker rendered before startContent as a direct flex child. Use for list bullets/counters that need custom baseline alignment.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Content rendered before the label/description area, such as an icon, avatar, or checkbox.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary text: subtitle, description, or supporting info.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label/description area, such as badges, metadata, timestamps, or action buttons.

props.name: as
props.description: What the root renders as: an HTML element, or a component for a caller that needs the root to be something else. A menu row that navigates passes the application's link component here, so the row's root IS the anchor. Give a component only when the row carries a role, and only when no interactive node sits in startContent or endContent.

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment of start/end content slots. 'center' centers each slot on the whole text block; 'start' lines up slot tops with the text's top; 'first-line' centers each slot on the label's first line, so a small mark stays level with the first line of a wrapped label. A slot taller than that line moves the text down. The `item` theme target reflects the value as `align`.

props.name: density
props.description: Spacing density. "compact" uses 4px block padding, "balanced" uses 8px, and "spacious" uses 12px block and inline padding.

props.name: labelLines
props.description: Max lines before label truncates with ellipsis.

props.name: descriptionLines
props.description: Max lines before description truncates with ellipsis.

props.name: layout
props.description: How the label and description sit together. stacked puts the description on its own line below the label; inline keeps both on one line, description ellipsizing first, so the row fits a fixed-height host.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler. Makes the item clickable with button semantics.

props.name: interactiveRef
props.description: Ref to a nested control (e.g. a checkbox in startContent) that owns the item's keyboard access and action. The row becomes an enlarged click/tap target that delegates surface clicks to it (useClickableContainer) and renders no invisible button/anchor, so the row adds no second tab stop (WCAG 4.1.2). Mutually exclusive with onClick/href; those are ignored when set.

props.name: href
props.description: Link URL. Makes the item a link via an invisible anchor element. A row whose root is already a link component (see `as`) carries the address on that root instead, and no invisible anchor is rendered.

props.name: target
props.description: Link target. Only used with href. target="_blank" automatically adds noopener noreferrer.

props.name: rel
props.description: Link relationship tokens. noopener noreferrer are merged automatically for target="_blank".

props.name: isHighlighted
props.description: Highlighted state (hover/keyboard focus appearance).

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Selected state.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disabled state.

props.name: swipeActions
props.description: Swipe actions for touch: the verbs a sideways drag uncovers on each side, outermost last, each `{id?, label, icon?, onActivate, isDisabled?, variant?: 'neutral' | 'accent' | 'destructive', hasRemoval?}`. `leading` is uncovered by a drag toward the inline end, `trailing` toward the inline start. A mouse never starts the drag and a mostly vertical drag stays the scroller's. The gesture is a touch accelerator and never a row's only path to a verb: a verb reachable only by swipe is unreachable by keyboard and by mouse, so every entry must also be reachable through the row's own content. Served on a row whose role permits interactive descendants (a listitem, a row with no role) and not on an option, a menu item, or a row that is the enlarged target of a native radio. The element containing the rows clips in the inline axis with overflow-inline: clip — List does; any other host does it once. `hasRemoval` only says the row holds out after the action fires instead of springing back. The gesture and its panels are loaded on demand the first time a row has swipe actions, so a row without them ships none of it.

props.name: swipeBehavior
props.description: What a swipe does. `reveal` rests the row open with every entry a real button and fires the outermost on a long drag or a fling; `commit` slides the row out and fires the outermost on release, with nothing resting and a presentational panel. `commit` fits one entry per side.

usage.description: A single, flexible item primitive that unifies the "start content + label + description + end content" pattern across Astryx. Use it wherever you need a structured row: dropdown menus, selectors, contact lists, notifications, file browsers, and activity feeds.

bestPractices.description: Use named slots (startContent, label, description, endContent) for the common layout. These cover the 80% case.
Use density="compact" for menus and dense lists, "balanced" for standard rows, and "spacious" for roomier layouts.
Set labelLines and descriptionLines to control truncation when content length varies.

Use align="first-line" when a wrapping label sits beside a small mark (a status dot, a radio, a timestamp) that belongs to its first line. Use align="start" to line up the tops of a tall slot and the text.
Give a swipe action a second home in the row (a menu or a button in endContent): the swipe is a touch accelerator, and a verb reachable only by swipe is unreachable by keyboard and by mouse.
Don't nest interactive elements (buttons, links) inside an interactive Item; it creates confusing focus and click targets.
Don't use Item for navigation between views; use proper navigation components instead.
Don't add read/unread or inbox-specific behavior directly; compose a thin wrapper like PreviewItem instead.

usage.description: Layer utilities provide the app-level provider used by overlay systems. Use LayerProvider at the app root for toast/layer configuration; use higher-level Popover, HoverCard, or Tooltip APIs for most overlay UI. Rendered layer content, not the provider’s application subtree, uses theme body text defaults and exits ancestor surface/group membership. Establish intentional groups and complete required providers inside each layer. Every anchored layer keeps a gutter from each viewport edge — the spacing-4 step or the device safe-area inset, whichever is larger — and is capped to the viewport, never to the room beside its trigger: an explicit width renders at its size, flips when it does not fit beside the trigger, and slides into view when it fits on neither side. An app that floats a persistent bar over a viewport edge declares it once as inset on LayerProvider (blockStart, blockEnd, inlineStart, inlineEnd); each edge adds to that edge’s gutter for every anchored layer and moves the toast viewport by the same amount, and defaults to zero. The inset is app configuration, not a theme value.

bestPractices.description: Declare a persistent bar floating over the viewport once, as inset on LayerProvider; every anchored layer and toast then stays clear of it.
Use LayerProvider once near the app root when you need shared toast/layer configuration.
Build on higher-level components like Popover, HoverCard, and Tooltip for common overlay patterns.
Nest a LayerProvider to change toast settings: a nested provider keeps the outer toast configuration and mounts no second toast viewport.

returns.name: render
returns.description: Render function for the popover element. Pass placement/alignment in context mode or x/y in fixed mode. Placement/alignment are logical: they map to the self-* position-area keyword family, which resolves against the popover's own inherited direction, so RTL contexts mirror automatically in pure CSS. Pass `positioning: "custom"` in context mode to author position styles yourself via `style` (e.g. explicit anchor() insets or an anchor-size() cover): the hook keeps the popover behavior and position-anchor wiring but derives no position styles, including the automatic RTL mirroring, which becomes your responsibility. Pass `offset` (a CSS length; a number is px) in context mode for clearance from the anchor: it applies to both edges of the placement axis, so the gap survives a flip. Layers are flush by default. Context mode first renders an inert `<template>` marker in matching server and client markup. The final layer stays at that JSX position if its parent is safe; otherwise it is portaled to the nearest ancestor outside paragraphs, links, buttons, inline formatting, and structurally restricted containers. The nearest safe host keeps CSS custom properties inheriting live, while the layer preserves direction and writing mode from its JSX position. By default this resolution occurs after hydration so closed-layer DOM remains available, and it re-renders only the slot that holds the marker and the layer, not the component that called the hook (which renders again only when a resolved mount is replaced by a render call that moved to another host); `lazyMount` defers it until `show()` and unmounts the content again on hide while the marker remains. The Popover API promotes the layer to the top layer when shown, so it escapes ancestor clipping and stacking wherever it is hosted. When the layer would overflow the viewport, position-try fallbacks flip it to the opposite side; centered layers additionally slide along the alignment axis (span fallbacks) so they stay on-screen near viewport edges.

usage.description: Core positioning hook for rendering overlay content using CSS Anchor Positioning and the Popover API. Use it as the foundation for custom popovers, hover cards, tooltips, and fixed-position layers when higher-level components are not enough. Both modes use theme body text defaults and end ancestor surface/group membership as a whole, including group-owned state. Explicit props and unrelated contexts remain unchanged. Apply intentional formatting through render styles or content, and establish complete content-local providers inside the rendered layer.

bestPractices.description: Use context mode for anchor-positioned overlays relative to a trigger element, and fixed mode for manually positioned overlays at specific coordinates.
Build on higher-level components like Popover, HoverCard, and Tooltip for common overlay patterns.

Rely on the Popover API top layer to escape ancestor clipping and stacking, and host the layer near its trigger rather than in the body so it inherits the trigger's theme cascade and keeps a natural focus order.
Implement ARIA patterns directly in a Layer unless you also own the full accessibility behavior.

Both modes use theme body defaults and end ancestor surface/group membership as a whole. RTL mirroring, which becomes yours). `offset` (context mode) = clearance from the anchor as a CSS length (number = px), applied to both edges of the placement axis so it survives a flip; layers are flush by default. Context mode begins with an inert `<template>` marker for stable SSR/hydration, then keeps the final layer inline at a safe JSX position or portals it to the nearest safe ancestor; CSS custom properties keep inheriting from that host while direction and writing mode are preserved from the JSX position. `lazyMount` waits for show and unmounts content on hide while the marker remains. The Popover API top layer escapes clipping/stacking wherever it is hosted. Viewport overflow: flips to opposite side; centered layers also slide along the alignment axis (span fallbacks).

usage.description: Core positioning hook for overlay content via CSS Anchor Positioning + Popover API. Foundation for custom popovers, hover cards, tooltips, fixed-position layers. Both modes use theme body defaults and end ancestor surface/group membership as a whole. Explicit props and unrelated contexts remain unchanged; establish intentional groups and complete required providers inside the rendered layer.

bestPractices.description: Use context mode for trigger-anchored overlays; fixed mode for explicit coordinates.
Build on Popover/HoverCard/Tooltip for common overlay patterns.
Rely on the Popover API top layer to escape clipping/stacking; host the layer near its trigger (not in the body) to inherit the trigger theme cascade and natural focus order.
Implement ARIA directly in Layer unless you own full accessibility behavior.

docs.description: General five-slot layout primitive for arranging header, start, content, end, and footer regions.

props.name: content
props.description: Content slot (center). Accepts any ReactNode; use LayoutContent when a content region is needed. Children passed to `<Layout>` render here too: `<Layout>{main}</Layout>` is shorthand for `<Layout content={main} />`.

props.name: header
props.description: Header slot. Accepts any ReactNode; use LayoutHeader when a header region is needed.

props.name: footer
props.description: Footer slot. Accepts any ReactNode; use LayoutFooter when a footer region is needed.

props.name: start
props.description: Logical-start slot (left in LTR). Accepts any ReactNode; use LayoutPanel when a panel region is needed.

props.name: end
props.description: Logical-end slot (right in LTR). Accepts any ReactNode; use LayoutPanel when a panel region is needed.

props.name: height
props.description: Height behavior: fill the container's height or grow with content. Fill needs a container with a set height, such as AppShell's content area; under an app root with no height, the layout grows with its content.

props.name: contentWidth
props.description: Maximum width of the aligned content within each slot (header, content, footer, panels), centered when narrower than the available space. Without panels, LayoutContent spans the available width so its scrollbar stays at the outer edge while its children align internally to contentWidth. With exactly one panel, the panel stays aligned to the contentWidth frame while LayoutContent extends to the opposite open edge. With both panels, contentWidth includes the complete middle composition. Percentage widths—including percentage-bearing calc(), min(), max(), and clamp() values—and intrinsic widths, plus bare var(...) values, retain the constrained composition; use calc(var(...)) for a variable guaranteed to resolve to a length. Dividers stay full-bleed. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is (e.g. `60ch`). Common page widths: 640 for forms, settings, and text-focused pages; 960 for content pages and wider layouts.

props.name: padding
props.description: Padding at the layout's outer edges using the spacing scale. Applies to this Layout's own header, footer, panels, and content. A nested Layout does not inherit it: without `padding`, its regions use the enclosing Card, Section, or Dialog padding, or the default inset (spacing 4). That keeps a page Layout inside AppShell inset even though AppShell's own regions are full bleed.

props.name: children
props.description: Shorthand for the content slot: `<Layout>{main}</Layout>` is the same as `<Layout content={main} />`. When both are given, `content` wins.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root layout element.

props.name: defaultHasDividers
props.description: Default divider visibility for LayoutHeader and LayoutFooter children. Headers and footers that don't pass `hasDivider` use this value; when unset, nested layouts inherit from their parent context.

usage.description: Layout is a general five-slot primitive for arranging header, start, content, end, and footer regions within a page or bounded container. AppShell owns the page shell and app-wide navigation behavior; use HStack or VStack for simple directional stacking.

bestPractices.description: Use Layout when content needs named header, start, content, end, or footer regions.
Use HStack and VStack for simple directional stacking within a content area.
Hide a region by passing `false`, `null`, or `undefined` to its slot, for example `isOpen && <LayoutPanel />`. The slot counts as empty, so the neighbouring regions move out to the layout edge.
Give a region a landmark role and label on the region component when it is a page landmark, for example `<LayoutPanel role="navigation" label="Sections">`. Layout adds no role or name.
Use Layout for simple stacking layouts; use HStack or VStack instead.
Use Layout as the page shell or for app-wide navigation; use AppShell for that responsibility.

props.description: Width of the panel. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is. Ignored when resizable is provided; the hook controls width. Beside a ResizeHandle given a useResizable region's props, a panel at width={region.size} is inert while the region is collapsed, and focus inside it moves to the handle as it collapses.

props.name: resizable
props.description: The output of useResizable(), or its props. When provided, the hook drives the panel width and a ResizeHandle should be placed adjacent to the panel. Carries the region's axis ('horizontal' | 'vertical'), which must match the adjacent ResizeHandle's direction. With the hook's own value, the panel slides closed and open from the edge facing its ResizeHandle; a hand-built object does not slide. Either way, focus inside the panel moves to its ResizeHandle as it collapses, and the panel is inert while collapsed.

vars.name: --_hit-border-bottom
vars.description: Width of the divider below a divided row, 0 on the last row. The row's touch hit layer adds it to its offset, so its band starts past the divider. ListItem sets it on the row's own ::after from --border-width under hasDividers, so content inside the row never inherits it, and a theme changes the divider through that token.

docs.description: List container with density, dividers, and header support.

props.name: children
props.description: List items (ListItem components).

props.name: density
props.description: Spacing density for items. Under a finger, an interactive row's hit target reaches 44px where its neighbors leave room, with no change to how rows look or lay out.

props.name: hasDividers
props.description: Show dividers between items.

props.name: animatedLayout
props.description: The handle from useAnimatedLayout({containerRef}). With it, when rows are inserted, removed or reordered, an inserted row enters, a removed row collapses in place, a row that crosses rows moving the other way rides above them with the surface color behind it, and the rows after a change and the content after the list, up to that container, glide to their new places, all on one shared motion, under every pointer. Under Reduce Motion nothing travels. A row is identified by its itemKey: a row without one changes at once. Without a handle the list changes at once.

props.name: reorderable
props.description: Makes the rows reorderable, with the object createReorderable({onReorder, isReorderable}) makes: each ListItem with an itemKey gets a reorder handle at its end, and each committed move calls onReorder once with the row's key and its index after the move ({key, to}); render the rows in the new order to apply it. A row the object's isReorderable rejects has no handle and keeps its place; one at either end of the list also bounds the others. The object may be made on every render. On a touch screen, a finger held still on a handle for a moment picks up its row (a flick on it still scrolls): the row stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other rows stay still, the page scrolls near the edges, and on release the rows rearrange, gliding to their new places. A mouse drags a handle at once with the same copy and line, and the rows take their places without motion; a drag reports once, at the drop, and a cancelled drag puts everything back at once. In reorder mode the line marks the row's new place after each move. Without a drag, the handle is a toggle: a click, Space or Enter turns on reorder mode for its row (aria-pressed), in which each Up or Down arrow moves the row a place at once and reports it, and Escape or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves. Each move is announced once it renders, with the row's place and its neighbours ('Milk, position 3 of 5, after Eggs, before Bread'), and a move into a row that keeps its place is refused and announced. While the mode is on, a hint anchored to the handle shows the moves and Done as buttons that do what the keys do, so a row can also be reordered by taps alone. The object's start(key) enters the same mode from your own UI, such as a row's context menu. A disabled row's handle stays focusable but moves nothing.

props.name: edge
props.description: Where each row's text, dividers, and hover and selection backgrounds sit, relative to the list's edges and the container around it. 'padded' keeps text inside each row's padding, so it starts a little in from a heading above the list and backgrounds have room around it. 'flush' drops the rows' side padding: text starts on the heading's line, and dividers and backgrounds stop at the row's content, with no room beyond it on either side. It works anywhere and suits static rows. 'outset' puts text on the heading's line and reaches dividers and backgrounds a little past it into the container's padding; it suits interactive rows in a container. 'bleed' puts text on the heading's line and reaches dividers and backgrounds to the container's edges, like Table rows in a Card. Rows are square, except that when the list is the first or last child of a rounded Card or Dialog that holds no other Table or bleeding List deeper inside, its first row (when it has no header) or last row takes the container's corner, less the container padding above or below it. A row's first content is what lines up with the heading: its marker, icon, or avatar when it has one, otherwise its label. 'outset' and 'bleed' reach into the padding of the nearest container that shares its padding: a Card, Section, Dialog, or BottomSheet, or a transparent container such as a Layout region with explicit padding or a padded ScrollableArea. Place the List directly in that container's padding: padding that Stack, Center, or your own styles add in between is not counted. Drawers and the automatic padding of LayoutContent and LayoutPanel aren't supported yet. With no such container, including in a Popover, they look like 'padded'. In a container with less padding than the rows' own, text starts a little after the heading's line. A theme's inline padding on `item` replaces the row padding of every value, including the zero padding of flush.

props.name: edgeCompensation
props.description: Deprecated: use edge="outset", which this sets. Still works; edge wins when both are set. `astryx upgrade` rewrites existing usage.

bestPractices.description: Provide a header to label the list and give context to screen readers.
Use start and end content slots to add icons, avatars, or badges to each item.
Set edge to line row text up with a heading above the list: flush for static rows, outset or bleed for rows in a Card, Section, or Dialog.

To line text up with a heading and keep room around the highlight where there is no Card, such as a sidebar, put the heading and the list in a Section with variant="transparent" and set edge="outset".
