params.name: onReorder
params.description: Called once per committed move (a drop, or each move in reorder mode) with the moved item's key and its index after the move, in the full order of the collection's items. Apply it by rendering the items in their new order. A cancelled move calls nothing. The latest function given is the one called, so the object may be made on every render.

params.name: isReorderable
params.description: Whether the item with this key can move. An item it rejects shows no handle and cannot be picked up; one at either end of the collection also bounds the others, so nothing drops beyond it and a keyboard move into it is refused. Every item moves without it.

returns.name: reorderable
returns.description: The collection's reorder behavior: pass it as `List`'s `reorderable` prop, with an `itemKey` on each `ListItem`. Make it once per collection (with useMemo); one made on every render still works. Its one method, `start(key)`, enters reorder mode for that item from your own UI (a Move item in its context menu, a toolbar button): the focus moves to its handle, as activating it does; a key that cannot move or is not mounted does nothing and warns in development. One object may serve several collections, each reordering on its own; `start` then uses the one mounted last.

usage.description: Makes a collection's rows reorderable. On a touch screen a finger held still on a row's handle for a moment picks it up (a flick on the handle still scrolls): the row stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other rows stay still, the page scrolls near its edges, and on release the rows rearrange. A pen held still on a handle where the primary pointer is coarse picks the row up as a finger does. A mouse, or a pen where the primary pointer is fine, drags a handle at once the same way, and the rows take their places without motion; a cancelled drag puts everything back at once. Without a drag, the handle toggles reorder mode for its row (a click, Space or Enter): each arrow key moves the row a place at once, and Escape or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves; screen readers hear each move with the row's place and neighbours, and a hint shows the moves and Done as buttons, for taps alone. The reorder code ships with this function: a collection without the prop loads none of it.

bestPractices.description: Give each row a stable key from your data, a string or a number (`itemKey={item.id}`), and apply each move by rendering the items in their new order in the same task.
Use `isReorderable` for rows that must stay put, such as a pinned first row.
Offer reorder mode from your own UI too, such as a row's context menu, with `reorderable.start(item.id)`.
Use React's `key` as the reorder key, or index-based keys: a move changes every index after it.

docsDense.description: A collection's reorder behavior, for List's reorderable prop; ListItem itemKey on each row.

paramDescriptions.onReorder: ({key, to}) once per committed move; to is the index after the move.
paramDescriptions.isReorderable: (key) => boolean; a rejected row has no handle, and at an end bounds the drop.

returnDescriptions.reorderable: pass as List's reorderable prop; start(key) enters reorder mode from your own UI.

usage.description: UIKit edit-mode reorder: hold then drag (finger; pen on a coarse primary pointer), drag at once (mouse; pen on a fine one); without a drag, the handle toggles reorder mode (click, Space, Enter), arrows move, Escape ends.

bestPractices.description: Stable data keys as itemKey; apply the move at once.
React's key or indexes as reorder keys.

usage.description: Hook-based resizable panel system. useResizable() manages size state and ResizeHandle provides the interactive pill-grip separator. Pass the hook's output to existing layout components via their resizable prop.

bestPractices.description: Use percent(value, {min: pixel(value)}) or percent(value, {max: pixel(value)}) when a percentage needs exactly one pixel floor or ceiling. Reuse Table’s pixel() helper; numbers, exact Npx, and pixel(value) remain pixels. State, persistence, callbacks, paint, and ARIA remain resolved pixels.
Use useResizable() with existing Astryx layout components. Pass its output to the resizable prop on LayoutPanel, ResizeHandle or SideNav; any other element can use its size.
Provide an accessible label on each ResizeHandle when multiple handles exist (e.g. "Resize sidebar", "Resize terminal").
Wrap panels in extra container components for resize. The hook-first architecture avoids extra DOM; use it directly on existing components.

params.name: defaultSize
params.description: Initial size. Numbers, exact "Npx", and pixel(value) are pixels. Exact "N%" has no additional pixel bound. percent(value, {min: pixel(value)}) or percent(value, {max: pixel(value)}) adds one pixel floor or ceiling. A percentage resolves ONCE into pixels — against containerRef when supplied, against the viewport otherwise — and does not track its basis afterwards. The released broad number | string type remains compatible; runtime validation is authoritative.

params.name: minSize
params.description: Minimum size. Numbers, exact "Npx", and pixel(value) remain pixels; exact "N%" has no additional pixel bound; percent(value, {min: pixel(value)}) or percent(value, {max: pixel(value)}) adds exactly one. Percentage minimums re-resolve when their basis changes and clamp the current pixel selection.

params.name: maxSize
params.description: Maximum size. Numbers, exact "Npx", and pixel(value) remain pixels; exact "N%" has no additional pixel bound; percent(value, {min: pixel(value)}) or percent(value, {max: pixel(value)}) adds exactly one. Percentage maximums re-resolve when their basis changes and clamp the current pixel selection.

params.name: containerRef
params.description: The element a percentage is a share of. Caller-owned: the hook never infers one. Omitted, percentages use the viewport, which is the released behaviour. The ref may point at a different element over time — the basis follows it. Until that element is actually laid out (not yet mounted, display:none, detached) percentages use a temporary 1200px basis rather than its zero measurement, and nothing is persisted from it.

params.name: direction
params.description: Which axis this region resizes along. Selects the container's inline or block content-box size as the percentage basis, and must match the direction given to ResizeHandle.

params.description: Whether a lift or a key step below the collapsed threshold collapses the region to zero.

params.name: snaps
params.description: Pixel values to snap to during drag.

params.name: autoSaveId
params.description: Key for localStorage persistence of size and collapse state across sessions.

params.name: defaultIsCollapsed

params.name: isCollapsed
params.description: Controlled collapse state. collapse(), expand(), a lift or a key step past the threshold, and a drag that reopens the region then report through onCollapseChange instead of changing state internally.

params.name: onCollapseChange
params.description: Called once per collapse state change: a lift or a key step that closes the region, a drag or a key that reopens it, Enter, a double-click, or a call to collapse(), expand() or resize().

usage.description: Hook for adding drag-to-resize behavior to layout regions. Supports single-region and multi-region configurations with snap points, collapsible panels, localStorage persistence, and cascade resize ordering.

bestPractices.description: Use percent(40, {min: pixel(333)}) for a 40% size with a 333px floor, or percent(10, {max: pixel(400)}) for a 10% size with a 400px ceiling. The options argument is required and carries a floor XOR a ceiling.
A structured default is an initial choice only; a structured minSize or maxSize remains live. State, persistence, callbacks, resize(), paint, and ARIA all use resolved pixel numbers.

Import percent and Table’s same pixel binding from @astryxdesign/core/Resizable/utils when constructing configuration in a Server Component; the root package exposes one pixel symbol and one percent symbol without collision.
Use with Layout or AppShell sidebar for resizable navigation panels.
Set autoSaveId to persist user-chosen sizes across page reloads.
Set minSize too small; content becomes unreadable. Prefer collapsible for panels that can hide entirely.

usage.description: Adds drag-to-resize behavior to layout regions. Supports single-/multi-region configs w/ snap points, collapsible panels, localStorage persistence, cascade resize ordering.

Set autoSaveId to persist user-chosen sizes across page reloads.

usage.description: Provides a native scroll viewport and a real observed content box. The viewport enters the tab order only while a requested logical axis is effectively scrollable, and containment applies only to effective axes.

bestPractices.description: Give every area a concise label that identifies the content keyboard users will scroll.

Leave `role` unset (it renders `group`) for ordinary scroll containers. Choose `role="region"` only when the area is significant enough to appear in screen-reader landmark navigation; every `region` adds an entry to that list.
Choose `inline`, `block`, or `both` from content intent; the component maps the logical axes through writing mode and direction.
Keep the default `overscroll="allow"` for nested areas unless the interaction deliberately needs containment.

Use `useScrollableArea` instead when a component already owns both a viewport and a suitable content box, or when children must remain direct flex/grid items or retain a definite percentage block-size basis.

ScrollableArea owns one normal block content box with a 100% minimum size. Inline and both-axis modes use max-content inline sizing, so intrinsic inline layout is intentionally wider than the viewport.
Use logical padding props on the content box so nested full-bleed components receive the same inset geometry.
Set `isFullBleed` only when the viewport itself should reach an ancestor container edge; it is off by default.
Set `stickyContainment="always"` only when a fitting viewport should intentionally remain a Sticky boundary.
Hide the native scrollbar without another visible and operable overflow affordance.
Add another overflow wrapper around ScrollableArea; one native viewport should own scrolling.

usage.description: Section is the correct way to create page regions and group related content on a page. Use it for settings groups, form sections, sidebar areas, or any time you need visual separation between parts of a page. If you are tempted to use a Card for a page section, use Section instead.

bestPractices.description: Use Section for page-level grouping: settings panels, form groups, sidebar regions. These are sections of a page, not discrete items.
Start with the default variant. Use muted only to call attention to a specific region.
Add dividers between same-background sections that need separation.
Combine with a heading + Stack for a typical page section pattern.
Use Card when you mean Section. Cards are for discrete items (one notification, one profile). Sections are for page regions.

To center a Section, set marginInlineStart and marginInlineEnd to 'auto' in xstyle. If Astryx source is compiled in your app's own StyleX pass, the marginInline shorthand loses to Section's own inline margins.

usage.description: A segmented button group that allows users to make a single selection from a small set of mutually exclusive options. Use SegmentedControl when all options should be visible at once and the selection controls a value or mode, not page navigation. Under a finger, on a touch device (a coarse primary pointer), the selection slides to the new segment, whether a tap, an arrow key or a new value moved it; with Reduce Motion nothing travels: the old selection fades out as the new one fades in. There, dragging the selected segment carries the selection along with the selected label’s colour following it, and the segment under the finger is chosen when it lets go (letting go outside the control selects nothing); a tap selects through the browser’s click; a pressed segment shows the shared pressed overlay, and nothing lifts or dims. With a mouse or a pen every change, a click included, slides on the theme’s duration and easing, and dragging the selected segment carries it as a finger does.

accessibility.name: Text label
accessibility.description: Each label must have at least 4.5:1 contrast with its segment background. Check unselected, Hover, Pointer down, and selected colors as they appear on screen. For Hover and Pointer down, measure the final background after the overlay is applied.

accessibility.name: Essential icon
accessibility.description: When a segment has no visible label, its icon must have at least 3:1 contrast with the segment background. An icon beside a visible label does not need its own check.

accessibility.name: Selected state indicator
accessibility.description: The selected background must reach 3:1 only when users need it to tell selected from unselected. Label color and weight also show selection.

accessibility.name: Visible control boundary
accessibility.description: The control edge or segment borders need at least 3:1 contrast when users need them to see the choices.

accessibility.name: Keyboard focus indicator
accessibility.description: The focus outline must have at least 3:1 contrast with the area around the segment. Check it on the track and selected background.

accessibility.name: Disabled appearance
accessibility.description: Disabled controls do not need to meet these contrast ratios.

bestPractices.description: Use for switching between 2–5 mutually exclusive views or modes where all options should be visible.
Provide a descriptive label for the control to ensure the group is accessible to screen readers.
Use for page-level navigation; use TabList instead. TabList is a navigation component, while SegmentedControl is an input that always has exactly one selected option.
Use for simple on/off states; use ToggleButton instead. ToggleButton can be toggled on or off independently, while SegmentedControl enforces a single selection from a group.
Wrap a disabled SegmentedControl in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; the reason is then not attached to the control or its segments. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.description: Whether to show a search input for filtering options. As the user types, the match count (or "No results found") is announced to screen readers via a polite live region. The selection surface, clear action, and disclosure indicator are removed. Unlike isDisabled, the control is not dimmed. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set.

props.description: Explains why the selector is disabled. props.description: Custom render function for each selectable option in the dropdown. Use this instead of JSX children; dividers and sections are rendered by the selector.

props.name: renderValue
props.description: Custom render function for the selected option inside the closed trigger. A one-line value follows the active size token, including compact or wide spacing scales with icons or a clear control. Padding accommodates the trigger line box, and each extra line grows the control by one line (28/32/36 for one line and 48/52/56 for two with the default tokens). Content inherits the trigger line height; content that sets a larger font should set its own line height so the trigger grows to fit it. Inside an InputGroup the group owns the row height: a SelectorOption folds onto one line and ellipsizes, and any taller node is cut off at the row.

props.name: indicatorPosition
props.description: Which logical edge of the option row carries a rendered selection mark. An empty mark consumes no space, so selected and unselected labels may shift or have different available width. end is the house convention shared with Typeahead and CommandPalette.

props.name: presentation
props.description: How the option list is presented. adaptive uses a bottom sheet on compact touch screens and an anchored popover otherwise.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned. Without a width the field follows its displayed value and can shrink with its row (the value truncates) instead of overflowing it; use `<HStack wrap="wrap">` for filter bars so selectors move to a second line on phones.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon displayed at the start of the selector trigger.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a loading spinner in the trigger.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler on the trigger button. Runs before the selector toggles its surface; preventDefault() does not keep it closed.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Focus handler on the trigger button. Runs before the selector's own focus handling.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Key handler on the trigger button. Runs after the built-in keyboard model and is skipped for keys it handles and cancels.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds the value, icons, and end controls. Never the trigger button itself.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

usage.description: A dropdown selector for choosing a single value from a list of options. Supports labels, validation, descriptions, and required/optional states. Use it in forms and settings when presenting a moderate number of options. Keyboard typeahead matches a native select: typing on the focused closed trigger selects the matching option directly, repeated presses cycle through options sharing a first letter, and spaces count as match characters ("new y" reaches "New York"). With the menu open, typing moves the highlight and Enter commits. With hasSearch, typing on the closed trigger opens the popup and seeds the search input.

bestPractices.description: Provide a visible label so users understand what they are selecting.
Use sections and dividers to organize options when the list exceeds ~8 items.
Use renderOption for custom option rows. Do not pass SelectorOption directly as JSX children.
Set a meaningful placeholder that hints at the expected selection (e.g. "Choose a country" not "Select...").
Use inside InputGroup only when the selector needs a short prefix or suffix addon as part of one decorated input surface.

Use variant="secondary" when a selector sits in a nav or toolbar beside secondary buttons or a segmented control, so it shares their treatment instead of reading as a form field. Use variant="ghost" when a selector sits in a toolbar with ghost buttons. If validation status is needed there, prefer statusVariant="tooltip" so the toolbar height stays compact.
Use presentation="adaptive" when the selector should become a bottom sheet on compact touch screens.
Use for action menus; use Dropdown Menu for triggering commands or navigation.
Use when there are only two options; use a SegmentedControl or radio buttons instead.
Use Selector for navigation; links should be links, not dropdown options.
Use for yes/no or on/off choices; use Switch or CheckboxInput instead.
Put more than ~20 options without sections; consider Typeahead for large lists.
Wrap a disabled Selector in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the trigger itself.

docs.description: Helper component for custom item rendering inside an Selector renderOption prop.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text for the item.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon displayed before the label. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: layout
props.description: How the label and description sit together. 'stacked' puts the description on its own line; 'inline' keeps both on one line so the row fits a fixed-height host. Inside a Selector trigger the trigger's padding sizes itself to whichever layout you pick, so both land on the 4px rhythm; an InputGroup pins the row height and forces 'inline'.

docsZh.description: 用于在 Selector 的 renderOption 渲染函数中自定义选项渲染的辅助组件。

props.name: label
props.description: 选项的主标签文本。

params.name: options
params.description: Configuration object.

params.name: options.selectableItems
params.description: The options in the same order as they render: `SelectorOptionData`, or any option type with a string `value` and an optional `disabled`. Options with `disabled` cannot be picked and are skipped while moving through the open list; ArrowDown or ArrowUp that opens the list from `onKeyDown` lands on the selected option when it is enabled, else on the first or last enabled option.

params.name: options.isOpen
params.description: Whether the list is shown. The caller owns this state.

params.name: options.onOpen
params.description: Called to show the list. Return `false` to refuse; the hook then leaves the highlight alone.

params.name: options.onClose
params.description: Called when the hook hides the list; the hook resets the highlight first. When the caller closes the list itself (an outside press, say), it should also call `setHighlightedIndex(-1)`.

params.name: options.listboxId
params.description: The listbox element's id. Option ids are derived from it through `getItemId`.

params.name: options.value
params.description: The selected value. Opening the list highlights it when it is enabled; otherwise ArrowUp opens on the last enabled option and ArrowDown, a press, Enter or Space on the first. A disabled option is never highlighted on opening, and with no enabled option nothing is.

params.name: options.onSelect
params.description: Called with the picked value. Picking also closes the list.

params.name: options.onClear
params.description: Clears the value. When provided, Delete or Backspace on the closed control clears it, so clearing is not pointer-only. Ignored while the list is open or with `hasSearch`.

params.name: options.hasSearch
params.description: Whether the list has its own search field. Space then types instead of picking, opening by a press or Enter does not pre-highlight (ArrowDown and ArrowUp still open on the selected or the first or last enabled option), and printable keys on the closed control go to `onSearchSeed`.

params.name: options.onSearchSeed
params.description: With `hasSearch`, receives each printable character except Space typed while the control has focus, opening the list first when it is closed, so type-to-find needs no separate open step.

params.name: options.isDisabled
params.description: Whether the control ignores clicks and keys.

returns.name: highlightedIndex
returns.description: Index of the active option, or -1 when none is active. With `hasSearch`, opening by a press or Enter does not set one, so it stays -1 after the hook itself closes the list; ArrowDown and ArrowUp still open on the selected or the first or last enabled option. Render it as the active option and name it in `aria-activedescendant` only while it points at a rendered option.

returns.name: setHighlightedIndex
returns.description: Sets the active option, for example from a filter that changes the options.

returns.name: getItemId
returns.description: The id to render on the option at `index`. Set the control's `aria-activedescendant` to `isOpen && highlightedIndex >= 0 && highlightedIndex < selectableItems.length ? getItemId(highlightedIndex) : undefined`, so it never names an option that does not exist, including in an empty list.

returns.name: onTriggerClick
returns.description: Toggles the list from a press on the control.

returns.name: onKeyDown
returns.description: Key handler for the control that keeps focus. ArrowDown and ArrowUp open the list or move the active option; Enter (and Space without search) picks it or opens the list; Escape and Tab close it; Home, End, PageUp and PageDown jump to the first or last option. An editable control that keeps Home and End for the caret does not pass them to this handler, as CommandPalette does.

returns.name: onItemSelect
returns.description: Picks an option from a press on it, then closes the list.

returns.name: onItemMouseEnter
returns.description: Makes the hovered option active without scrolling the list or moving focus.

returns.name: getFieldProps
returns.description: Props for a single-line `input` you render: `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-controls` only while the listbox renders (`isOpen` with at least one option), `aria-activedescendant` only while an option is active, and the field’s key handler. Pass your own `onKeyDown` here rather than beside the spread: it runs after the hook’s handler unless that handler claimed the key, and it may be typed for its element.

returns.name: getListboxProps
returns.description: Props for the listbox you render, anywhere in the document, including the page’s flow: its `id` and `role`, and a press handler that keeps focus in the field. Render it while `isOpen` and there are options, and name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

returns.name: getOptionProps
returns.description: Props for the option at `index`: its `id`, `role`, `aria-selected` (true on the active option), `aria-disabled` on a disabled one, a pointer move that makes it active without moving focus, and a press that picks it.

usage.description: Tracks the active option of a single-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers Selector and CommandPalette; use it to build a combobox those components do not cover, including one over a single-line text field you render yourself, such as a search field whose results replace a page section, or an “add people” field in a dialog. It renders nothing: you render the field, the listbox and the options, and spread `getFieldProps`, `getListboxProps` and `getOptionProps` onto them, or wire `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` yourself from `onKeyDown` and `getItemId` for a control such as a button.

bestPractices.description: Render each option with `id={getItemId(index)}` and set the control's `aria-activedescendant` only while `isOpen` and `highlightedIndex` points at a rendered option, as CommandPalette does.
For type-to-select without a search field, run useTypeahead's handler first and fall through to this `onKeyDown` when it returns false, as Selector does.
For a field you render, spread the prop getters, and set the active option yourself when a new query changes the options: the first option so Enter picks it, or -1 so Enter stays the field’s.
Announce the number of results through useAnnounce when the options change for a new query (AST-075 DEC-2). When nothing matches, announce the words the field shows for it.
Render controls that are not options, such as a create button or an empty message, inside the listbox; render them beside it.
Move DOM focus onto the options; the active option is announced through `aria-activedescendant` while focus stays on the control.

accessibility.name: Focus stays in the field
accessibility.description: With the prop getters, moving the active option never moves focus out of the field. The field names the active option through `aria-activedescendant` and carries none while no option is active.

accessibility.name: Expanded state follows the list
accessibility.description: While the listbox renders, the field exposes `aria-expanded="true"` and `aria-controls` naming it. Otherwise it exposes `aria-expanded="false"` and references nothing.

accessibility.name: Roles
accessibility.description: The field is a `combobox` with `aria-autocomplete="list"`. The list is a `listbox` of `option`s with `aria-selected="true"` on the active one. You name the field and the listbox.

accessibility.name: Keys
accessibility.description: While the list shows, ArrowDown and ArrowUp move the active option and wrap; Enter picks an active option and only then stops the field’s own Enter; Escape, whatever modifier is held, hides the list without closing an enclosing dialog or popover on the same press. While it is hidden, ArrowDown shows it when there are options. An open field with no options still takes Escape, which closes the list, so render an empty message while it is open. Home, End, other chords such as Shift+Enter, and every other key reach the field.

accessibility.name: Input method
accessibility.description: No key moves, picks or hides while an input method is composing text.

accessibility.name: Pointer
accessibility.description: Moving the pointer over an option makes it active without moving focus; pressing an option picks it, and the field keeps focus through the press.

accessibility.name: Result count
accessibility.description: Yours to announce: compose useAnnounce (AST-075 DEC-2) so each new query announces the number of options, or that there are none, once and politely. For none, announce the words the field shows.

docsDense.description: Single-select combobox state + keys; focus stays on control. Powers Selector / CommandPalette, and comboboxes over a single-line field you render (search whose results replace a section, an add-people field). props.type: {isCollapsed: boolean, onCollapsedChange: (isCollapsed: boolean) => void, defaultIsCollapsed?: boolean, hasButton?: boolean, buttonLabel?: string}
props.description: The same controlled collapsible config passed to SideNav, with all its keys. Only needed when the button is rendered outside the sidenav, where collapse context cannot reach it.

props.type: boolean | { defaultIsCollapsed?: boolean; isCollapsed?: boolean; onCollapsedChange?: (isCollapsed: boolean) => void; hasButton?: boolean; buttonLabel?: string }
props.description: Enables collapse behavior. true for uncontrolled with default toggle button, or an object for controlled mode and advanced config (defaultIsCollapsed, isCollapsed + onCollapsedChange, hasButton, buttonLabel). A controlled config can also be passed to a SideNavCollapseButton rendered outside this SideNav, so both share one state.

props.name: resizable
props.type: boolean | { defaultWidth?: number; minWidth?: number; maxWidth?: number; autoSaveId?: string; onWidthChange?: (width: number) => void; defaultIsCollapsed?: boolean; isCollapsed?: boolean; onCollapseChange?: (isCollapsed: boolean) => void } | ResizableRegion
props.description: Enables a resize handle at the inline-end edge. true for defaults (260px initial, 180-480px range), or a ResizableConfig object (defaultWidth, minWidth, maxWidth, autoSaveId for localStorage persistence of width and collapse state, onWidthChange). It can also own collapse state (defaultIsCollapsed, isCollapsed + onCollapseChange); when both props carry collapse state, resizable wins and a dev warning names the conflicting keys. It also takes the output of useResizable(), whose axis ('horizontal' | 'vertical') must be 'horizontal': that region then owns the width and the collapse state, so the rail follows its isCollapsed, the toggle calls its collapse and expand, and its autoSaveId saves the width. With the hook's output, the region's own collapsible option also decides whether the rail collapses; a collapsible prop that disagrees, or the collapse state it sets, is ignored, with a dev warning. The handle is hidden while collapsed.

usage.description: A sidebar navigation component for organizing application pages with sections, nested items, and icons. Use SideNav as the primary navigation when an app has 5 or more destinations or requires hierarchical grouping.

bestPractices.description: Use sections to group related navigation items and help users scan for their destination.
Pair outline and filled icon variants so the selected state is visually distinct.
Mark the current page with isSelected: it sets aria-current="page", so the current destination is announced rather than carried by color alone.

SideNav renders a navigation landmark, and a collapsible item follows the WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/): the toggle carries aria-expanded and aria-controls, and the group it owns is inert while collapsed. Keep item labels short; they name icon-only items unless a meaningful aria-label supplies more context.

While the nav is collapsed, an item with children shows them in a submenu flyout. On a device that can hover, pointing at the item opens it after a short delay and moving away closes it; a flyout opened by clicking stays open until it is dismissed. On touch, it opens on tap. Do not put an action in there that has no other route to it.
Include a SideNavHeading when a TopNav is already providing app identity; this duplicates branding.
Use for filtering content; use tabs or filter buttons instead.

usage.description: A draggable control for selecting a numeric value or range within defined bounds. Supports single value and range selection, tick marks, custom value formatting, and vertical orientation. Use it when users need to explore a continuous range, such as volume, price, or percentage. Under a finger, on any touch device, it tracks as UISlider does: only the thumb takes a drag, through a target larger than it, the value follows the finger’s travel rather than jumping to it, a release coasts on before `onChangeEnd`, a swipe from the track scrolls the page, and a tap on the track or a mark sets the value when the finger lifts (the thumb springs there). A mouse drag on a thumb tracks the same way, past the same 10 px in any direction, with no lift or coast; a mouse press on the track moves the thumb there, and only a primary click presses. A pen drags as a finger does, claiming only along the track, and its drag ends at the release with no coast. A wheel or a trackpad scroll over the slider goes to whatever scrolls under it.

bestPractices.description: Always provide a label, even if visually hidden, so the slider is accessible to screen readers.
Format values with meaningful units like "$50" or "75%" instead of raw numbers.
Use for precise numeric entry; pair with a text input or use NumberInput instead.
Set a step size so large that only a few positions are possible; use SegmentedControl or radio buttons instead.
Wrap a disabled slider in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

anatomy.description: Background rail representing the available numeric range.

anatomy.name: Filled range
anatomy.description: Accent segment from the minimum to a single value, or between two range values.

anatomy.name: Tick mark
anatomy.description: Position marker supplied through the marks collection.

anatomy.name: Mark label
anatomy.description: Optional text displayed beside a tick mark.

anatomy.name: Thumb
anatomy.description: Draggable value indicator; range mode renders a minimum and maximum thumb.

anatomy.description: Formatted current value shown beside the slider when valueDisplay is text.

usage.description: A draggable control for selecting a numeric value or range within defined bounds. Supports single value and range selection, tick marks, custom value formatting, and vertical orientation. Use it when users need to explore a continuous range, such as volume, price, or percentage. Under a finger, on any touch device, it tracks as UISlider does: only the thumb takes a drag, through a target larger than it, the value follows the finger’s travel rather than jumping to it, a release coasts on before `onChangeEnd`, a swipe from the track scrolls the page, and a tap on the track or a mark sets the value when the finger lifts (the thumb springs there). A mouse drag on a thumb tracks the same way, past the same 10 px in any direction, with no lift or coast; a mouse press on the track moves the thumb there, and only a primary click presses. A pen drags as a finger does, claiming only along the track, and its drag ends at the release with no coast. A wheel or a trackpad scroll over the slider goes to whatever scrolls under it.

bestPractices.description: Always provide a label, even if visually hidden, so the slider is accessible to screen readers.
Format values with meaningful units like "$50" or "75%" instead of raw numbers.
Use for precise numeric entry; pair with a text input or use NumberInput instead.
Set a step size so large that only a few positions are possible; use SegmentedControl or radio buttons instead.
Wrap a disabled slider in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

propDescriptions.containerXstyle: StyleX styles for the field container; no effect in InputGroup or horizontal-labels FormLayout. No root xstyle/className/style.
propDescriptions.containerClassName: Class name for the field container.
propDescriptions.containerStyle: Inline styles for the field container.
propDescriptions.controlXstyle: StyleX styles for the visual control box (border, background, icons); not the native input.
propDescriptions.controlClassName: Class name for the visual control box.
propDescriptions.controlStyle: Inline styles for the visual control box.
propDescriptions.label: Label text (always rendered for a11y).
propDescriptions.value: Current value; number for single thumb, [number, number] for range.
propDescriptions.onChange: Fired on value change during drag.
propDescriptions.formatValue: Custom value formatting fn for display + aria-valuetext.
propDescriptions.marks: Tick marks at specified positions w/ optional labels. Unfilled marks use the track color; filled marks use the accent color.
propDescriptions.minStepsBetweenThumbs: Min steps between thumbs in range mode; prevents overlap.
propDescriptions.htmlName: HTML name attr; hidden inputs carry the value (two in range mode).
propDescriptions.isLabelHidden: Visually hide label.
propDescriptions.status: Status indicator ({type, message}) for validation feedback.
propDescriptions.labelTooltip: Tooltip text for info icon next to label.

props.description: 标签文本（始终渲染以确保无障碍可访问性）。

props.name: value
props.description: 当前值——`number` 用于单滑块模式，`[number, number]` 用于范围模式。

props.name: onChange
props.description: 拖拽过程中值变更时触发的回调。

props.name: onChangeEnd
props.description: 拖拽结束时触发的回调。

props.name: min
props.description: 最小值。

props.name: max
props.description: 最大值。

props.name: step
props.description: 步进增量。

props.name: orientation
props.description: 滑块的方向。

props.name: formatValue
props.description: 自定义值格式化函数，用于显示和 `aria-valuetext`。

props.name: valueDisplay
props.description: 当前值的显示方式。

props.name: marks
props.description: 在指定位置的刻度标记，带可选标签。未填充区域的标记使用轨道颜色；填充区域内的标记使用强调色。

props.name: minStepsBetweenThumbs
props.description: 范围模式下滑块之间的最小步数；防止滑块重叠。

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: 是否禁用滑块。

props.name: htmlName
props.description: 用于表单提交的 HTML name 属性。渲染携带当前值的隐藏输入（范围模式下为两个条目）。

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the slider is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the thumb focusable via aria-disabled (value changes stay blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Slider in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: 字段是否为可选。

props.name: isRequired
props.description: 字段是否为必填。

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: 是否在视觉上隐藏标签。

props.name: description
props.description: 标签下方渲染的描述文本。

props.name: status
props.description: 验证反馈的状态指示器对象（`{ type, message }`）。

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: 标签旁信息图标的提示文本。

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: 字段容器（标签、控件和状态整体）的 StyleX 样式。在 InputGroup 内（请改为设置 InputGroup 的样式）或 `horizontal-labels` FormLayout 中无效。不接受根级 `xstyle`、`className` 和 `style`。

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: 字段容器的类名，作用目标同 `containerXstyle`。

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: 字段容器的内联样式，作用目标同 `containerXstyle`。

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: 可视控件框的 StyleX 样式：绘制边框和背景并包含图标与尾部控件的元素，而非原生输入元素。

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: 可视控件框的类名。

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: 可视控件框的内联样式。

params.name: options
params.description: What one flick moves. 'view' moves one view and lands on the item start edge nearest one viewport on; 'item' moves one item. A new value applies from the next flick.

returns.name: paging
returns.description: Snap paging for Carousel's hasSnap. The value is the same for the component's life, and Carousel keeps the value it first attached.

usage.description: Gives a Carousel iOS paging on native snap's stops: pass the value as hasSnap={useSnapPaging()}. Under a finger and on a trackpad swipe, a flick moves one view, or one item with {pages: 'item'}, and the row rests on an item's start edge. A mouse wheel keeps native snapping. Only a carousel given the value loads the paging code.

bestPractices.description: Use it for a row read one view at a time, such as onboarding screens or a photo strip, where a fast flick must not skip past the next view.
Pass {pages: 'item'} when several items show at once and each flick should move only one of them.
Use it for a row people scan quickly; plain hasSnap keeps native momentum, which can pass several items in one swipe.

docsDense.description: iOS paging for Carousel on native snap's stops: hasSnap={useSnapPaging()}. Finger or trackpad swipe: one view per flick ({pages: 'item'}: one item); mouse wheel keeps native snap. Only that carousel loads the pager.

paramDescriptions.options: {pages: 'view' | 'item'}: what one flick moves. Default 'view'. A new value applies from the next flick.

returnDescriptions.paging: value for Carousel's hasSnap; same for the component's life; Carousel keeps the first value it attached.

usage.description: hasSnap={useSnapPaging()}: one view per flick under a finger or trackpad swipe, resting on an item start edge. {pages: 'item'}: one item. Mouse wheel stays native.

bestPractices.description: Use for rows read one view at a time (onboarding, photo strip).
{pages: 'item'} when several items show and a flick should move one.
Use for rows scanned quickly; plain hasSnap keeps native momentum.

props.name: size
props.description: Spinner size: ring diameter (10px, 14px, 18px, 28px).

props.name: shade
props.description: Color shade for light or dark backgrounds.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible content below the spinner. A string label names the indicator through aria-labelledby.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name for screen readers. Defaults to label (if string) or a translated "Loading" from the i18n catalog.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

vars.name: --spinner-diameter
vars.description: Diameter of the drawn ring. Set it on a size-variant target to retheme what each named size resolves to, e.g. spinner: { 'size:xl': { '--spinner-diameter': '2.5rem' } }. The rendered box is this plus the stroke width on each side, and follows automatically. Any length works: rem, em and calc() are resolved before the ring is drawn.

vars.name: --spinner-stroke-width
vars.description: Stroke width of both circles the ring is drawn from: the moving arc and the track behind it. Set it per size alongside the diameter. One stroke width drives both, so 0 is honoured as a zero-width stroke and paints nothing at all rather than falling back to the default; for an arc with no track behind it, set --spinner-track-color to transparent instead.

vars.name: --spinner-color
vars.description: Color of the moving arc. Defaults to the shade's token, so set it on a shade-variant target to retheme one shade (spinner: { 'shade:subtle': { '--spinner-color': 'var(--color-text-tertiary)' } }), or on the base target to retheme all four. Accepts any color notation, including var(), color-mix() and currentColor.

vars.name: --spinner-track-color
vars.description: Color of the track the arc travels on. Set it to `transparent` for an arc with no track. The onMedia and inherit shades draw the track at reduced alpha (30%) so it reads against an arbitrary backdrop; that fade applies to a themed color too.

vars.name: --spinner-arc-fraction
vars.description: Fraction of the ring the moving arc covers, as a plain number (not a percentage or angle). Set it on a size-variant target the same way as --spinner-diameter, e.g. spinner: { 'size:xl': { '--spinner-arc-fraction': '0.75' } } for a 270deg sweep. Only takes effect once the stylesheet loads; a render with no CSS (SSR, no-JS) always draws the default 135deg arc.

usage.description: An animated loading indicator for processes with unknown duration, such as data fetching or form submission. Supports visible labels, multiple sizes, and a dark background variant. For content with known dimensions, use Skeleton instead.

bestPractices.description: Provide a meaningful label to describe what is loading for screen reader users.
Use the "onMedia" shade when placed on dark or accent-colored backgrounds.
Use for content areas with known dimensions; use Skeleton to preserve layout instead.
Stack multiple spinners in the same view; use one to represent the overall loading state.

props.name: size
props.description: 旋转器尺寸——环直径（10px、14px、18px、28px）。

props.name: shade
props.description: 浅色或深色背景的颜色色调。

props.name: label
props.description: 旋转器下方的可见内容。未设置 aria-label 时，字符串标签提供无障碍名称。

props.name: aria-label
props.description: 屏幕阅读器的无障碍名称。默认为 label（如果是字符串）或来自 i18n 词条的已翻译 "Loading"。

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX 样式，用于布局自定义（边距、定位、尺寸）。必须是 stylex.create() 的值，而非内联样式对象如 style={{}}。

vars.name: --spinner-diameter
vars.description: 绘制环的直径。在尺寸变体目标上设置，以重新定义每个命名尺寸的解析值，例如 spinner: { 'size:xl': { '--spinner-diameter': '2.5rem' } }。渲染盒子的尺寸为该值加上两侧的描边宽度，并自动跟随。支持任意长度单位——rem、em 与 calc() 会在绘制前解析。

vars.name: --spinner-stroke-width
vars.description: 绘制环的两个圆——移动圆弧与其后的轨道——的描边宽度。与直径一起按尺寸设置。同一个描边宽度同时驱动两者，因此 0 会被采纳为零宽描边——什么都不绘制，而不会回退到默认值；若想要没有轨道的圆弧，请改将 --spinner-track-color 设为 transparent。

vars.name: --spinner-color
vars.description: 运动圆弧的颜色。默认取所在 shade 的令牌，因此可在 shade 变体目标上设置以重新定义单个 shade——spinner: { 'shade:subtle': { '--spinner-color': 'var(--color-text-tertiary)' } }——或在 base 目标上设置以覆盖全部四种。接受任意颜色写法，包括 var()、color-mix() 与 currentColor。

vars.name: --spinner-track-color
vars.description: 圆弧所在轨道的颜色。设为 `transparent` 可得到无轨道的圆弧。onMedia 与 inherit 两种 shade 会以降低的透明度（30%）绘制轨道，以便在任意背景上可辨；该淡化同样作用于主题化的颜色。

vars.name: --spinner-arc-fraction
vars.description: 运动圆弧覆盖圆环的比例，为纯数字（非百分比或角度）。在尺寸变体目标上设置，方式与 --spinner-diameter 相同，例如 spinner: { 'size:xl': { '--spinner-arc-fraction': '0.75' } } 可得到 270 度的圆弧。仅在样式表加载后生效；无 CSS 的渲染（SSR、无 JS）始终绘制默认的 135 度圆弧。

components.name: Stack
components.description: Unified stack layout component with a direction prop. Use direction="horizontal" to flow along the inline axis (left to right in LTR, right to left in RTL) or direction="vertical" (default) for top-to-bottom. For convenience, HStack and VStack are pre-configured wrappers.

props.name: direction
props.description: Direction of the stack layout. 'horizontal' flows items along the inline axis, left to right in LTR and right to left in RTL (like HStack), 'vertical' flows top-to-bottom (like VStack). Note: the value is 'horizontal', NOT 'row'.

props.name: gap
props.description: Spacing step (number literal): 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10. Pass as a JSX number expression e.g. gap={4}, NOT a string like gap="4".

props.name: padding
props.description: Inner padding on all sides, using the spacing scale. Pass as a JSX number expression e.g. padding={3}.

props.name: paddingInline
props.description: Inline (horizontal) padding. Overrides padding on the inline axis when both are set.

props.name: paddingInlineStart
props.description: Inline-start padding, using the spacing scale (left in LTR, right in RTL). Overrides paddingInline and padding on that edge only.

props.name: paddingInlineEnd
props.description: Inline-end padding, using the spacing scale (right in LTR, left in RTL). Overrides paddingInline and padding on that edge only.

props.name: paddingBlock
props.description: Block (vertical) padding. Overrides padding on the block axis when both are set.

props.name: paddingBlockStart
props.description: Block-start (top) padding, using the spacing scale. Overrides paddingBlock and padding on that edge only.

props.name: paddingBlockEnd
props.description: Block-end (bottom) padding, using the spacing scale. Overrides paddingBlock and padding on that edge only.

props.name: isScrollable
props.description: Enables scrollable overflow (overflow: auto).

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the stack container. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is (e.g., '100%').

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the stack container. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is (e.g., '100%').

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum width of the stack container.

props.name: minHeight
props.description: Minimum height of the stack container.

props.name: hAlign
props.description: Horizontal alignment. When direction='horizontal': main-axis (justify-content). When direction='vertical': cross-axis (align-items).

props.name: vAlign
props.description: Vertical alignment. When direction='horizontal': cross-axis (align-items). When direction='vertical': main-axis (justify-content).

props.name: justify
props.description: Main-axis alignment alias. Resolves to hAlign (horizontal) or vAlign (vertical). Note: use 'between', NOT 'space-between'.

props.name: align
props.description: Cross-axis alignment alias. Mirrors CSS align-items.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Flex wrap behavior.

props.name: as
props.description: HTML element to render as the stack container.

props.name: children
props.description: Stack content.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name added to the stack element, after the component styles.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the stack element. width, height, maxWidth, and minHeight win over the same properties here.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the rendered stack element.

bestPractices.description: Use StatusDot as a binary present/absent signal; avoid encoding many distinct states in a single dot, since color and size alone cannot reliably distinguish them.
Always pair with a visible text label so status is not conveyed by color alone.
Provide a descriptive `label` prop for screen reader accessibility.
Pair the dot with an icon that carries the status as a distinct shape when it must stand on its own without adjacent text, so meaning survives without color.

docs.name: Step
docs.description: Individual step within a Stepper. Renders a progress-bar segment, an indicator, and a label with optional description. Progress (completed/active/not-started) is derived from the parent Stepper's activeStep and this step's step index.

props.name: step
props.description: Zero-based index of this step. Used to derive progress (completed/active/not-started) relative to the parent activeStep.

props.name: label
props.description: Step label text. Kept to a single line and ellipsized when the step is narrower than the label, so a row of horizontal steps stays the same height and the track under them stays straight. The full string is still read out as part of the step, so a truncated label costs nothing in the accessible name — but short labels survive narrow layouts better.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional description shown below the label for additional context.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered below the label and description. Useful in vertical steppers for form fields or detailed step content. In a compact horizontal Stepper, the content remains mounted to preserve local state while it is hidden with the expanded step details.

props.name: status
props.description: Semantic color for the step. Controls color only and maps to the global Astryx semantic tokens. Leave unset for the progress-derived default coloring.

props.name: indicator
props.description: What to show as the step indicator. 'auto' shows a number until completed then a check, 'number' always shows a numbered badge, 'none' hides it, or pass any ReactNode (e.g. an Icon) for a fully custom indicator.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables interaction and dims the step indicator and label.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Marks the step as optional, appending an "Optional" affordance after the label.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Trailing content rendered at the end of the label row.

props.name: density
props.description: Controls vertical padding of the step. Falls back to the stepper-level density when unset.

usage.description: Steppers display progress through a sequence of logical and numbered steps. Use them for multi-step workflows like forms, onboarding flows, or checkout processes where users need to see their position and the steps ahead. Rendered as an ordered list (not a navigation landmark).

bestPractices.description: Keep step labels short and descriptive: "Payment" not "Enter your payment information".

Use the vertical orientation when steps carry longer descriptions. A horizontal stepper handles narrow containers itself: once the frame gives each step less than horizontalOptions.minimumStepWidth (112px by default) it drops the labels for a segmented track and uses the configured collapsedVariant beneath it.

Set horizontalOptions.collapsedVariant to 'withLabel' when the page already supplies Back/Continue, or to 'hiddenLabel' when surrounding UI owns both the current-step heading and navigation and only a bare progress track is needed.
Provide onStepClick for non-linear workflows where users may need to revisit earlier steps.
Use status only to apply a semantic color (accent/success/warning/error); pass a custom icon for richer indicators.
Use a stepper for fewer than 3 steps; a simple heading or progress bar works better.
Use more than 7 steps; consider grouping related steps or using a different pattern.

anatomy.name: Frame
anatomy.description: The layout frame that groups the ordered steps with the optional compact summary shown at narrow widths.

anatomy.name: Compact summary
anatomy.description: The optional row a horizontal Stepper adds directly beneath the track once it is too narrow to label every step. horizontalOptions.collapsedVariant chooses a label with Previous/Next controls, the label alone, or no row for a bare progress track. The on-track layout keeps its indicators on the rail instead of repeating the active indicator beside the label. Every step keeps its name in the accessible sequence at any width.

anatomy.name: Step
anatomy.description: One step in the flow, and the element carrying its status. Wraps the indicator, label, description, and the track segments belonging to it.

anatomy.name: Progress bar
anatomy.description: A 4px segmented bar per step. Filled for completed and active steps. Advancing one step grows the fill along the track it just covered, so the movement reads as progress rather than a bar changing color. Every other change applies at once: going back, jumping forward by more than one step, mounting mid-flow, and any change at all under prefers-reduced-motion. Where a span is drawn by more than one segment (the on-track layouts split it between two steps, three when a content slot sits between them), the segments run in track order at one constant speed, so the fill reads as a single line growing rather than pieces lighting in turn.

anatomy.name: Connector
anatomy.description: The track drawn between indicators in the on-track layouts. Each connector paints an unfilled line and, over it, the accent fill covering the progress made. How many pieces a connector is drawn from is an implementation detail of the layout, not a themeable part; use --step-connector-gap to hold the track off the indicator.

anatomy.name: Indicator

vars.description: Gap a connector leaves where it meets the indicator, spent on the side facing it. Applies to the on-track layouts, whose connector is drawn as one segment either side of the node; 0 leaves the track running unbroken through it.

usage.description: A toggle control for on/off states that take effect immediately. Supports labels, descriptions, loading states, and validation. Use it for settings or preferences that apply instantly. For changes requiring a form submission, use a checkbox instead. Under a finger it moves like the iOS switch on every touch screen: a press lifts the thumb, a drag across flips it, lifting the finger commits, and a tap toggles through the browser’s click. The thumb keeps its circle and size on every device, and under a coarse pointer the invisible hit area grows toward 44 × 44 px, stopping halfway to any neighbouring control so a tap goes to the nearer one. With reduced motion on, a change cross-fades on a touch screen and is immediate with a mouse.

bestPractices.description: Use for settings that apply immediately; the toggle should take effect without a separate save action.
Pair with a clear, concise label that describes the setting being controlled.
Use for options that require a form submission to take effect; use a checkbox instead.
Use a switch for multi-state values; it's strictly on/off.
Wrap a disabled switch in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

With isMultiSortEnabled, Shift+click adds tiebreaker columns. For data sorted on a server, use useTableSortable directly and sort where the data lives.

docs.description: Styled, data-driven table with density, dividers, hover highlight, striped rows, and named plugin support. T must extend Record<string, unknown>.

props.name: data
props.description: Array of data items to render as rows. T must extend Record<string, unknown> (use `interface MyRow extends Record<string, unknown>` for custom types).

props.name: columns
props.description: Column definitions: each column has {key, header, width?, align?, renderCell?}. The `header` field sets the column heading text. If omitted, columns are auto-generated from data object keys. The `width` field is typed as `ColumnWidth` (not a number); use `proportional(n)` or `pixel(n)` helpers imported from `@astryxdesign/core/Table`. Omitting `width` keeps an equal flexible share with a compact 60px readability floor. To give one column a different floor, set `width: proportional(1, {minWidth: 80})`; its `minWidth` replaces the 60px floor for that column. Example: `width: pixel(120)` for 120px fixed, `width: proportional(1)` for a flexible column with a 120px default minimum.

props.name: idKey
props.description: Canonical row identity: a property name projects valid strings and finite numbers to strings; a function retains string/number type. Optional legacy tables fall back to index. Virtualization requires explicit unique valid keys.

props.name: density
props.description: Row density controlling cell padding and font size.

props.name: dividers
props.description: Divider style rendered between cells.

props.name: isStriped
props.description: Applies a background wash to even-numbered rows.

props.name: hasHover
props.description: Applies a hover highlight background to rows on pointer devices.

props.name: verticalAlign
props.description: Vertical alignment for body row cells. Controls `vertical-align` on the `<td>` elements.

props.name: textOverflow
props.description: How body cell text behaves when it exceeds the column width. 'wrap' lets text wrap and the row grow taller; 'truncate' clips with an ellipsis (default-rendered cells show a tooltip on hover when truncated). Header cells always truncate.

props.name: virtualization
props.description: Geometry-only capability from useTableRowsVirtualization({rowHeight, viewportHeight}), both positive finite CSS pixels. Pass complete flat data and an explicit idKey. Default text truncates; custom renderers, wrapping, structural plugins, incompatible offsets, invalid identity or unrepresentable geometry use full rendering. Logical row positions include the header.

props.name: plugins
props.description: Named plugins that extend table behavior via the transform pipeline. Converted to an ordered array internally.

props.name: rowIndexStart
props.description: ARIA row index (1-based) for the first rendered body row. The row ordinal is an accessibility concern independent of any visible index column, so setting this (or rowCount) makes the table emit aria-rowindex on body rows and aria-rowcount on the table. For a paginated/windowed view, pass the offset of the first visible row (e.g. (page - 1) * pageSize + 1) so aria-rowindex reflects position in the full dataset. Data-driven mode only.

props.name: rowCount
props.description: Total number of body rows across all pages/windows, used for aria-rowcount so assistive tech can announce "row X of Y" against the full dataset. When omitted but rowIndexStart is set (windowed view with an unknown total), aria-rowcount is set to -1 per the ARIA unknown-count convention. Data-driven mode only.

props.name: children
props.description: Children mode: compose the table yourself from TableHeader / TableBody / TableFooter, each holding TableRow and TableCell, instead of using data-driven rendering. The children are passed straight to the <table>, so the section is yours to supply. A TableRow placed directly in Table emits <table><tr>, which is invalid HTML and mismatches on hydration (the parser inserts an implied <tbody> for server-rendered markup; React does not on the client). Data-driven mode renders the sections for you.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

usage.description: Table displays structured data in rows and columns with consistent dimensionality. It supports rich cell content, sorting, selection, pagination, and column management through a composable plugin system. Use Table for data sets with uniform structure; for simpler or inconsistent data, consider a list or card layout instead.

bestPractices.description: Use density and divider variants to match the information density and scanning needs of your data.
Compose rich cell content with Astryx components like Badge, StatusDot, and Avatar via renderCell.

In children mode, put every row inside TableHeader, TableBody, or TableFooter. <table> cannot contain a <tr> directly: the HTML parser inserts an implied <tbody> for server-rendered markup and React does not on the client, so unwrapped rows mismatch on hydration.

Omit width for equal flexible columns with a compact 60px readability floor. Give one column its own floor with proportional(1, {minWidth}), weight columns with proportional(n), and fix widths with pixel(); the Table scroll region activates when the combined floors no longer fit.

Use the data-driven API from React Server Components: proportional(), pixel(), and column definitions without function props are server-safe. Columns using renderCell (or any function prop) need the table wrapped in a "use client" component, since functions cannot cross the server-client boundary.
Use a table for data without consistent columns. Use a list or card layout for heterogeneous content.
Enable every plugin at once. Add only the features your use case requires to keep the interface focused.
Rely on the 60px omitted-width floor when a text-heavy column needs more room; set proportional(1, {minWidth}) on that column instead.

usage.description: Table displays structured data in rows and columns with consistent dimensionality. It supports rich cell content, sorting, selection, pagination, and column management through a composable plugin system. Use Table for data sets with uniform structure; for simpler or inconsistent data, consider a list or card layout instead.

bestPractices.description: Use density and divider variants to match the information density and scanning needs of your data.
Compose rich cell content with Astryx components like Badge, StatusDot, and Avatar via renderCell.
Use a table for data without consistent columns. Use a list or card layout for heterogeneous content.
Enable every plugin at once. Add only the features your use case requires to keep the interface focused.

docs.name: useTableGroupedRows
docs.description: Hook that groups a flat data array into collapsible section rows. Each distinct groupBy value becomes a full-width section-header row with a chevron toggle, the group label, and a member count; collapsing hides that group's data rows while keeping the header visible. The disclosure state lives on the chevron button, not the native table row. Mirrors useTableTreeState: the consumer owns the collapsedGroups set and the hook returns {data, plugin, idKey}: pass them to Table as data, plugins, and idKey respectively. Grouping runs on the rows you hand it, so with pagination the order is filter, sort, slice, then group: sort by the group key first and the user's keys second, so a section's rows stay contiguous and each page appends to the bottom of the table instead of splicing rows in above the reader. A page that ends on a row count still cuts mid-section, and the heading then counts what has loaded rather than what exists: "6" quietly becoming "10". Where the full result set is in hand, carry the cut forward to the end of the section it lands in: every rendered section is then whole and its count is a total.

Returns {data, plugin, idKey}: pass them to Table data / plugins / idKey. Consumer owns the collapsedGroups set. Under pagination the order is filter, sort, slice, group: sort by the group key first so sections stay contiguous and pages append at the bottom. A row-count cut lands mid-section and the heading counts the page, not the section; where the whole result set is in hand, carry the cut to the end of the section it lands in so every rendered section is complete.

docs.name: useTableRowExpansion
docs.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which expands a full-width detail panel below a row, rendered by the consumer via renderExpanded(item). Adds a leading chevron column and a right-click "Expand/Collapse row" action; the consumer owns the expandedKeys set. The panel spans the row but starts its content at the first column, past the chevron, so detail lines up with the labels above it; the inset follows the table density. Use it for master-detail rows (order details, forms, charts, nested tables). For hierarchical data where child rows reuse the parent columns, use useTableTreeData + useTableTreeState instead.

props.description: Set of currently-expanded row keys. Consumer-owned.

props.name: onToggle
props.description: Called with a row key when its expansion is toggled (chevron click or context-menu action).

props.name: getRowKey
props.description: Derive a stable unique key from a row item.

props.name: getRowLabel
props.description: Derive a human-readable row identity for the chevron accessible name. Astryx combines it with localized expand/collapse wording. Omit it, or return blank text, to keep the generic "Expand row" and "Collapse row" labels.

props.name: renderExpanded
props.description: Render the detail content shown in a full-width panel below the row when it is expanded. Receives the row item.

props.name: getIsItemExpandable
props.description: Control which rows are expandable. Non-expandable rows show no chevron, no context-menu action, and never render a panel. Defaults to all rows expandable.

props.name: panelVariant
props.description: Background behind the detail panel. 'transparent' (default) paints nothing: the panel is the row's continuation and takes whatever surface the table sits on, so a Card shows through and a striped table's zebra reads on unchanged. 'muted' washes it, marking it as commentary rather than another row of data — reach for it in a bare table with no card, dividers or striping, where nothing else makes that distinction. The wash is a low-alpha near-black, so it is close to invisible over a dark card: 'muted' is largely a light-theme effect.

props.name: hasRowClickExpansion
props.description: Toggle a row by clicking anywhere on it, not only on its chevron. A pointer-only convenience layered over the chevron, which stays the accessible control for keyboard and assistive tech. Clicks on interactive cell content (buttons, links, form controls) or on a text selection do not toggle, and non-expandable rows stay inert.

props.name: animatedLayout
props.description: A handle from useAnimatedLayout. With it, opening or closing a panel glides the rows after it (and the content after the table) to their new places instead of jumping, the opening panel plays in on the same motion, and each row's divider moves with it. Under Reduce Motion the rows fade in place on a touch screen and change at once with a mouse; in a table with column lines (dividers columns or grid, which do not move yet) they change at once. Without it, rows jump.

docs.name: useTableRowStatus
docs.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which prepends a narrow column signaling per-row status. Return {status, label} for a semantic success, warning, or error: Table resolves the matching glyph and tone through the active theme. Return {color, icon?, label} for a custom marker: every color is paint-only, an omitted icon renders the stable 8px dot, and an explicit icon renders that caller-selected glyph. Named custom icons keep their released Icon color mapping; raw CSS custom icons inherit the caller's exact paint instead of the previous primary fallback. Existing callers require no source migration. label is required and becomes the accessible image name plus supplemental hover tooltip; return null for no indicator. The column header is visually blank but carries a screen-reader-only localized name ("Row status", i18n key @astryx.table.rowStatus.columnHeader). Memoize getStatus with useCallback for a stable plugin identity.

props.name: getStatus
props.type: (item: T) => ({ status: 'success' | 'warning' | 'error'; color?: never; icon?: never; label: string } | { status?: never; color: 'accent' | 'success' | 'error' | 'warning' | 'red' | 'orange' | 'green' | 'yellow' | 'blue' | 'gray' | string; icon?: IconName; label: string }) | null
props.description: Derive either a semantic outcome or a custom marker. {status, label} accepts the closed success/error/warning vocabulary and resolves its glyph and tone through the active theme. {color, icon?, label} preserves the stable custom-marker path: color always selects paint, no icon renders an 8px dot, and icon renders the explicit caller glyph. Even color values named success/error/warning remain dots without icon. Valid icon names: close, chevronDown, chevronLeft, chevronRight, chevronsLeft, chevronsRight, check, success, error, warning, info, calendar, clock, externalLink, menu, moreHorizontal, search, upload, arrowUp, arrowDown, arrowsUpDown, funnel, eyeSlash, viewColumns, copy, checkDouble, wrench, stop, microphone. The branches are exclusive, label is required and announced via role="img", and null leaves the row status cell empty. Memoize with useCallback for a stable plugin identity.

docsDense.description: Returns a TablePlugin with a narrow per-row status column. {status,label} resolves themed success/error/warning glyph + tone. Stable {color,icon?,label} stays custom: color is paint-only, no icon = 8px dot, icon = caller glyph. label is required; null leaves the cell empty. Memoize getStatus.

docs.description: Headless tree plugin for Table: renders nested rows with per-level indentation and expand/collapse chevrons in the tree column (the first column by default), and reflects hierarchy with aria-level on body rows and aria-expanded on each expand/collapse button. Composable with the other Table plugins: the canonical plugin order places tree before selection, so the checkbox column lands left of the indented tree column. Feed it the treeConfig from useTableTreeState, or construct the config directly for server-driven or pre-flattened trees. Known limitation: the tree column wraps its cell content, so textOverflow="truncate" tooltips do not apply within the tree column.

props.name: isFullBleed
props.description: Makes the tab strip escape its parent's container padding, extending to the container's content edges (cancels the nearest padded Layout container's --container-padding-* custom properties with negative margins). The inner strip pads back by the portion of the container inset that is not already supplied by the first or last tab stop, keeping edge labels aligned while a hasDivider underline spans the full content width. Matches Divider's isFullBleed: inline (start/end) edges only; block-edge docking stays with the surrounding layout.

props.description: ARIA role for the strip. 'tablist' asks for the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: role="tablist" / role="tab" and aria-selected, with each tab pointing at the panel it controls via its panelId; only tabs may live in a tablist strip, and an href on a tab is ignored there. Left unset, the strip is a nav landmark marking the current tab with aria-current. Any other value is passed through to the element unchanged.

props.description: What happens when the tabs are wider than the strip. 'auto' lets the component choose, which today always scrolls. 'scroll' scrolls the tabs horizontally, with edge fades and arrow affordances for pointers that can hover. 'visible' turns overflow handling off and lets the tabs spill out of the strip. The selected tab is always scrolled back into view.

accessibility.description: Each label must have at least 4.5:1 contrast with the tab surface behind it. For Hover and Pointer down, measure the final background after the overlay layer is applied.

usage.description: TabList provides tab-style navigation for organizing content into categorized sections. Use it to let users switch between related views without leaving the page. A strip narrower than its tabs scrolls horizontally and keeps the selected tab in view.

bestPractices.description: Keep tab labels short and descriptive so users can quickly scan available sections.
Leave overflow handling on: a strip narrower than its tabs scrolls, and the selected tab is kept in view. Use TabMenu when you want a curated group of extra options rather than a scrolling strip.

When using hasDivider with action buttons alongside tabs, match the Button size to the TabList size (both md, both sm); the divided tab strip reserves space so tabs and same-size buttons align to a shared baseline above the rail.

Reach for role="tablist" when the strip switches panels in place, and give each tab a panelId pointing at the panel it opens: that link is how a screen reader gets from a tab to its content. Leave it off for navigation between views.
Set isFullBleed to stretch a tab bar inside a padded LayoutHeader, Card, or Section to the container's inline content edges, instead of reaching for negative-margin CSS.
Use tabs for sequential steps or workflows; use a stepper or wizard pattern instead.
Place more than 6–8 visible tabs before the overflow menu; prioritize the most important categories.

Confuse TabList with SegmentedControl or ToggleButton. TabList is for navigation between views. SegmentedControl and ToggleButton are input controls: SegmentedControl always has exactly one selected option, while ToggleButton can be toggled on or off.

usage.description: TabList provides tab-style navigation for organizing content into categorized sections. Use it to let users switch between related views without leaving the page. A strip narrower than its tabs scrolls horizontally and keeps the selected tab in view.

bestPractices.description: Keep tab labels short and descriptive so users can quickly scan available sections.
Leave overflow handling on: a strip narrower than its tabs scrolls, and the selected tab is kept in view. Use TabMenu when you want a curated group of extra options rather than a scrolling strip.

When using hasDivider with action buttons alongside tabs, match the Button size to the TabList size (both md, both sm); the divided tab strip reserves space so tabs and same-size buttons align to a shared baseline above the rail.

Reach for role="tablist" when the strip switches panels in place, and give each tab a panelId pointing at the panel it opens: that link is how a screen reader gets from a tab to its content. Leave it off for navigation between views.
Set isFullBleed to stretch a tab bar inside a padded LayoutHeader, Card, or Section to the container's inline content edges, instead of reaching for negative-margin CSS.
Use tabs for sequential steps or workflows; use a stepper or wizard pattern instead.
Place more than 6–8 visible tabs before the overflow menu; prioritize the most important categories.

Confuse TabList with SegmentedControl or ToggleButton. TabList is for navigation between views. SegmentedControl and ToggleButton are input controls: SegmentedControl always has exactly one selected option, while ToggleButton can be toggled on or off.
