params.name: placement
params.description: Position relative to the trigger. Logical: start/end resolve against the popover's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors in pure CSS).

params.name: alignment
params.description: Alignment along the placement axis. Logical: start/end resolve against the popover's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors in pure CSS).

params.name: delay
params.description: Delay before showing on hover, in milliseconds.

params.name: hideDelay
params.description: Delay before hiding after mouse or focus leaves, in milliseconds.

params.name: focusTrigger
params.description: When focus should open the tooltip. auto opens when the trigger itself takes focus, or focus lands inside a trigger that is focusable at that moment, so a roving-tabindex member opens when the arrow keys reach it.

params.name: touchTrigger
params.description: What a tap does where there is no hover. auto opens on tap unless the trigger performs an action of its own (an aria-disabled control performs none); tap always opens (a button whose only job is revealing the tooltip); none never opens on touch.

params.name: isEnabled
params.description: Whether hover and focus triggers are enabled.

params.name: isOpen
params.description: Controlled open state. true force-shows; false force-hides, and focus that would show it calls onShow; undefined lets hover/focus manage visibility.

params.name: isDefaultOpen
params.description: Whether the tooltip should be shown on mount.

params.name: onShow
params.description: Callback fired when the tooltip becomes visible. Under isOpen={false}, it reports focus that would show the tooltip.

params.name: onHide
params.description: Callback fired when the tooltip is hidden.

returns.name: ref
returns.description: Combined ref that sets both position and interaction on the same trigger element.

returns.name: positionRef
returns.description: Ref for the positioning anchor element.

returns.name: interactionRef
returns.description: Ref for the hover/focus interaction element.

returns.name: anchorId
returns.description: CSS anchor name for advanced positioning cases.

returns.name: describedBy
returns.description: ID to compose into aria-describedby on the trigger.

returns.name: renderTooltip
returns.description: Render function for the anchor-positioned tooltip content. The positioning opt-out is excluded: the tooltip always derives its position from placement/alignment.

returns.name: show
returns.description: Opens the tooltip now and keeps it open until hide(), Escape, a press outside, or focus leaving its trigger. Its text is announced once, and onShow fires. Under a controlled isOpen it only calls onShow. Does nothing while isEnabled is false.

returns.name: hide
returns.description: Closes the tooltip now, and onHide fires. Under a controlled isOpen it only calls onHide.

usage.description: Headless hook for hover/focus-triggered tooltips. Builds on useLayer with hover intent, keyboard focus handling, and accessible aria-describedby linking. Use for custom trigger elements that need tooltip behavior without the wrapper component.

bestPractices.description: Use for brief text labels that describe icon buttons, truncated text, abbreviations, or compact controls.
Prefer the Tooltip component for standard wrapping; use the hook when the trigger is not a simple child.

For a toggle-style trigger, have your own button call show() and hide() on each press. Give it aria-describedby and aria-controls set to describedBy, and aria-expanded (true while show() holds the tooltip, false after hide() or onHide), and keep its own accessible name. For an info icon, use InfoTip instead.
Put interactive content inside tooltips: use Popover or HoverCard instead.

paramDescriptions.focusTrigger: when focus opens tooltip; auto = focus on the trigger, or inside a trigger focusable when focus arrives.
paramDescriptions.touchTrigger: tap behavior with no hover; auto = tap unless trigger acts, tap = always, none = never.
paramDescriptions.isOpen: controlled open state: true force-show, false force-hide, undefined unmanaged.

returnDescriptions.show: opens + holds until hide()/Escape/outside press/focus leave; announces once; onShow. Controlled: onShow only. No-op when disabled.

usage.description: An expandable tree structure for displaying hierarchical data with branch connector lines. Use it for file explorers, nested category browsers, or any interface that visualizes parent-child relationships. Under a finger, expanding a row glides the rows below it while its children fade in on the same timing, and a collapse plays it back; pass an `animatedLayout` handle for content after the tree to glide too.

bestPractices.description: Provide meaningful labels and icons for each node to make the hierarchy easy to scan.
Pre-expand important branches so users see key content immediately.

Leaf rows reserve space for a chevron column whenever the tree has any expandable item to line up under; only a fully flat tree (no expandable items at all) renders its rows flush. Rely on this rather than nudging indentation with custom CSS.
Nest more than 4–5 levels deep; flatten the structure or use a different pattern.
Use a tree for flat, non-hierarchical data; use a List instead.

usage.description: Composable combobox engine providing a bare input, search, keyboard navigation, and a styled result dropdown. It renders no input wrapper, border, or selected-value token. Typeahead and Tokenizer compose it for standard fields.

bestPractices.description: Use Typeahead or Tokenizer for standard fields; they wrap BaseTypeahead with input chrome and selected-value rendering it intentionally omits.
Provide your own visible label or aria-label and custom input wrapper so the bare combobox has an accessible name, focus treatment, border, and layout.
Pass anchorRef pointing to your wrapper so the dropdown positions against your custom input chrome, not just the bare input element.
Expect input chrome or selected-value rendering. BaseTypeahead is an engine; the caller owns those visible parts.
Use BaseTypeahead when Typeahead or Tokenizer would suffice; the extra wrapper and styling work is only justified for truly custom compositions.
Treat Escape as cancellation of pending source work. It hides the current popup, but a late response can reopen it.

props.description: Data source providing search and bootstrap methods. `search(query, context)` may call `context.update(items)` to show matches it already has before it returns; the value it returns is the final list, and every list after the first for a query keeps the shown rows first and adds new rows after them.

usage.description: A searchable input for selecting a single item from a large or dynamic dataset. Results appear as the user types, with support for async data sources, debounced search, and custom item rendering. Use it when the option list is too large for a Selector dropdown.

bestPractices.description: Provide descriptive placeholder text that hints at what users can search for.
Show suggestions on focus when users benefit from seeing popular or recent options before typing.
Add a search delay for remote data sources to avoid excessive network requests.

For a remote source, show the matches the page already has at once: call `context.update(local)` in `search`, pass `debounceMs={0}`, delay the server request in the source, and return the server answer with the shown rows first.
Use inside InputGroup when the typeahead needs a single-line prefix or suffix addon.
Use for short, static option lists; use Selector for better discoverability.
Use for multi-selection; use Tokenizer instead.
Place multiple Typeaheads adjacent to each other without clear labels differentiating them.
Wrap a disabled Typeahead in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled triggers swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

docs.name: ChatTypingIndicator
docs.description: Animated three-dot typing hint with a localized, grammar-aware label: "Ana is typing...", "Ana and Ben are typing...", or "Ana and 2 others are typing...". Dots bounce with staggered stylex.keyframes delays, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. Each new label is announced once, politely, through the shared announcement channel (useAnnounce); inside a chat log the log announces it instead. The indicator itself carries no live role, so it can mount conditionally without being skipped or heard twice.

docs.name: ChatVirtualizer
docs.description: Windowed message list for long transcripts: only the rows near the viewport are rendered, and the rest is represented by two spacer elements, so a thread of thousands of messages costs a viewport of DOM. Rows stay in normal document flow. While a finger scrolls the list, position corrections are written as spacer height rather than a scrollTop jump, so nothing moves under the finger; they settle when that scroll ends. Outside a touch gesture the list writes scrollTop. Follows the newest message by default, re-engaging that follow when a user scroll lands within endThreshold of the bottom. Renders its own scroll container, or nests inside one the caller already owns (see scrollElement).

props.name: data
props.description: Rows to render, oldest first. Changes are detected by REFERENCE, so replace the array instead of mutating it — a mutation leaves the geometry stale.

props.name: getRowKey
props.description: Stable identity per row, coerced with String(). The size cache and the running size averages are keyed by it, so deriving a key from the index discards every measurement whenever the list shifts.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Renders one row. Row spacing must live inside what this returns (padding) — container gap and margins are invisible to measurement, so the geometry would drift by one gap per row.

props.name: estimatedItemSize
props.description: Height assumed for rows that have not been measured yet; a function is authoritative and is never overridden by the running averages. Bias it LOW — an estimate that is too small lets content grow below you and leaves your position valid, while one that is too large shrinks the scroll range and the browser clamps your position into it.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle exposing scrollToDistanceFromBottomPx and anchorToKey. Both DECLARE a reference frame rather than performing one scroll: the list keeps restoring the declared position as rows measure in, so a landing is not lost to content that arrives after it.

props.name: getItemType
props.description: Classifies a row so measured sizes feed a running average per type. A transcript mixing one-line tool stubs with long markdown then converges to an honest price per shape instead of one blended number.

props.name: scrollElement
props.description: Attach mode: the scroll container the caller already owns, into which spacers and rows render as one content block instead of the list creating its own scroller. Pass the ELEMENT, not a ref: a parent's ref attaches after its children's layout effects, so a ref still reads null on the commit that first needs the scroller, and a ref mutation is invisible to React — nothing re-renders and no effect re-runs when it lands, while an element in state makes its arrival a render and a real dependency (scroll listeners, observation, and the gesture state machine are rebuilt when the container changes). Read it in a passive effect and hold it in state. Pass null (not undefined) while it is still pending: undefined means own-container mode, and one commit of that inside an unbounded parent mounts every row.

props.name: endThreshold
props.description: How close to the bottom, in px, a user scroll must land to re-engage following the newest message; disengaging is any upward movement past it. Too tight and a user who stops visually at the bottom (trackpad inertia, fractional row heights, page zoom) silently stops following while output grows below them.

props.name: overscanTop
props.description: Extra px of rows kept mounted above the viewport, absorbing upward scrolls before a new window has to be computed.

props.name: overscanBottom
props.description: Extra px of rows kept mounted below the viewport.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the scroll container the list creates, which keyboard users can focus and scroll. Own-container mode only; in attach mode the caller names its own scroller.

props.name: style
props.description: Applied to the scroll container the list creates. Own-container mode only.

props.name: className
props.description: Applied to the scroll container the list creates. Own-container mode only.

propDescriptions.getRowKey: stable id per row; keys the size cache + running averages — never index-derived

docsZh.name: ChatVirtualizer
docsZh.description: 面向长会话的窗口化消息列表：只渲染视口附近的行，其余用两个占位元素表示，因此上千条消息的线程只消耗一个视口的 DOM。行保持在正常文档流中。手指滚动列表期间，位置修正写入占位高度而非跳写 scrollTop，所以手指下的内容不会移动；该次滚动结束后修正落定。触摸手势之外，列表直接写入 scrollTop。默认跟随最新消息，用户滚动落在距底部 endThreshold 以内时重新接管跟随。可自建滚动容器，也可嵌入调用方已有的容器（见 scrollElement）。

propDescriptions.data: 要渲染的行，按时间正序。变更通过引用比较检测，所以请替换数组而不要原地修改。
propDescriptions.getRowKey: 每行的稳定标识（内部用 String() 转换）。尺寸缓存与运行时均值都以它为键，用下标派生会在列表位移时丢弃全部测量结果。
propDescriptions.renderItem: 渲染单行。行间距必须放在返回内容内部（padding）——容器的 gap 和 margin 测量不到，会让几何每行漂移一个间距。
propDescriptions.estimatedItemSize: 未测量行的假定高度；传函数则以函数为准，不受运行时均值覆盖。要往小估：估小了内容向下生长、位置依然有效；估大了滚动范围收缩，浏览器会把位置钳进新范围，无法挽回。
propDescriptions.handleRef: 暴露 scrollToDistanceFromBottomPx 与 anchorToKey 的命令式句柄。两者都是“声明参考系”而非执行一次滚动：行陆续测量进来时列表会持续恢复所声明的位置。
propDescriptions.getItemType: 为行分类，使测量结果按类型累积均值。工具调用短行与长 markdown 混排的会话因此能收敛出各自诚实的价格，而非一个混合数字。
propDescriptions.scrollElement: 接管模式：调用方已有的滚动容器，占位与行包在一个内容块里渲染进去，列表不再自建滚动容器。传元素本身而非 ref：父的 ref 在子的 layout effect 之后才装配，所以最先需要滚动容器的那次提交里 ref 仍读到 null；而且 ref 赋值对 React 不可见，落地时既不重渲染也不重跑 effect，元素存进 state 才让“到达”成为一次渲染和真正的依赖（换容器时滚动监听、观察和手势状态机都要重建）。请在 passive effect 里读出并存进 state。尚未就绪时传 null 而不是 undefined：undefined 表示自建容器模式，在不限高的父容器里哪怕只有一次提交也会挂载全部行。
propDescriptions.endThreshold: 用户滚动落点距底部多少 px 才重新接管跟随；脱离则是任何越过该范围的向上移动。设得太紧，视觉上停在底部的用户（触控板惯性、小数行高、页面缩放）会在内容持续产出时悄悄停止跟随。
propDescriptions.overscanTop: 视口上方额外保持挂载的行数（按 px），用于在需要重算窗口前吸收向上滚动。
propDescriptions.overscanBottom: 视口下方额外保持挂载的行数（按 px）。
propDescriptions.label: 列表自建滚动容器的无障碍名称，键盘用户可聚焦并滚动它。仅自建容器模式有效；接管模式下由调用方为自己的滚动容器命名。
propDescriptions.style: 应用在列表自建的滚动容器上。仅自建容器模式有效。
propDescriptions.className: 应用在列表自建的滚动容器上。仅自建容器模式有效。

docs.name: CircleCheckIndicator
docs.description: The iOS multiple-selection mark: an empty circle, a filled circle with a checkmark, or a filled circle with a bar for the partial state. A checkbox-family indicator: map it to `checkbox` with defineTheme({indicators}) and every CheckboxInput and CheckboxList draws it. Decorative (aria-hidden); the owning control keeps the input, role, accessible name, focus, and keyboard behavior. Its colors fade over the theme duration on every pointer and change at once under Reduce Motion.

props.name: state
props.description: Which state to draw. The unchecked circle is an empty ring, not nothing.

props.name: size
props.description: Control size. The circle draws at UIKit’s diameters, 18px (sm) or 21.8px (md), centred in the host’s 20px or 24px slot.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Draws the disabled look. Purely visual; the owning control keeps the disabled semantics.

props.name: children
props.description: Content drawn inside the circle instead of the mark, e.g. the loading Spinner CheckboxInput passes while a change is pending.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

usage.description: Use it where iOS shows a selection circle: the rows of a list in edit mode, and multiple-choice sets whose product follows iOS. Map it to `checkbox` in a theme to change every checkbox at once, or render it in a row you lay out yourself.

bestPractices.description: Map it with defineTheme({indicators: {checkbox: CircleCheckIndicator}}) so CheckboxInput and CheckboxList keep their semantics and focus ring.
Map it only in a theme meant for iOS. It draws the circle on every platform, and Android marks multiple choice with a square box.
Keep a visible label beside it; the circle is decorative and announces nothing.
Use it for a single choice; a radio, or a checkmark on the chosen row, says "one of these".
Give it a role, a label or a tab stop; the owning control has those.

usage.description: A circular progress indicator that shows completion as a ring or arc. Use it for upload progress, score displays, dashboard gauges, or compact progress where horizontal space is limited. Complements ProgressBar for radial layouts.

bestPractices.description: Pass a value for determinate progress; set isIndeterminate when the duration is unknown.
Show the value with hasValueLabel, or pass children for custom center content: an icon or short label.
Always provide a label, even though it is visually hidden by default; screen readers need it.
Use circular progress for long text labels; use ProgressBar instead, which has more room for label and value display.
Use an indeterminate CircularProgress for small inline loading states; Spinner is the inline indicator.

docs.name: CommentPin
docs.description: Avatar-first button for opening one anchored annotation thread or a caller-defined group. A single marker shows its lead participant; a grouped marker shows up to three participant circles (two plus an ellipsis beyond three) and the total thread count. Whenever any represented thread is unread, an accent status dot appears after the count. Three sizes follow the element-size scale. The host owns anchors, coordinates, grouping, collision handling, and the comments surface.

props.name: label
props.description: Required accessible action name and hover/focus tooltip. Include grouped, unread, or resolved context when it changes the action meaning, for example “Open 4 grouped annotations from Ada and Lin, 2 unread”.

props.name: participants
props.description: Non-empty ordered participants, lead first. A single pin renders the first. A grouped pin renders distinct IDs as an AvatarGroup of at most three circles: every participant when three or fewer are distinct, otherwise the first two plus an ellipsis overflow circle. Pass every distinct participant so the overflow appears exactly when more than three people participate. Each record has id, name, and optional avatarSrc.

props.name: size
props.description: Pin height on the element-size scale: sm 28px, md 32px, lg 36px, with 22px, 24px, and 28px participant circles. Padding is equal on every side, so the avatars and overflow sit the same distance from each edge; the trailing count or unread dot adds a little end padding so it never crowds the edge.

props.name: threadCount
props.description: Total represented threads. A finite positive integer above one switches to grouped presentation and displays the exact count. The host still owns the clustering policy.

props.name: unreadCount
props.description: Represented threads with unread activity. When above zero, an accent status dot appears at the end of the pin, after the thread total or the single participant; the number itself is not shown. Invalid values are ignored and values above threadCount are capped. Repeat the unread context in label.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Whether the pin is the active annotation target. Draws a solid 2px accent outline outside the pin, keeping its elevation, plus aria-pressed; the shared offset focus outline remains farther outside for keyboard focus. Follow aria-pressed toggle semantics: activating the selected pin again should clear the host selection.

props.name: isDimmed
props.description: Whether another pin is selected. Lowers this pin’s opacity without disabling it, so it remains available to switch selection. Leave it false on every pin when nothing is selected. Selected presentation wins if both are true.

props.name: isResolved
props.description: Whether every represented thread is resolved. A resolved pin renders nothing unless it is selected: resolved discussion leaves the content, while a thread the reader opened (or resolved from its popover) keeps its anchor, with the selected treatment, until the host clears the selection.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables activation: the pin exposes aria-disabled, keeps its tab stop, and blocks every activation path. Useful for a pending anchor before its thread exists.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Product-owned activation handler. Open or select the represented thread/group here; CommentPin owns no comments or popover state.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX layout customization for the button root. Hosts may position it over content or in a margin; absolute anchors map to the logical bottom-start corner by placing the inline-start edge at the anchor and translating the pin upward by its full height.

anatomy.name: Marker surface
anatomy.description: The compact speech-bubble button surface, with a fixed 2px logical bottom-start corner, 28, 32, or 36px tall by size and padded equally on every side. It owns selected, resolved, disabled, hover, press, focus-visible, and grouped presentation, but no coordinates.

anatomy.name: Representative avatars
anatomy.description: One Avatar for a single thread. A group shows its distinct participants as an AvatarGroup capped at three circles: up to three Avatars, or two Avatars plus the overflow indicator when more than three people participate. Avatars are decorative inside the marker; the button label owns accessibility.

anatomy.name: Overflow indicator
anatomy.description: An ellipsis AvatarGroupOverflow circle that takes the third position when a group has more than three distinct participants. It shows no number, so the group count stays the pin’s only number. Decorative and non-interactive inside the pin.

anatomy.name: Group count
anatomy.description: Exact total number of represented threads. Appears when threadCount is greater than one, before the unread dot when there is one; it is a quantity, not ordinal identity. Extra end padding keeps it clear of the pin’s edge.

anatomy.name: Unread dot
anatomy.description: An accent StatusDot at the end of the pin that marks unread activity whenever unreadCount is above zero: after the group count, or after the participant on a single-thread pin. It adds no second number; decorative inside the pin.

usage.description: Use CommentPin as the interactive anchor for comments attached to images, documents, canvases, table regions, or content margins. Pass the distinct participants (lead first), the total number of threads the host grouped at that anchor, and how many of them are unread. The component intentionally has no coordinates, anchor IDs, thread IDs, clustering algorithm, popover, or Comments dependency: those stay with the product so the same marker can sit over transformed media or in normal document layout. Participant Avatars and the overflow circle suppress their own tooltips and interaction; the pin is the only button and its label is the complete action name.

accessibility.name: Native button activation
accessibility.description: CommentPin is one native button. Tab reaches an enabled pin; Enter and Space activate it. A disabled pin stays in the tab order and is announced as disabled through aria-disabled, and every activation path is blocked.

accessibility.name: Selected state and name
accessibility.description: The required label is the button name and tooltip. aria-pressed communicates controlled selection; participant Avatars, the overflow circle, the visible thread total, and the unread dot remain decorative, so repeat grouped and unread context in label.

accessibility.name: Selection and focus
accessibility.description: The solid 2px accent outline hugs the pin while the shared focus-visible outline sits farther outside it, so selection and keyboard focus remain distinguishable; forced colors uses the platform Highlight treatment. Verify both selected and selected-plus-focused states against the host surface.

bestPractices.description: Pass the lead commenter first. For a group, pass every distinct participant ordered by how well they help users recognize the cluster; the pin shows up to three circles and summarizes the rest with an ellipsis.
Write a complete label that names the action and relevant context, such as “Open 4 grouped annotations from Ada and Lin”.
Keep coordinates, zoom/rotation transforms, collision handling, group membership, and thread selection in the host; position the pin with layout composition or xstyle.
Map an absolute anchor coordinate to the pin’s logical bottom-start corner, not its center. Place the pin’s inline-start edge at the anchor and translate it upward by its full height.

When one pin is selected, pass isDimmed to the other pins instead of disabling them. They stay available to switch selection while the active pin holds visual focus. When nothing is selected, no pin dims.
Treat selection as an aria-pressed toggle: when the selected pin is activated again, clear the host selection.
Treat threadCount as quantity only. The Avatar identities stay primary even when the total is large.
Pass unreadCount whenever represented threads have unread activity. Its accent dot keeps unread work visible beside the total; repeat the unread count in label.
Use an ordinal number as the marker identity. Numbering becomes unstable and hard to scan as annotations are inserted, removed, filtered, or grouped.
Put interactive Avatar links or buttons inside the marker. The marker root owns the one action and accessible name.
Slice participants yourself to control the overflow. Pass every distinct participant so the ellipsis appears exactly when more than three people participate, and name the hidden people in label.

examples.label: Single thread
examples.code:
<CommentPin
  label="Open annotation from Ada"
  participants={[{id: 'ada', name: 'Ada Lovelace', avatarSrc: '/ada.jpg'}]}
  onClick={() => openThread('thread-1')}
/>

examples.label: Grouped threads
examples.code:
<CommentPin
  label="Open 4 grouped annotations from Ada and Lin"
  participants={[
    {id: 'ada', name: 'Ada Lovelace', avatarSrc: '/ada.jpg'},
    {id: 'lin', name: 'Lin Chen', avatarSrc: '/lin.jpg'},
  ]}
  threadCount={4}
  isSelected={selectedCluster === 'cluster-1'}
  onClick={() => setSelectedCluster('cluster-1')}
/>

docsDense.description: avatar-first annotation anchor; 1 lead Avatar for one thread; groups show max 3 circles (2 Avatars + ellipsis beyond 3) + exact total; accent StatusDot after the total (or the avatar on a single pin) when unreadCount > 0; sm/md/lg = 28/32/36px; host owns placement/grouping

usage.description: Interactive anchor for comments over content or in margins. Pass every distinct participant, the total thread count, and the unread thread count; keep coordinates, clustering, collisions, thread state, and opened UI in the host. Absolute coordinates map to the logical bottom-start corner, while another pin is selected its siblings use isDimmed and remain interactive, and activating the selected pin again clears the host selection.

bestPractices.description: Pass the lead commenter first and write a complete action label, including unread context.
Use threadCount as quantity, never ordinal identity; pass unreadCount so an accent dot marks unread work.
Nest interactive Avatars, slice participants to fake the overflow, or pass coordinates/grouping logic into the marker.

propDescriptions.label: required action name + hover/focus tooltip; include grouped/unread context
propDescriptions.participants: non-empty ordered tuple of {id,name,avatarSrc?}; single renders 1; groups render ≤3 circles (2 + ellipsis overflow beyond 3 distinct)
propDescriptions.threadCount: positive integer total; >1 selects grouped presentation; default 1
propDescriptions.unreadCount: unread represented threads; >0 shows an accent dot after the total (or the avatar on a single pin); capped at threadCount; default 0
propDescriptions.isSelected: controlled active pin; solid 2px accent outline outside the pin + aria-pressed; host clears it when the selected pin is activated again
propDescriptions.isDimmed: controlled de-emphasis for non-selected siblings only while another pin is selected; remains interactive
propDescriptions.isResolved: resolved pins render nothing unless selected
propDescriptions.isDisabled: disabled marker: aria-disabled, keeps its tab stop, blocks every activation path
propDescriptions.onClick: host activation handler
propDescriptions.xstyle: root layout/positioning styles; marker owns no coordinates

docsZh.description: 用于打开单个锚定批注线程或调用方定义线程组的头像优先按钮。单线程显示主要参与者头像；分组标记最多显示三个圆形（超过三人时显示两个头像和省略号圆形），并显示线程总数；有未读线程时在末尾（总数或单个头像之后）显示强调色状态点。三种尺寸遵循元素尺寸刻度。

propDescriptions.label: 必填的无障碍操作名称及悬停/聚焦提示；包含分组、未读或已解决上下文。
propDescriptions.participants: 有序参与者列表（主要参与者在前）；单线程显示第一个；分组最多显示三个圆形，超过三位不同参与者时显示前两个头像和省略号溢出圆形。
propDescriptions.size: 标记高度：sm 28px、md 32px、lg 36px，参与者头像分别为 22px、24px、28px；四边内边距相等。
propDescriptions.threadCount: 所代表的线程总数；大于 1 时使用分组样式并显示准确数量。
propDescriptions.unreadCount: 有未读活动的线程数；大于 0 时在总数之后（单线程时在头像之后）显示强调色状态点，不显示该数字。
propDescriptions.isSelected: 标记是否为当前批注目标；再次激活已选中的标记时，宿主应清除选择（aria-pressed 切换语义）。
propDescriptions.isDimmed: 其他标记被选中时降低此标记的视觉突出度，但不禁用操作；未选中任何标记时不应降低。
propDescriptions.isResolved: 所代表的线程是否都已解决；已解决的标记除非被选中否则不渲染。
propDescriptions.isDisabled: 通过 aria-disabled 禁用激活：保留 Tab 焦点，拦截所有激活路径。
propDescriptions.onClick: 由产品拥有的激活处理函数。
propDescriptions.xstyle: 根按钮的 StyleX 布局样式；由宿主决定内容上方或边距中的位置。

docs.name: CommentComposer
docs.description: A comment composer: an input that grows to five lines, with typeahead triggers and pasted or dropped images, above attach and emoji buttons and Post. Controlled: your app owns the draft.

usage.description: A comment composer writes a new comment. Use it where comments start outside a Comments panel, such as a new margin comment on a text selection. Comments and CommentThread use it for new comments, replies, and edits.

anatomy.name: Quoted passage
anatomy.description: The passage a new inline comment attaches to, in a muted card above the input.

anatomy.name: Input
anatomy.description: Grows with its text to five lines. Enter posts; Shift+Enter adds a line.

anatomy.name: Footer
anatomy.description: Attach images (with `onUploadImages`), Add emoji, your `controls`, then Post at the end.

bestPractices.description: Clear the draft once the comment posts, and keep it when posting fails: show `error` with `onRetry`.
Name the input for its context with `label` when the placeholder alone would be vague, such as "Reply to Maya Chen".
Disable the composer while posting. Pass `isSubmitting`: the input keeps focus, and Post stays focusable but refuses a second press.
Put long instructions in the placeholder. It disappears as the viewer types; keep guidance in surrounding text.

props.name: value
props.description: The draft, controlled.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new draft as the viewer types, picks an emoji, or uploads an image.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Posts the draft from Enter or Post. Empty drafts never post.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder, and the input’s accessible name unless `label` is set. Defaults to the localized "Write a comment…".

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the input.

props.name: isSubmitting
props.description: Holds the attach and emoji buttons while a post is in flight, and makes Post refuse a second press. The composer reports busy.

props.name: error
props.description: Shows an error Banner above the composer.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Adds Retry to the `error` Banner.

props.name: anchor
props.description: The passage a new inline comment attaches to, quoted above the input.

props.name: onAnchorDismiss
props.description: Adds Remove quoted text to the quoted passage; clear `anchor` when it is called.

props.name: highlightColor
props.description: The palette color your app highlights passages in; the quote draws its rule in it.

props.name: onUploadImages
props.description: Uploads attached, pasted, or dropped images and appends them to the draft as Markdown. Adds the attach button.

props.name: triggers
props.description: Typeahead triggers, such as an `@` people search.

props.name: agentCommands
props.description: Agents the comment can address: typing `/` lists them.

props.name: hasEmojiPicker
props.description: Whether the Add emoji button shows.

props.name: controls
props.description: Product-owned controls after the attach and emoji buttons.

examples.label: New comment

docs.name: Comments
docs.description: The comments on one item: comment threads with one level of replies, reactions, edit history, controlled typing and seen metadata, inline-comment quotes, and activity events in time order, with a composer for new comments. Controlled: your app owns the data and every mutation; the panel owns presentation, selection, and focus.

usage.description: The Comments panel shows the conversation about a document, task, or record: its comment threads and activity, with a composer for new comments. Use it as a side panel or section that fills a sized container, or embedded at its content height inside a card or popover. Render a single thread with CommentThread and a standalone composer with CommentComposer.

anatomy.name: Thread
anatomy.description: An outlined Card on a section parent, or an edge-to-edge Section with 1px dividers on a card parent. Selecting it opens the thread: the body unclamps, replies show, and the reply composer opens, taking focus on a pointer press.

anatomy.name: Avatar
anatomy.description: A 28×28 picture or initials: a circle for people, a rounded square for agents. In an open thread a 2px rail joins the avatars in segments.

anatomy.name: Header
anatomy.description: One avatar tall: name, relative time, Edited (opens the edit history), and Resolved. Mark as resolved or Reopen, Add reaction, Reply, Copy link, and the more menu (Edit, Delete) appear while the pointer or focus is on the thread, collapsing into the more menu when room runs out.

anatomy.name: Quoted passage
anatomy.description: An inline comment quotes its passage as an italic blockquote whose rule takes the highlight color. A passage edited away keeps a neutral rule and an Outdated badge.

anatomy.name: Body
anatomy.description: Markdown, clamped to three lines until the thread opens. Images open in a Lightbox. A comment still being written shows its progress instead.

anatomy.name: Reactions
anatomy.description: A toggle for each reaction, pressed where the viewer reacted; its tooltip names who reacted.

anatomy.name: Replies
anatomy.description: One level, behind View replies. A host-marked unread reply reveals without selecting the thread, moving focus, or opening the reply composer. Replying to a reply posts to the thread.

anatomy.name: Live state
anatomy.description: Controlled typing state appears at the end of an open thread, with its pulsing dots in the avatar column and its label on the comment-text line. Controlled `seenBy` metadata is available to comment render callbacks but has no default presentation.

anatomy.name: Activity event
anatomy.description: A timeline row for a status change or other event, interleaved with threads by time.

anatomy.name: Composer
anatomy.description: A two-row CommentComposer docked at the bottom (or top): the input above attach and emoji buttons and Post.

bestPractices.description: Keep the data controlled: update `comments` after each callback. Return a Promise so the panel shows the pending state and, when it rejects, an error with Retry.
Match the surface: give a pane a definite height, use `layout="embedded"` inside a card or popover, and set `container="card"` on a card parent so cards never nest.
For inline comments, keep anchoring in your app: pass each thread its `anchor`, mark it `orphaned` when it no longer resolves, and sync `selectedThreadId` with the passage you highlight.

Keep live state controlled and transport-neutral: map your collaboration layer to `typingUsers` and `seenBy`, and use `onComposerDraftChange` to publish local activity. `seenBy` stays hidden unless a comment render callback presents it. Debounce and expire transient activity in your app.
Put data fetching, authorization, or telemetry in render slots. Keep them in your app and pass the results as data.
Assume `selectedThreadId` moves focus or opens a composer. It reveals and scrolls the controlled thread without interrupting the viewer; only their Reply action opens the reply composer.

accessibility.name: Comment list
accessibility.description: The threads sit in a log named after the region, such as "Threads in Launch plan", so screen readers hear new comments politely. Each comment is an article named by its author, and the region reports busy while comments load.

accessibility.name: Live updates
accessibility.description: Typing is a polite status message with reduced-motion-safe dots. `seenBy` metadata has no default presentation and introduces no additional live region.

accessibility.name: Thread toggle
accessibility.description: Each thread has one toggle button (the WAI-ARIA Button pattern, with aria-pressed) named "Thread by" and its author. Enter or Space opens or closes it and keeps focus on it; a pointer press on the thread opens it with focus in the reply composer. The whole surface takes the system focus ring while the toggle has focus.

accessibility.name: Replies and actions
accessibility.description: View replies is a disclosure button with aria-expanded and aria-controls (the WAI-ARIA Disclosure pattern). The more menu follows the Menu Button pattern; when an edit is saved or cancelled, or the delete dialog closes, focus returns to it.

accessibility.name: Focus after changes
accessibility.description: Focus never drops to the page. After a delete it moves to the next thread, or to the thread when a reply was deleted. Load earlier comments keeps focus on itself, or on the Retry that replaces it when loading fails. A thread selected when the panel mounts opens without taking focus.

accessibility.name: Busy actions
accessibility.description: Post and reactions stay focusable while a request is in flight and refuse a second press, so focus never drops to the page mid-request.

accessibility.name: Errors
accessibility.description: Failures show in error Banners next to the thing that failed, each with Retry when the action can be repeated. A Banner carries no live role of its own: its failure is announced once, assertively, through the shared announcement channel, unless it sits inside the chat log, which delivers it. The progress label of a comment still being written follows the same rule, politely. The edit-history dialog announces its failure through an alert region inside the dialog. A failed delete is announced once, assertively, as the confirmation dialog changes its text.

components.name: Comments
components.description: Comment threads and activity events in time order, with a composer for new comments and the dialogs threads open.

props.name: comments
props.description: The threads: each thread’s first comment, carrying `replies` (one level), `reactions`, transient `typingUsers`, hidden per-comment `seenBy` metadata, `anchor` for inline comments, `isResolved`, `status`, `progress`, and per-comment permissions. `seenBy` remains available to comment render callbacks. Shown in time order with `events`.

props.name: events
props.description: Activity on the item, interleaved with the threads by `createdAt` as compact timeline rows.

props.name: currentUser
props.description: The viewer: their own comments get Edit and Delete, and their avatar sits beside the reply composer. Authorization stays with your app.

props.name: mode
props.description: `interactive` enables every permitted action; `non-editable` keeps create, reply, and react but removes edit and delete; `read-only` removes every control that changes data.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the Comments region. Defaults to the localized "Comments".

props.name: composerPosition
props.description: Where the composer for new comments renders.

props.name: density
props.description: Spacing between threads and around the list.

props.name: container
props.description: The parent surface. `section` renders each thread as an outlined Card; `card` renders divider-bounded Sections whose dividers overlap into single lines.

props.name: layout
props.description: `pane` fills its container and scrolls, with the composer docked. `embedded` takes its content’s height inside a host surface: no scroll area or dock, and on a card parent no outer rules.

props.name: composerPlaceholder
props.description: Placeholder of the new-comment composer. Defaults to the localized "Write a comment…", with replies saying "Reply to <name>…"; a custom value replaces both.

props.name: selectedThreadId
props.description: The open thread, controlled, for hosts that sync threads with a document. A host-selected thread opens its body and replies and scrolls into view without moving focus or opening the reply composer.

props.name: onSelectedThreadChange
props.description: Called when the viewer opens a thread or closes the open one.

props.name: composerAnchor
props.description: The passage a new comment will attach to, quoted in the composer. An anchor that arrives while the panel is on screen moves focus to the composer.

props.name: onComposerAnchorDismiss
props.description: Adds Remove quoted text to the composer’s quote; clear `composerAnchor` when it is called.

props.name: composerControls
props.description: Product-owned controls in the new-comment composer’s footer, after its attach and emoji buttons.

props.name: highlightColor
props.description: The palette color your app highlights passages in. Quotes draw their rule in its `--color-border-<color>` token.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows comment-shaped placeholders and reports the region busy.

props.name: loadError
props.description: Shows an error Banner above the threads, for comments that failed to load.

props.name: onRetryLoad
props.description: Adds Retry to the `loadError` Banner; a Promise keeps Retry busy until it settles.

props.name: hasOlderComments
props.description: Shows Load earlier comments above the threads.

props.name: isLoadingOlder
props.description: Holds Load earlier comments busy while your app fetches the page. A Promise from `onLoadOlder` does the same on its own.

props.name: onLoadOlder
props.description: Loads the previous page: prepend it to `comments`. A rejected Promise shows an error Banner whose Retry takes the button’s place.

props.name: isSubmitting
props.description: Host-controlled pending state for the composers. Promise callbacks get a built-in pending state as well.

props.name: onComposerDraftChange
props.description: Reports drafts owned inside Comments: new comments, replies, and edits. It includes programmatic seeds and reports an empty value after submit, cancel, or a target switch. Route each update by `context`; debounce and expire typing in your app.

props.name: composerError
props.description: Host-controlled error above the new-comment composer. A rejected `onSubmit` shows its own error with Retry.

props.name: reactionOptions
props.description: The reactions Add reaction offers: Like, Love, Haha, Wow, Sad, and Celebrate by default, named in the viewer’s language. Give your own options a `description` to name them.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Posts a comment or a reply. Replies always receive the thread’s first comment as the parent. A rejected Promise restores the draft and shows an error with Retry.

props.name: onSaveEdit
props.description: Adds Edit to the viewer’s own comments and saves the new Markdown. A rejected Promise shows an error Banner with Retry.

props.name: onDelete
props.description: Adds Delete to the viewer’s own comments, confirmed in a dialog first. A rejected Promise keeps the dialog open with the error.

props.name: onRetryComment
props.description: Adds Retry to a comment whose `status` is `error`.

props.name: onReact
props.type: (commentId: string, reactionKey: string, option?: CommentReactionOption) => void | Promise<void>
props.description: Toggles the viewer’s reaction by its stable key.

props.name: onResolveThread
props.description: Adds Mark as resolved to open threads. Set `isResolved` when the call succeeds, and filter resolved threads where they should not show.

props.name: onReopenThread
props.description: Adds Reopen to resolved threads. Clear `isResolved` when the call succeeds.

props.name: loadVersions
props.description: Loads a comment’s edit history, newest first. `previousVersions` works when the data is already loaded.

props.name: onUploadImages
props.type: (files: readonly File[], context: CommentComposerContext) => CommentUploadedImage[] | Promise<CommentUploadedImage[]>
props.description: Uploads images attached, pasted, or dropped in a composer and appends them as Markdown images. Your endpoint authorizes the viewer and validates the files.

props.name: composerTriggers
props.description: Typeahead triggers for every composer, such as an `@` people search whose tokens your Markdown plugins render.

props.name: agentCommands
props.description: Agents a comment can address: typing `/` lists them, and a posted comment shows the command as the agent’s chip. Your app runs the agent.

props.name: markdownPlugins
props.description: Block Markdown plugins for comment bodies, such as embeds for your own entities.

props.name: markdownInlinePlugins
props.description: Inline Markdown plugins for comment bodies, such as the mentions your triggers insert.

props.name: getReplyMention
props.description: Seeds a reply to a reply with a mention of its author in your mention format.

props.name: hasEmojiPicker
props.description: Whether composers offer the emoji picker.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Replaces the default no-comments state.

props.name: renderAnchor
props.description: Replaces a thread’s quoted passage, for example to link it back to the document.

props.name: renderBody
props.description: Replaces a comment’s Markdown body.

props.name: renderVersionBody
props.description: Replaces the body of a version in the edit history.

props.name: renderEvent
props.description: Replaces an activity event’s timeline row.

props.name: renderAdditionalActions
props.description: Adds product actions to a comment’s header, after the built-in ones.

props.name: renderComposer
props.description: Replaces every composer’s input while the panel keeps its draft, pending, error, and context state. Your composer owns its own focus and keyboard handling.

docs.name: CommentThread
docs.description: One comment thread on its own: its first comment, one level of replies, reactions, edit history, controlled typing and seen metadata, and a reply composer. For a margin comment beside a document, a popover under a highlight, or any surface that shows a single thread.

usage.description: A comment thread shows one conversation: its first comment and the replies under it. Use it where a surface shows a single thread, such as a margin card beside a document or a popover opened from a highlight. To show many threads with a composer for new ones, use Comments.

anatomy.name: Surface
anatomy.description: An outlined Card on a page, or a Section without outer rules inside a card or popover. A press anywhere on it opens the thread; a visually hidden toggle carries its name and focus.

anatomy.name: Quoted passage
anatomy.description: The passage an inline comment discusses, as an italic blockquote ruled in the highlight color, with an Outdated badge once the passage is edited away.

anatomy.name: First comment
anatomy.description: Avatar, header (name, time, Edited, Resolved, and the actions shown on hover or focus), Markdown body clamped to three lines until the thread opens, and reactions.

anatomy.name: Replies
anatomy.description: One level of replies behind View replies, joined to the first comment by an avatar rail while the thread is open. A host-marked unread reply reveals without selecting the thread, moving focus, or opening the reply composer.

anatomy.name: Live state
anatomy.description: Controlled typing state follows the conversation while the thread is open, with its pulsing dots in the avatar column and its label on the comment-text line. Controlled `seenBy` metadata remains available to comment render callbacks but has no default presentation.

anatomy.name: Reply composer
anatomy.description: A CommentComposer that opens with the thread, beside the viewer’s avatar.

bestPractices.description: Inside a card or popover, set `container="card"` and give the card no padding: the thread supplies its own insets and draws no outer rules.
Control `isSelected` when the thread opens from elsewhere, such as its highlight in a document. Controlled selection reveals the body and replies without moving focus or opening the reply composer.

In a Popover over a document, pass `onDismiss` and pair it with `hasLightDismiss={false}` and `hasEscapeDismiss={false}` on the host Popover. A press outside the thread or Escape then closes it, except that the first one over an unsaved reply or edit shakes the thread and keeps the draft.

Map your collaboration state to `typingUsers` and `seenBy`, then publish local reply and edit activity with `onComposerDraftChange`. `seenBy` stays hidden unless a comment render callback presents it. The thread never opens a connection or expires participants.
Stack several CommentThreads with a composer to build a discussion. Use Comments, which keeps one thread open at a time and orders threads with activity.
Wrap the thread in your own button or link to open it. The thread is already one toggle; a second control nests interactive elements.
Leave the host Popover’s light dismiss on while passing `onDismiss`. The browser closes the Popover before the thread can keep a draft.

accessibility.name: Escape
accessibility.description: With `onDismiss`, Escape dismisses the thread only when no layer inside it is open. An open emoji picker, menu, or dialog closes first, one Escape at a time.

accessibility.name: Unsaved draft warning
accessibility.description: When a dismissal would discard an unsaved reply or edit, the thread stays open, focus returns to the draft, and a polite live region says the draft is unsaved and that dismissing again discards it. The shake is never the only signal.

accessibility.name: Reduced motion
accessibility.description: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the thread does not shake. Focus and the announcement still mark the kept draft.

props.name: comment
props.description: The thread: its first comment, carrying its replies, reactions, optional anchor, transient `typingUsers`, and per-comment `seenBy` metadata. `seenBy` is not rendered by default but remains available to comment render callbacks.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Whether the thread is open, controlled: body unclamped and replies shown. Omit it to let the thread own selection. Host-controlled selection never moves focus or opens the reply composer; a viewer Reply action does.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.description: Called when the viewer opens or closes the thread.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Hands the thread its anchored host’s light dismissal. A press outside the thread, or an Escape no layer inside it handled, calls it. While a reply or edit holds unsaved text, the first request instead shakes the thread, returns focus to the draft, and announces; the next consecutive request dismisses, and typing or pressing inside the thread re-arms the warning. Pair it with `hasLightDismiss={false}` and `hasEscapeDismiss={false}` on the host Popover. Omit it and the thread never dismisses anything.

props.name: currentUser
props.description: The viewer, for own-comment actions and the reply avatar.

props.name: mode
props.description: Which actions show, as on Comments.

props.name: container

docsDense.description: One comment thread alone: first comment, one reply level, reactions, edit history, controlled typing/seen metadata, reply composer. For margin comments, highlight popovers, any single-thread surface.

usage.description: One conversation: first comment plus replies. For margin cards or highlight popovers. Many threads with a new-comment composer: use Comments.

bestPractices.description: In a card or popover: `container="card"`, card padding 0. Thread owns insets, draws no outer rules.
Control `isSelected` when opened from elsewhere (a document highlight). Reveals body and replies without moving focus or opening the composer.

In a Popover over a document: pass `onDismiss`, set `hasLightDismiss={false}` and `hasEscapeDismiss={false}` on the host. Outside press or Escape closes; the first over an unsaved reply/edit shakes and keeps the draft.
Map collaboration state to `typingUsers`/`seenBy`; publish local drafts via `onComposerDraftChange`. `seenBy` hidden unless a render callback shows it. No connections, no participant expiry.
Stack CommentThreads plus a composer as a discussion. Use Comments.
Wrap the thread in your own button/link. It is already one toggle.
Keep host Popover light dismiss on with `onDismiss`. The browser closes it before the thread can keep a draft.

accessibility.name: Escape

accessibility.name: Unsaved draft warning
accessibility.description: A dismissal over an unsaved reply/edit keeps the thread open, refocuses the draft, and announces politely. Shake is never the only signal.

accessibility.name: Reduced motion

docsZh.description: 单独呈现的一个评论线程：首条评论、一级回复、表情回应、编辑历史、受控的输入中与已读元数据，以及回复输入框。适用于文档旁的边注、高亮下方的弹出层，或任何只显示单个线程的界面。

usage.description: 评论线程展示一段对话：首条评论及其下的回复。用于只显示单个线程的界面，例如文档旁的边注卡片，或从高亮处打开的弹出层。要显示多个线程并提供新评论输入框，请使用 Comments。

bestPractices.description: 放在卡片或弹出层中时，设置 `container="card"` 并去掉卡片的内边距：线程自带内边距，且不绘制外框线。
当线程从其他位置打开（例如文档中的高亮）时，控制 `isSelected`。受控选中会展开正文和回复，但不会移动焦点或打开回复输入框。
在覆盖文档的 Popover 中，传入 `onDismiss`，并在宿主 Popover 上设置 `hasLightDismiss={false}` 和 `hasEscapeDismiss={false}`。这样在线程外按下或按 Escape 会关闭线程；但若回复或编辑中有未保存的文字，第一次只会抖动线程并保留草稿。
将协作状态映射到 `typingUsers` 和 `seenBy`，再通过 `onComposerDraftChange` 发布本地的回复和编辑动态。`seenBy` 默认不显示，除非评论渲染回调展示它。线程从不建立连接，也不会让参与者过期。
把多个 CommentThread 与输入框堆叠成讨论区。请使用 Comments，它一次只展开一个线程，并按动态排序线程。
用自己的按钮或链接包裹线程来打开它。线程本身已是一个切换控件；再加一个控件会嵌套交互元素。
传入 `onDismiss` 时仍保留宿主 Popover 的轻触关闭。浏览器会在线程保留草稿之前关闭 Popover。

accessibility.name: Escape
accessibility.description: 传入 `onDismiss` 后，只有当线程内没有打开的图层时，Escape 才会关闭线程。打开的表情选择器、菜单或对话框会先关闭，每次 Escape 只关闭一层。

accessibility.name: 未保存草稿提示
accessibility.description: 当关闭会丢弃未保存的回复或编辑时，线程保持打开，焦点回到草稿，礼貌型实时区域会说明草稿尚未保存，再次关闭将丢弃它。抖动从来不是唯一的提示。

accessibility.name: 减少动态效果
accessibility.description: 在 `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` 下线程不会抖动。焦点移动和播报仍会提示草稿已保留。

propDescriptions.comment: 线程：首条评论，携带其回复、表情回应、可选锚点、临时的 `typingUsers`，以及每条评论的 `seenBy` 元数据。`seenBy` 默认不渲染，但评论渲染回调可以使用。
propDescriptions.isSelected: 线程是否展开（受控）：正文不截断并显示回复。省略时由线程自行管理选中。宿主控制的选中从不移动焦点或打开回复输入框；查看者点击“回复”才会。
propDescriptions.onSelectedChange: 查看者展开或收起线程时调用。
propDescriptions.onDismiss: 把锚定宿主的轻触关闭交给线程处理。在线程外按下，或线程内没有图层处理的 Escape，都会调用它。若回复或编辑中有未保存的文字，第一次请求改为抖动线程、把焦点移回草稿并播报；紧接着的下一次请求才会关闭，输入或在线程内按下会重新启用提示。请在宿主 Popover 上同时设置 `hasLightDismiss={false}` 和 `hasEscapeDismiss={false}`。省略时线程不会关闭任何东西。
propDescriptions.currentUser: 查看者，用于本人评论的操作和回复头像。
propDescriptions.mode: 显示哪些操作，与 Comments 相同。
propDescriptions.container: 父级界面：页面上的描边 Card，或卡片、弹出层中不带外框线的 Section。
propDescriptions.onSubmit: 发布回复，父级始终是线程的首条评论。被拒绝的 Promise 会恢复草稿，并显示带“重试”的错误。
propDescriptions.onComposerDraftChange: 报告线程内部管理的回复和编辑草稿，包括预填内容，以及提交、取消或切换目标后的空值。请按 `context` 分发更新，并在应用中自行控制传输时机。
propDescriptions.onSaveEdit: 为查看者自己的评论添加“编辑”，并保存新的 Markdown。
propDescriptions.onDelete: 为查看者自己的评论添加“删除”，先在对话框中确认。
propDescriptions.onReact: 按稳定的键切换查看者的表情回应。
propDescriptions.onRetryComment: 为 `status` 为 `error` 的评论添加“重试”。
propDescriptions.onResolveThread: 为未解决的线程添加“标记为已解决”。
propDescriptions.onReopenThread: 为已解决的线程添加“重新打开”。
propDescriptions.loadVersions: 加载评论的编辑历史，最新的在前。
propDescriptions.onUploadImages: 上传在回复输入框中附加、粘贴或拖入的图片，并以 Markdown 图片追加。
propDescriptions.isSubmitting: 宿主控制的回复输入框等待状态。
propDescriptions.composerPlaceholder: 回复输入框的占位文字。默认为本地化的“回复 <name>…”。
propDescriptions.highlightColor: 应用中高亮该线程所引用段落的调色板颜色。
propDescriptions.agentCommands: 回复可以通过 `/` 命令呼叫的智能体。
propDescriptions.composerTriggers: 回复输入框的联想触发器，例如 `@` 人员搜索。
propDescriptions.markdownPlugins: 评论正文的块级 Markdown 插件。
propDescriptions.markdownInlinePlugins: 评论正文的行内 Markdown 插件，例如提及。
propDescriptions.getReplyMention: 回复某条回复时，用提及其作者的内容预填。
propDescriptions.hasEmojiPicker: 回复输入框是否提供表情选择器。
propDescriptions.renderBody: 替换评论的 Markdown 正文。
propDescriptions.renderVersionBody: 替换编辑历史中某个版本的正文。
propDescriptions.renderAdditionalActions: 向评论标题栏添加产品操作。
propDescriptions.renderComposer: 替换回复输入框的输入区域，线程仍保留其草稿和状态。

docs.name: DialogHeroHeader
docs.description: Experimental hero-style header for Dialog, available from @astryxdesign/lab@canary: a full-bleed media slot above the title with the close button overlaid on the media. The high-emphasis sibling of DialogHeader for featured, marketing, or onboarding dialogs.

props.name: title
props.description: Dialog title. A string is wrapped in a level 2 Heading (matching DialogHeader); pass a pre-styled Heading element to customize the treatment. Provides the accessible label for the parent Dialog via aria-labelledby unless the Dialog has an explicit label. The visible title is the default initial focus target; another eligible descendant autofocus request takes priority. A custom Heading receives the label and focus on its own element; if it sets its own id, name the Dialog with aria-labelledby.

props.name: media
props.description: Full-bleed visual rendered above the title (image, illustration, or icon). Stretches to the dialog's padded edges; the close button overlays its top-trailing corner. Size the media itself (e.g. width 100%) to fill the slot.

props.name: mediaMode
props.description: Luminance of the media surface. Composes MediaTheme under the hood so content overlaid on the media (the close button) picks up contrast-safe inverted tokens: 'dark' media gets light overlay content, 'light' media gets dark. Omit to keep ambient theme tokens.

props.name: isTitleHidden
props.description: Visually hides the title row while keeping it available to screen readers, so the dialog stays named by the title.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Content placed before the title (e.g. an icon), inline with the heading.

props.name: maxLines
props.description: Max lines before the title truncates with an ellipsis. Only applies when title is a string (auto-wrapped in a Heading).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Close button callback, called with false when the close button is clicked. If not provided, no close button is rendered. Same contract as DialogHeader.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Adds a themed border at the bottom edge. Defaults to the parent Layout's defaultHasDividers context value.

usage.description: Drop into Layout's header slot inside a Dialog, exactly like DialogHeader. Use when the dialog opens onto a featured, marketing, or onboarding moment where the compact DialogHeader is too understated. The media bleeds to the dialog's edges automatically and the close button floats over its top-trailing corner. The visible title is the default initial focus target; inline previews do not move focus. Install @astryxdesign/lab@canary with @astryxdesign/core@canary and import both packages’ CSS. Lab APIs can change between canary versions.

bestPractices.description: Set mediaMode to match the media's luminance so the overlaid close button stays legible: dark imagery needs mediaMode="dark".
Size the media content to fill the slot (width 100% for images); the slot itself only positions and bleeds.
Keep actions (CTAs) in LayoutFooter; the hero header takes no actions slot.
Use isTitleHidden when the media already communicates the message visually; the title still names the dialog for screen readers.
Use for routine confirmations or forms; use the compact DialogHeader instead.
Pass decorative media without an empty alt: use alt="" on purely decorative images so screen readers skip them.

examples.label: Onboarding dialog
Hidden title (media carries the message)
examples.code:
<DialogHeroHeader
  title="Product tour"
  media={<AnnouncementIllustration />}
  isTitleHidden
  onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
/>

docsDense.description: canary-only lab hero Dialog header: full-bleed media slot + title, close button overlaid on media (MediaTheme via mediaMode)

usage.description: High-emphasis sibling of DialogHeader for featured/marketing/onboarding dialogs. Drops into Layout header slot; media bleeds to dialog edges; title names the dialog; visible title is the default initial focus target. Import from @astryxdesign/lab and load core + lab CSS; install both packages at @canary.

bestPractices.description: Match mediaMode to the media luminance for close-button contrast.
Size media to fill the slot (width 100%).
Keep CTAs in LayoutFooter.
Use isTitleHidden when the media carries the message; SR name is kept.
Use for routine confirmations/forms; use DialogHeader.

usage.description: 像 DialogHeader 一样放入 Dialog 内 Layout 的 header 插槽。当对话框呈现精选、营销或引导场景，紧凑的 DialogHeader 不够醒目时使用。媒体自动延伸到对话框边缘，关闭按钮浮动在媒体的尾部上角。可见标题是默认的初始焦点目标；内联预览不会移动焦点。安装 @astryxdesign/lab@canary 和 @astryxdesign/core@canary，并导入两个包的 CSS。Lab API 可能在 canary 版本之间变化。

bestPractices.description: 让 mediaMode 与媒体的明暗匹配，保证浮动关闭按钮清晰可读：深色图片需要 mediaMode="dark"。
让媒体内容填满插槽（图片用 width 100%）；插槽本身只负责定位和延伸。
操作按钮（CTA）放在 LayoutFooter；hero 头部不提供操作插槽。
当媒体已经在视觉上传达信息时使用 isTitleHidden；标题仍会为屏幕阅读器命名对话框。
用于常规确认或表单；请改用紧凑的 DialogHeader。
装饰性媒体缺少空 alt；纯装饰图片请使用 alt="" 让屏幕阅读器跳过。

usage.description: Read-only, syntax-highlighted diff of one file for code review surfaces. Renders a file header (path, Added/Deleted/Renamed token, +/− line counts, a headerEnd slot, and an optional disclosure) over the file's hunks in unified or split (side-by-side) view. Rows use the same syntax-theme diff slots as CodeBlock with isDiff, so one syntax theme styles both. renderLineAnnotation adds a full-width row under any line (for review comments) and onLineNumberClick turns line numbers into buttons. Build the file model with parseUnifiedDiff(patch), which returns one file per file in a git or diff -u patch, or with createDiffFile({oldValue, newValue}) when you hold two versions of a text. Display options cover how a change is marked (classic +/− glyphs, bars, or none), whether changed rows are tinted, and word- or character-level highlighting of what changed inside each removed/added line pair. Each changed line carries a visually hidden "Added"/"Removed" label, so the change reads without colour in every mode. Unwrapped, line numbers and change indicators stay pinned while the code scrolls; in split view each side is its own scroller, so the split stays fixed at half and half, the sides scroll sideways in lockstep, and a row is as tall as its taller side. While code overflows sideways, sideways overscroll is off, so trackpads neither bounce past a line nor swipe the browser back. In right-to-left pages the hunk area stays left-to-right, like a code editor: annotation content reads in the page direction, and annotation rows scroll with the code. When a change is too large to compare line by line, createDiffFile marks its hunk with isReplacedBlock: it lists every old line as removed and every new line as added. DiffViewer folds those lines behind a "Large change: N lines" row, where N counts the block's removed plus added lines, with a Show full diff button. A file with more than 2,000 other changed lines starts folded the same way, because every row costs render time. Its line diff is still there when the reader opens it. A fold opens by itself when a line it would hide has an annotation, so no review comment is hidden. Rows are plain DOM with no virtualization: collapse or window very large files.

bestPractices.description: Render one DiffViewer per file and lay out the list yourself; parseUnifiedDiff(patch).map(file => <DiffViewer key={file.newPath ?? file.oldPath} file={file} />) is the multi-file case.
Anchor review comments with the DiffViewerLineRef side + lineNumber pair: it is the same in unified and split view.
Put file-level actions such as a "Viewed" checkbox in headerEnd, and drive isCollapsed from the same state if viewed files should fold away.
Use DiffViewer for a short diff inside prose or a chat message; a CodeBlock with isDiff (or a ```diff fence in Markdown) is the lighter fit there.

examples.label: Unified diff from a patch
examples.code:
const [file] = parseUnifiedDiff(patch);

<DiffViewer file={file} />

examples.label: Split view
examples.code: <DiffViewer file={file} viewMode="split" />

examples.label: Diff two versions of a text
examples.code:
const file = createDiffFile({oldValue: before, newValue: after, path: 'src/app.ts'});

<DiffViewer file={file} />

examples.label: Bars, character highlighting, no row tint
examples.code:
<DiffViewer
  file={file}
  viewMode="split"
  changeIndicator="bars"
  inlineHighlight="char"
  hasChangeBackground={false}
/>

examples.label: Review comments
examples.code:
<DiffViewer
  file={file}
  onLineNumberClick={(ref) => startComment(ref.side, ref.lineNumber)}
  renderLineAnnotation={(ref) => {
    const thread = threads.get(`${ref.side}:${ref.lineNumber}`);
    return thread ? <CommentThread thread={thread} /> : null;
  }}
/>

props.name: file
props.description: The file to render: paths, status, binary flag, and hunks of numbered lines. Build it with parseUnifiedDiff or createDiffFile.

props.name: viewMode
props.description: 'unified' shows one column with removed lines above their replacements; 'split' shows the old file on the left and the new file on the right, pairing each removed line with the added line that replaced it.

props.name: language
props.description: Syntax-highlighting language: a built-in identifier, or a CodeBlock language value imported on its own (e.g. graphql from @astryxdesign/core/CodeBlock/languages/graphql) or made with createCodeLanguage. Defaults to one inferred from the file name or extension among the built-ins and codeLanguages; an unmatched file renders as plain text.

props.name: codeLanguages
props.description: Language values the file name or extension may infer, such as [graphql, dockerfile]; a later entry wins. Pass the same list to every DiffViewer on a review page.

props.name: hasLineNumbers
props.description: Show the old and new line-number gutters.

props.name: isWrapped
props.description: Wrap long lines instead of scrolling them horizontally. Unwrapped, line numbers and change indicators stay pinned while the code scrolls; in split view each side is its own scroller, the split stays fixed at half and half, and the two sides scroll sideways in lockstep. While code overflows sideways, sideways overscroll (elastic bounce, swipe navigation) is off.

props.name: changeIndicator
props.description: How changed lines are marked beside their code: 'classic' +/− glyphs, 'bars' (a solid bar for added lines, a dashed bar for removed lines), or 'none'. Screen readers hear "Added"/"Removed" in every mode.

props.name: inlineHighlight
props.description: Highlight the changed words (or characters) inside each removed line and the added line that replaced it, paired as in split view. Lines that share nothing but whitespace get no inline highlight.

props.name: hasChangeBackground
props.description: Tint the rows of added and removed lines. Without it only the change indicator, the line numbers, and the inline highlight mark a change.

props.name: isCollapsible
props.description: Make the file header a disclosure that hides and shows the hunks. Applies when the file has a path to name the control.

props.name: isCollapsed
props.description: Controlled collapsed state. Pair with onCollapsedChange.

props.name: defaultIsCollapsed
props.description: Initial collapsed state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onCollapsedChange
props.description: Called with the next collapsed state when the header is toggled.

props.name: headerEnd
props.description: Content at the end of the file header, such as a "Viewed" checkbox or a file actions menu.

props.name: renderLineAnnotation
props.description: Render content in a full-width row under a line, such as review comments; return null for lines with nothing to show. In split view the row sits under the line's own side.

props.name: onLineNumberClick
props.description: Makes each line's number a button, for example to start a comment on that line. The button is the number the line is anchored to: the original number of a removed line, and the changed-file number of an added or unchanged line (an unchanged line's original number stays plain text). Each line number is its own Tab stop.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Maximum height of the hunk area before it scrolls.

props.name: syntaxTheme
props.description: Per-instance syntax theme, as on CodeBlock. Without it the nearest SyntaxTheme or the theme syntax colors apply.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization.

docs.name: EmojiPicker
docs.description: A standalone emoji panel: a search field over every emoji by group, with your frequent emoji first. Place it inline or inside a Popover; picking an emoji calls onSelect.

usage.description: An emoji picker inserts an emoji into what the viewer is writing, such as a comment or a message. Put it in a Popover opened from an emoji button, or inline where emoji are the content. For a reaction from a short fixed set, offer the set directly.

anatomy.name: Search
anatomy.description: Matches every word of the search against the start of an emoji’s name or keywords. Enter picks the first match; Down moves into the emoji.

anatomy.name: Groups
anatomy.description: Frequently used first, then every emoji by CLDR group under a heading that stays at the top while its emoji scroll.

anatomy.name: Emoji
anatomy.description: Eight to a row, each group a grid, with one tab stop across them all. Arrow keys move through the rows and across groups, Home and End move within a row, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End jump to the first and last emoji, and Enter picks.

anatomy.name: Preview
anatomy.description: Names the emoji under the pointer or focus.

bestPractices.description: Pass the viewer’s recent emoji as `frequentEmojis`, so the ones they use most are first.
Open it from a button in a Popover and leave the Popover’s autofocus on, so typing searches right away. Inline or in a Dialog, set `hasAutoFocus` instead.
Use it for reactions with a small fixed vocabulary; offer those options directly instead.
Squeeze it below about 280 pixels wide. The rows keep eight emoji, so narrow pickers shrink every target.

accessibility.name: Emoji grids
accessibility.description: Each group is a WAI-ARIA grid named by its heading, with rows of eight cells. One roving tab stop crosses every group: Tab from the search field lands on it, and the next Tab leaves the picker. Arrow keys follow the layout and mirror in right-to-left text.

accessibility.name: Search field
accessibility.description: Down moves into the first emoji, and Up from the first row comes back. Enter picks the first match. While an input method is composing, Enter and the arrows stay with it.

accessibility.name: Emoji names
accessibility.description: Each emoji button is named by its CLDR name, such as "Party popper"; the glyph itself is hidden from assistive technology. The bundled names are English: pass `categories` and `frequentEmojis` with localized names for other languages.

accessibility.name: Focus ring
accessibility.description: The focused emoji draws the system focus ring inset, so it never overlaps a neighbor; the ring must keep 3:1 against the popover surface.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the picked emoji and its option.

props.name: frequentEmojis
props.description: Emoji listed first, under Frequently used. An empty array leaves the row out.

props.name: categories
props.description: The emoji to offer, by group. Omit it to load the bundled set (every emoji through Emoji 15, with English CLDR names) the first time a picker mounts; pass your own for a localized or custom set.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the scrolling emoji list.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Focuses the search field when the picker mounts, inline or in a Dialog. Inside a Popover, rely on the Popover’s own autofocus instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the emoji list. Defaults to the localized "Emoji".

props.name: searchLabel
props.description: Placeholder and hidden label of the search field. Defaults to the localized "Search emoji".
