props.name: children
props.description: Content to clamp: mixed inline content, nested elements, anything you would rather not wrap in a single Text.

props.name: maxLines
props.description: Maximum number of lines to show before clamping with an ellipsis.

props.name: hasTruncateTooltip
props.description: Show a tooltip with the full text content on hover or keyboard focus when clamped. A clamped root is focusable (tabindex 0) so keyboard users can reach the tooltip; a tabIndex you pass wins. The tooltip props follow Text's: when Text's hasTruncateTooltip is renamed in a minor, LineClamp follows.

props.name: truncateTooltipPlacement
props.description: Where the truncation tooltip opens.

props.name: as
props.description: HTML element to render.

usage.description: Clamps arbitrary content to a fixed number of lines with an ellipsis. Text's maxLines clamps a Text element; LineClamp clamps whatever it wraps and adds no typography of its own, so it suits mixed inline content and nested elements without changing their font, color or wrapping. Truncation detection reuses useTruncation (the same hook Text uses), so overflow is measured correctly even while -webkit-line-clamp clips scrollHeight.

bestPractices.description: Use LineClamp when clamping a block of mixed or composed content (not a single Text node).
Use Text's own maxLines prop when clamping a single Text node — no need to wrap it in LineClamp.
Disable the tooltip (hasTruncateTooltip={false}) when the clamped content is already reachable elsewhere on the page, to avoid a redundant announcement.

LineClamp makes a focusable descendant inert only when both hold: (1) it is in the clamp's own flow. A positioned element is in that flow when its containing block is an element inside the clamp that is itself in the flow, as a control's own positioned wrapper is; the line test then applies to that containing block's box. A fixed element, an absolute element whose containing block is the clamp itself or lies outside it, a top-layer element (a popover or dialog), and anything rendered elsewhere through a portal each start a subtree that is never made inert, at any depth. (2) its box lies wholly beyond the clamp's last visible line. A control any part of which is visible stays reachable. A focusable with no box when LineClamp checks is treated as beyond the last line until it gains a box; LineClamp re-checks then. LineClamp re-checks when its size, its content or its fonts change. Gap: an absolutely placed control that the clamp itself clips stays a tab stop; the author owns positioned content inside a clamp. Inert takes such a control out of the Tab order and the accessibility tree. LineClamp never rewrites your own tabIndex or aria-hidden, and the element that holds focus is never made inert.

docsDense.description: Clamps arbitrary content to N lines with an ellipsis; composable version of Text maxLines.

usage.description: Wrap any children (mixed inline content, nested elements) to clamp the whole block to N lines. Reuses useTruncation for overflow detection.

bestPractices.description: Use for clamping a block of mixed/composed content, not a single Text node.
Use Text's own maxLines for a single Text node instead.
Disable tooltip when content is reachable elsewhere, to avoid redundant announcement.

Inert only for a focusable in the clamp's own flow whose box lies wholly past the last visible line (a positioned element placed against an in-flow containing block in the clamp, like a control's own wrapper, is in the flow and judged by that block's box); never inside a fixed, escaping absolute, top-layer or portaled subtree; a partly visible control stays reachable; a focusable with no box counts as past the last line until it gains a box; re-checked on size, content and font changes. Gap: an absolutely placed control the clamp clips stays a tab stop. Never the focused element, never your own tabIndex or aria-hidden.

propDescriptions.children: Content to clamp. Composable version of maxLines — wraps arbitrary children.
propDescriptions.maxLines: Max lines before clamping with ellipsis.
propDescriptions.hasTruncateTooltip: Tooltip with full text on hover or focus when clamped. Clamped root is focusable. Follows Text's prop name.

props.name: children
props.description: 要截断的内容。LineClamp 包裹任意子节点（混合内联内容、嵌套元素）并截断整个区块，而不是单个 Text 组件。

props.name: maxLines
props.description: 截断前显示的最大行数。

props.name: hasTruncateTooltip
props.description: 截断时在悬停或键盘聚焦时显示完整文本的工具提示；被截断的根元素可聚焦（tabindex 0），你传入的 tabIndex 优先。工具提示相关属性与 Text 保持一致：Text 的 hasTruncateTooltip 在次版本中改名时，LineClamp 随之改名。

props.name: truncateTooltipPlacement
props.description: 截断工具提示的打开位置。

props.name: as
props.description: 要渲染的 HTML 元素。

usage.description: 将任意内容截断为固定行数并显示省略号。Text 的 maxLines 截断 Text 组件自身的内容；LineClamp 是可组合版本 —— 用它包裹任意子节点（混合内联内容、嵌套元素）即可将整个区块截断为 N 行。

bestPractices.description: 当需要截断混合或组合内容（而非单个 Text 节点）时使用 LineClamp。
截断单个 Text 节点时使用 Text 自身的 maxLines 属性，无需用 LineClamp 包裹。
当截断内容已在页面其他位置可访问时，禁用工具提示（hasTruncateTooltip={false}）以避免重复播报。

只有同时满足以下两点时，LineClamp 才会把可聚焦的后代设为 inert：(1) 它在截断容器自己的文档流中。若定位元素的包含块是容器内同样处于文档流中的元素（例如控件自己的定位包装元素），该定位元素也算在文档流中，此时按该包含块的盒子判断是否越过最后一行。fixed 元素、包含块是容器本身或位于容器之外的 absolute 元素、顶层元素（popover 或 dialog），以及通过 portal 渲染到别处的内容，各自开启一个无论多深都不会被设为 inert 的子树。(2) 它的盒子完全位于最后一个可见行之外。只要有一部分可见，控件就保持可达。检查时没有盒子的可聚焦元素会被视为位于最后一行之外，直到它获得盒子；届时 LineClamp 会重新检查。LineClamp 会在尺寸、内容或字体变化时重新检查。已知缺口：被容器本身截断的绝对定位控件仍是一个 Tab 停靠点；容器内的定位内容由作者负责。LineClamp 不会改写你自己设置的 tabIndex 或 aria-hidden，持有焦点的元素也不会被设为 inert。

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label that names the collection. It also provides the accessible name for the complete input.

props.name: value
props.description: Current ordered records. ListInput is controlled and never mutates this array or its records.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the next array after an add, update, or remove action. The change argument identifies the action and affected record. Moves go to the reorderable object instead.

props.name: getItemKey
props.description: Returns a stable, unique key for each record. Stable identity preserves focus and announcements when records move.

props.name: createItem
props.description: Creates the initial record inserted by the built-in add action. Return a new record with its stable key already assigned.

props.name: columns
props.description: Consistent simple fields shown for every record. Use each column width with proportional() or pixel() from @astryxdesign/core/Table to tune the width spread. ListInput owns the visible primary-tone column labels while renderer labels remain semantically available to assistive technology. At 640px or narrower, fields stack, every record shows its field labels, record groups use 32px vertical separation, and row actions align beside the first field. Renderers receive isLabelHidden, complete scoped validation status, statusVariant, and updateItem.

props.name: itemName
props.description: Singular noun used in built-in action labels and live announcements, such as "guest" in "Add guest".

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting text displayed between the collection label and its records.

props.name: status
props.description: List-level validation status displayed for the complete collection. An error marks the collection invalid and associates its message with the input.

props.name: getItemStatus
props.description: Returns validation status for a complete record, such as an invalid combination of otherwise valid fields.

props.name: getFieldStatus
props.type: (item: T, columnKey: string, index: number) => InputStatus | undefined
props.description: Returns validation status for one field. The renderer receives the complete status plus statusVariant="tooltip" and should forward both to its Astryx input so the native status affordance owns styling, description, keyboard access, and tooltip behavior without changing row height.

props.name: reorderable
props.description: Makes the records reorderable: pass the object createReorderable makes, keyed by getItemKey. Each record ends with core List's reorder handle, after Remove, as UIKit's reorder control ends an editing row. The handle appears while the record is hovered or holds keyboard focus and stays visible on touch screens. On a touch screen, hold the handle for a moment, then drag: the record stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other records stay still, the list autoscrolls near its edges, and on release the records rearrange. A flick on the handle scrolls and a pinch zooms the page. A mouse drags at once the same way, and the records take their places without motion. Activating the handle (a tap, a click, Space or Enter) turns on reorder mode for its record: the line marks the record's place, each Arrow Up or Arrow Down moves it a place, a hint shows the moves and Done as buttons, and Escape or Done ends the mode, keeping the moves. The object's isReorderable(key) says which records move: one it rejects has no handle. Each move goes to the object's onReorder({key, to}), to being the record's index in value after the move. In a disabled or loading list the handles stay focusable but move nothing. Without it, the records keep their order.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the collection and all built-in actions. The disabled state is also passed to each column renderer.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Marks the collection busy and prevents changes while work is pending. The loading state is also passed to each column renderer.

props.name: maxItems
props.description: Maximum number of records that can be added. Once the value reaches this limit, the built-in add action is unavailable.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the collection label while keeping it available to assistive technology.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Displays an optional indicator beside the collection label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Displays a required indicator beside the collection label and exposes the requirement to assistive technology. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

usage.description: ListInput edits a compact, ordered collection of records with consistent fields, built-in add and remove actions, and optional reordering. Standard Astryx controls rendered in its columns inherit the medium control size so inputs align with the Add, remove, reorder, and validation affordances; an explicit field size still takes precedence. Pointer activation measures Add before pointer-down blur or validation can change layout, then keeps it at that viewport position by adjusting available vertical scroll containers from nearest to outermost. The correction is interaction-scoped and rechecked for one animation frame without persistent scroll or resize observation. Added rows enter with tokenized translate motion; after removal, surviving rows animate into their new positions when their geometry stays stable. Motion never delays onChange, focus handoff, or the announcement, while reduced-motion preferences and unsupported browsers use an instant change. Use it for lists with fewer than seven records and up to three simple fields per record, such as guests, travelers, or tag options. Use a Table for larger collections and a card or step-based form when records need many, complex, or inconsistent fields.

bestPractices.description: Use stable record keys and consistent columns so focus, validation, and reorder announcements remain attached to the correct record.
Keep validation timing application-owned. Track touched fields by stable item and column keys when errors should appear after blur, while allowing submit or server errors to display immediately.
Place validation at the narrowest useful level: field status for one value, item status for a record-wide problem, and list status for collection-wide requirements.
Forward both status and statusVariant from every column renderer to the rendered Astryx input so field messages use the control's native accessible tooltip pattern.
Let records reorder through the handle: a drag reports one move on release, each key move in reorder mode reports one at once, and focus stays on the handle.

Keep collection motion informational and non-blocking. Added live rows translate into place; removed rows disappear immediately while stable-size survivors close the gap. onChange, focus, and announcements run without waiting, and reduced-motion preferences remain instant.

Keep repeated pointer adding spatially stable by measuring Add before pointer-down blur or validation changes layout, then preserving that viewport position from the nearest vertical scroll container outward. Slight field clipping should not move Add away from the pointer; a meaningfully hidden focused field still takes priority. Keyboard activation follows the normal focus flow.
Use for seven or more records or more than three simple fields per record; use a Table or a dedicated editing flow instead.
Prevent removal solely to enforce a minimum count; allow the action and explain the resulting requirement with list-level validation.

anatomy.name: Label and description
anatomy.description: Names the complete collection and optionally explains what records to add.

anatomy.name: First-record field labels
anatomy.description: ListInput renders primary-tone column labels without separate table chrome and keeps each rendered control's own label visually hidden but semantically associated. At wider widths, repeated labels are visually hidden; when fields stack at 640px or narrower, every record shows its field labels.

anatomy.name: Record fields
anatomy.description: Consumer-rendered inputs that receive scoped record state, complete validation status, the native tooltip status variant, and update behavior. When stacked responsively, label-to-input spacing is smallest, field spacing is larger, and record groups use 32px separation so each object remains visually distinct.

anatomy.name: Remove action
anatomy.description: Removes its record immediately, moves focus to a predictable neighboring control, and animates surviving rows into their new positions when supported. It is revealed while the record is hovered or contains keyboard focus and stays visible on touch screens; at rest it is transparent but keeps its column and its place in the tab order, so the fields never shift. In the stacked layout, it aligns beside the first field at the top of the record.

anatomy.name: Reorder handle
anatomy.description: Core List's reorder handle, three lines at the end of the record after Remove, in Remove's cell, with an accessible label naming the record and its position and no hover tooltip. Where the primary pointer is coarse, its target grows to at least 44 by 44 px. It is revealed while the record is hovered or contains keyboard focus and stays visible on touch screens; at rest it is transparent but stays in the tab order. In the stacked layout it sits at the top of the record beside Remove. A finger holds it a moment, then drags; a mouse drags at once; activating it (Space or Enter) turns on reorder mode, where Arrow Up and Arrow Down move the record a place and Escape ends the mode.

anatomy.name: Reorder-mode hint
anatomy.description: While a record is in reorder mode, core List's hint anchored to its handle shows the moves and Done as buttons, so taps alone can reorder. Each does what its key does and leaves the focus on the handle.

anatomy.name: Empty state
anatomy.description: When no records exist, a centered compact EmptyState names the empty collection and directs users to the Add action.

anatomy.name: Add action
anatomy.description: Fills the record-fields width, uses the inherited medium control size shared by ListInput fields and actions, and immediately appends a new record created by createItem unless maxItems has been reached. On pointer activation, available vertical scroll containers offset the inserted height from nearest to outermost so the action remains under the pointer; keyboard activation keeps the normal focus behavior, and newly focused field visibility always wins. The live row uses tokenized translate entrance motion when supported, and focus moves to its first field without waiting for the animation.

anatomy.name: Validation messages
anatomy.description: Explain field-, item-, or list-level errors, warnings, and success states. Field messages use each input's native tooltip status affordance and do not change row height. Item messages align to the record fields without extending under the remove control.

docsDense.description: Controlled compact-record input with typed columns, tokenized non-blocking add/remove motion, optional reorder, and field/item/list validation.

propDescriptions.label: Collection label and accessible name.
propDescriptions.onChange: Emits next records plus add/update/remove metadata.
propDescriptions.createItem: Creates a new keyed record for Add.
propDescriptions.columns: Typed simple fields: key, header, optional proportional/pixel width, and renderInput. ListInput owns visible column labels; narrow records stack with repeated labels, stronger separation, and top-aligned row actions. Renderers forward status and statusVariant.
propDescriptions.itemName: Singular noun for actions and announcements.
propDescriptions.status: List-level InputStatus.
propDescriptions.getFieldStatus: Per-field resolver; complete status plus tooltip variant are forwarded to the rendered input.
propDescriptions.reorderable: createReorderable object keyed by getItemKey: core List's reorder handle at each record's end (after Remove), revealed on hover/focus, shown on touch: hold then drag (touch), drag (mouse), activate for reorder mode then arrows (keys), with a hint showing the moves and Done; the record dims while a copy follows and a line marks the drop, the other records stay still; each move goes to the object's onReorder({key, to}); its isReorderable keeps a record in place; handles stay focusable but inert while disabled or loading.
propDescriptions.isDisabled: Disables collection, actions, and rendered inputs.
propDescriptions.maxItems: Makes Add unavailable at the limit.
propDescriptions.isLabelHidden: Visually hides label only.
propDescriptions.isRequired: Shows Required + accessible requirement; exclusive with isOptional.

usage.description: Use for compact ordered records: fewer than 7 items and up to 3 simple consistent fields. Add/remove motion does not delay onChange or focus and becomes instant under reduced motion. Use Table or a dedicated flow for larger or complex data.

bestPractices.description: Use stable keys and consistent columns.
Validate at field, item, or list scope as appropriate.
Reorder through the handle; one onReorder call per drop or key move, and no onChange; focus stays on the handle.
Keep add/remove motion non-blocking and instant under reduced motion.
Use for long datasets or complex/inconsistent records.
Block removal to enforce a minimum; report a list error instead.

usage.description: Experimental streaming log viewer: mono grid rows (timestamp | level | source | message) with token-derived level accents, expandable per-row detail panels, follow-scroll live tailing with a "Jump to latest" affordance, and an always-dark terminal variant. In the default variant, warning and error labels use their plain-surface status foreground roles. Appended rows fade in via @starting-style. Live announcements follow the pinning state: the role="log" region is aria-live="polite" only while following the tail, and aria-live="off" while unfollowed, so a busy stream never floods assistive tech.

props.name: entries
props.description: Array of log entry objects to render.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant style: 'default' uses theme surface background, 'terminal' uses fixed dark background.

props.name: isFollowing
props.description: Controlled follow-pinning state to auto-scroll to the newest entry.

props.name: onFollowChange
props.description: Callback fired when follow-pinning state changes.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Maximum container height before vertical scrolling.

props.name: hasTimestamps
props.description: Show or hide the timestamp column.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the log region.

props.name: renderEntry
props.description: Custom render function for replacing individual row layout.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization.

docs.name: NavigationStack
docs.description: Drill-down navigation for phone layouts: each screen pushes the next on top, and Back, the back swipe from the screen edge or from anywhere in the content returns to the previous one. Pushes, pops and the back swipe move like iOS: the new screen slides in from the trailing edge over the old one, which slides a third as far under a light dimming, and a released swipe finishes or springs back depending on how far and how fast it went. A push never waits for its animation: the new screen is usable as soon as it starts sliding in. With Reduce Motion the screens cross-fade instead. Experimental: lands in lab first.

components.name: NavigationStack
components.description: The navigator. You own the path: pass the entries pushed on the root screen and update them in onPathChange. The stack renders the root screen and one screen per entry, the top one last, keeps covered screens and their scroll positions alive, and makes them inert. The bar shows the top screen's title, its end content and a round Back button with a chevron, named by the screen it returns to. A push moves focus to the new screen's title; a pop returns it to the control that pushed the screen. Under a finger the bar paints no background and no hairline, as iOS 26's does. Once a screen's content has moved 10px under the bar, a veil of the body colour fades in at the top of that screen. Each screen keeps its own veil through a push, a pop or a back swipe. With a mouse the bar keeps its surface and hairline.

props.name: root
props.description: The root screen, a NavigationScreen. It has no Back button.

props.name: path
props.description: The entries pushed on the root, bottom first. Adding one at the end pushes its screen; removing the last pops it; removing several pops straight back to the new top.

props.name: onPathChange
props.description: Called with the new path when a screen pushes or pops (useNavigationStack), Back is pressed, or a back swipe is released past the point of no return.

props.name: renderScreen
props.description: Renders the screen for an entry: a NavigationScreen.

props.name: getKey
props.description: A stable key per entry, so a screen keeps its state while others are pushed on it. Defaults to the entry's position.

props.name: isInteractivePopEnabled
props.description: Whether the back swipe pops: a sideways drag anywhere in the content, under any pointer (a finger, a pen or a mouse drag), and in a web app opened from the home screen also a finger's swipe from the leading screen edge. In a browser tab that edge stays the browser's own back swipe, and on Android the system back owns both screen edges.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigator region.

components.name: NavigationScreen
components.description: One screen of a NavigationStack: its title, the title Back shows on the screen pushed after it, its end content and its content. Returned by NavigationStack's root and renderScreen; it renders nothing on its own.

props.name: title
props.description: Shown in the bar while the screen is on top, and read first when it arrives.

props.name: backTitle
props.description: What Back reads on the screen pushed on top of this one. Defaults to title.

props.name: titleDisplayMode
props.description: How the title shows. 'large' puts it above the content in a large bold type, scrolling with the content; once it has scrolled under the bar, the bar shows the title instead. Use it for a top-level screen, as iOS does.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content at the end of the bar while the screen is on top.

props.name: children
props.description: The screen's content. It scrolls on its own and keeps its scroll position while covered.

usage.description: Use NavigationStack for hierarchical drill-down on phones: lists of settings, folders, a list and its detail. Call push from a row with useNavigationStack inside a screen.

bestPractices.description: Keep the path in the app's state (or the URL) and give entries stable keys, so screens keep their state as the stack changes.
Push from the control the person activated (a row's onClick): focus returns to it when the screen is popped.
Don't use it for top-level sections that people switch between; those are tabs or a sidebar, which keep each section's own stack.

docs.name: PageControl
docs.description: A row of page indicators under a paging view, as on iOS: one dot per page, the current one highlighted. A tap or a click to either side of the current dot moves one page that way, and sliding a finger or dragging the mouse across the dots scrubs straight to the page under it. Under a finger (any touch device, iOS and Android alike), with more than ten pages the row is a window whose edge dots shrink to show there is more, and a held finger shows a platter behind the dots; with a mouse a long row is cropped to the control. Experimental: lands in lab first.

props.name: totalPages
props.description: Number of pages.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page number (1-based). Page 1 is the first page.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the page, 1-based, that a tap, a click, a scrub, an arrow key, Home, End or an assistive technology asks for; a scrub calls it each time the page under the pointer changes, so a quick sweep can skip a page. Update the paging view and page together.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the control for assistive technology. Defaults to "Page indicators", localized.

props.name: hidesForSinglePage
props.description: Render nothing when there is only one page.

usage.description: Use PageControl below a paging view, such as a Carousel with `hasSnap` or onboarding screens, to show how many pages there are and which one is showing. Keep its page in step with the view in both directions.

bestPractices.description: Pair it with a view that pages by swipe: the control is a secondary way to move and the main way to see where you are.
Keep pages few enough to count at a glance; past ten the row stays a fixed width, shows a window of them and scrolls as the page changes.
Don't use it for long lists of results (use Pagination) or for choosing between views (use SegmentedControl or TabList).

usage.description: Schedule is a calendar surface that renders events as a month grid, a day or week time grid, or a list grouped by day: the layout comes from a view object you pass in. It handles timezone-aware date math, paging between ranges, and async event loading, and exposes header slots that plugins fill with navigation controls. Use it to display an existing schedule; build the week, day, or month view with renderPopover to let people open an event's details in a popover the view manages. It has no event selection, creation, or editing affordances.

bestPractices.description: Hold the rendered date in state and wire onChangeDate to it. Schedule never advances the date itself, so without that handler the built-in previous/Today/next controls render but nothing moves.
Match the view to the density of the data: a month grid for at-a-glance load, a day or week time grid when start and end times matter, a list when the schedule is sparse.

Wrap Schedule in InternationalizationProvider to choose the language, numbering, and field order used by its date and time labels; the provider calendar, such as calendar="persian", writes those labels in another calendar. Schedule date values, its grids, and its date navigation stay Gregorian in every calendar and locale.
Give each event a category string that matches a categories entry so its color is meaningful and screen readers announce the category name. An unmatched name still renders, but always in blue.
Reach for Schedule when the user has to pick a date. It has no selection model; use DateInput, DateRangeInput, or Calendar instead.
Rely on event color alone to carry meaning. Only ten colors exist, so they repeat on larger category sets; the accessible label already announces title, category, and time.

When your page already pages the range with its own controls, keep date in your state and pass plugins={[]}: Schedule then renders the range title with no controls of its own, and your controls call the same setter as onChangeDate.
Pass a custom plugins array without useSchedulePaginationPlugin when you still want Schedule's previous, Today, and next controls; a custom array replaces the default set rather than extending it.

anatomy.name: Header start slot
anatomy.description: Leading header region filled by plugins. The default plugin set renders a previous / Today / next button group here.

anatomy.name: Header title
anatomy.description: A level-2 heading naming the range on screen, e.g. "May 2026". The same text is the accessible name of the schedule region.

anatomy.name: Loading spinner
anatomy.description: Sits beside the title while an async events loader is still pending, labelled "Loading events".

anatomy.name: Header end slot
anatomy.description: Trailing header region, empty by default. The view selector plugin renders its menu here.

anatomy.name: View body
anatomy.description: Whatever the view renders: a month grid, a day/week time grid with an hour gutter and an all-day row, or a list grouped under day headings. Grid views expose ARIA grid, columnheader, and gridcell roles and are marked aria-readonly. The day/week time grid scrolls inside one keyboard-reachable region named after the range; its day header, all-day row, and hour gutter stay pinned while the columns scroll. The all-day row also holds timed events that last 24 hours or more, as one span across their days.

anatomy.name: Event
anatomy.description: One pill (grid views) or row with a color dot (list view) per event, tinted by its category and dimmed once it is in the past. In the day and week grids, events that happen at the same time share the column side by side, and when the view is built with renderPopover each event with content is a button that opens the view's popover. In the month grid a week row shows at most three levels of chips; a busy day shows two and a "+N more" button that opens a popover listing every event of that day. A month chip leads with the title; the start time of a timed event follows it only when both fit. When the month view is built with renderPopover, each chip with content is a button that opens the same popover as its day's "+N more", and each later day a chip covers names its event for screen readers.

anatomy.name: Current time line
anatomy.description: A line across the day or week time grid at the current time, on the current day only. It ticks once a minute and is absent during server rendering. When the rendered range includes today, the grid opens scrolled to one hour before this line (clamped to the grid) once per range, and then leaves the scroll position alone until the person pages to another range or switches views.

props.name: view
props.description: The view object that owns the layout and the date range each page covers. Build one with createScheduleMonthlyView, createScheduleWeeklyView, createScheduleDayView, or createScheduleListView; each factory takes its own options (weekStartsOn, minHour/maxHour/hourHeight, days). The week, day, and month factories also take renderPopover(event): return the content for an event and the view renders that event as a button that opens a popover it manages — one popover for the view, named by the event title, with the system's standard surface, padding, Escape and light dismiss, and focus return; return null to leave an event read-only. In the month view that popover also shows a busy day's list, and a row in the list opens its event in place. The list view has no interaction option.

props.name: events
props.description: Either a static array, filtered to the events overlapping the rendered range and sorted by start, or a loader called with that range's start and end epoch milliseconds. A loader suspends while pending; the header shows a spinner and the view renders empty. Results are cached per loader identity and range, so keep the loader reference stable (useCallback) or every re-render refetches. When your page already holds the events, pass them as an array; Schedule picks out each range's events without a loader.

props.name: categories
props.description: Category definitions matched to each event by label === event.category. The match supplies the event's color and the category name in its accessible label. An event whose category names no entry keeps that name but falls back to blue; an event with no category is announced as "Event" in blue. A category can stand for any grouping you color by — an event kind, a calendar, or a team; to color events by calendar, give each calendar its own entry.

props.name: date
props.description: Unix epoch milliseconds anywhere inside the range to render; the view expands it to a full month, week, day, or list window. Fully controlled; Schedule never changes it, so pair it with onChangeDate.

props.name: focusDate
props.description: Unix epoch milliseconds marking the day treated as "today": in the month, week, and day views that cell gets aria-current="date" and the highlighted styling. The list view ignores it. When omitted it is captured once at mount and never advances afterwards.

props.name: onChangeDate
props.description: Called with the epoch milliseconds to render next when a pagination plugin pages backward or forward, or when Today is pressed. Paging preserves the time of day; Today passes the current time.

props.name: timezoneID
props.description: IANA timezone ID (e.g. "America/Los_Angeles") used for every date calculation and every formatted label, so the same events regroup across days when it changes.

props.name: plugins
props.description: Header plugins, applied in order; each may wrap or replace the start, center, and end header content. Supplying an array replaces the default pagination controls; compose useSchedulePaginationPlugin and useScheduleViewSelectorPlugin to keep both.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level for sub-headings inside the schedule (the weekday and day column headers in the grid views, and the day headings in the list view), so the schedule nests correctly under the surrounding page outline. The header range title is always a level-2 heading.

docs.name: SelectableCardGroup
docs.description: A set of selectable cards with the semantics of its selection. One choice (the default) is a radio group: the cards are native radios sharing one name, so the set is one tab stop, the arrow keys move and select, and screen readers speak the position ("2 of 3"). Several choices are a named group of checkboxes. Each SelectableCardGroupItem is a SelectableCard whose input, name and selection come from the group.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's visible label and accessible name.

props.name: selectionMode
props.description: `single`: a radio group with one value. `multiple`: a group of checkboxes with any number of values.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen value (`single`, `null` while none is chosen) or values (`multiple`).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the chosen value (`single`) or the new list of values (`multiple`).

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Hides the label visually; it still names the group.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text under the label, linked to the group.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The name the group's value is submitted under. The radios group by a generated name. Defaults to a generated one.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables every card; they stay focusable and announce disabled.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` wraps the cards in rows; `vertical` stacks them.

props.name: children
props.description: SelectableCardGroupItem cards. Each takes a `value` and the SelectableCard props other than isSelected and onChange.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the Field box around the label, description and cards (margins, positioning, sizing). The group composes Field, so it takes no root xstyle, className or style.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the Field box. Same targeting as containerXstyle.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the Field box. Same targeting as containerXstyle.

usage.description: Use it for a choice among a few rich options shown as cards: a plan, an appearance, a layout. One choice gives users the radio-group keyboard and the position they expect; use `multiple` when several cards can be on.

bestPractices.description: Give every card a `label` that names its option; it is the radio or checkbox name screen readers speak.
Start a single choice with a value when the product has a sensible default, so the tab stop lands on it.
Put buttons or links inside the cards; the whole card is the radio or checkbox target.
Use it for navigation or actions; use ClickableCard for those.

docsZh.name: SelectableCardGroup
docsZh.description: 一组可选卡片，语义与其选择方式一致。单选（默认）是一个单选按钮组：卡片是共享同一 name 的原生单选按钮，因此整组只占一个 Tab 停靠点，方向键移动并选中，读屏软件会读出位置（“第 2 项，共 3 项”）。多选是一个带名称的复选框组。每个 SelectableCardGroupItem 都是一个 SelectableCard，其输入类型、name 和选中状态由组提供。

props.name: label
props.description: 组的可见标签和无障碍名称。

props.name: selectionMode
props.description: `single`：单选按钮组，一个值。`multiple`：复选框组，任意多个值。

props.name: value
props.description: 选中的值（`single`，未选择时为 `null`）或值列表（`multiple`）。

props.name: onChange
props.description: 以选中的值（`single`）或新的值列表（`multiple`）调用。

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: 在视觉上隐藏标签；它仍为组命名。

props.name: description
props.description: 标签下方的辅助文字，并与组关联。

props.name: htmlName
props.description: 提交组的值时使用的名称。单选按钮按自动生成的名称分组。默认自动生成。

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: 禁用所有卡片；它们仍可聚焦，并读出禁用状态。

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` 将卡片按行换行排列；`vertical` 纵向堆叠。

props.name: children
props.description: SelectableCardGroupItem 卡片。每张卡片接受一个 `value`，以及除 isSelected 和 onChange 之外的 SelectableCard 属性。

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: 作用于标签、描述和卡片外层 Field 容器的 StyleX 样式（外边距、定位、尺寸）。该组由 Field 组成，因此不接受根级 xstyle、className 或 style。

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Field 容器的类名，作用范围与 containerXstyle 相同。

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Field 容器的内联样式，作用范围与 containerXstyle 相同。

usage.description: 用于在少数以卡片呈现的丰富选项中做选择：套餐、外观、布局。单选为用户提供他们预期的单选按钮组键盘操作和位置播报；当可以同时开启多张卡片时，使用 `multiple`。

bestPractices.description: 为每张卡片提供一个说明其选项的 `label`；它就是读屏软件读出的单选按钮或复选框名称。
当产品有合理的默认值时，让单选从一个值开始，这样 Tab 停靠点会落在它上面。
在卡片内放置按钮或链接；整张卡片都是单选按钮或复选框的目标。
用于导航或操作；这些场景请使用 ClickableCard。

props.name: label
props.description: Metric name shown above the value, e.g. "Total requests".

props.name: value
props.description: Headline metric rendered large with tabular numerals. Pass a pre-formatted string like "1.2M".

props.name: delta
props.description: Change indicator next to the value: an up/down/flat glyph plus colored text. sentiment overrides the direction color mapping (up=positive, down=negative, flat=neutral) for inverted metrics like error rate.

props.name: description
props.description: Muted supporting line under the value, e.g. "vs. previous 30 days".

props.name: media
props.description: Trend slot rendered below the text content, e.g. a sparkline or mini chart. Stat does not render a chart itself.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant controlling the value's font size.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

usage.description: A KPI/metric display for dashboards and summary rows: metric name, large tabular-nums value, an optional sentiment-aware delta, a supporting description, and a media slot for a sparkline or mini chart. Compose several in a Grid for a KPI row.

bestPractices.description: Pass pre-formatted strings for value and delta ("1.2M", "+12.4%"); Stat does not format numbers.
Set `sentiment` explicitly for inverted metrics where down is good, like error rate or latency.
Wrap Stat in a Card and lay out KPI rows with Grid columns={{minWidth: 240, max: 4}}.
Put a full-size chart in the media slot; it is meant for compact sparklines or trend glyphs.
Rely on delta color alone to convey meaning; the direction glyph and screen-reader text carry it too.

docsDense.description: KPI/metric display: label, large tabular-nums value, sentiment-aware delta, and trend media slot.

usage.description: A KPI/metric display for dashboards and summary rows: metric name, large tabular-nums value, an optional sentiment-aware delta, a supporting description, and a media slot for a sparkline or mini chart. Compose several in a Grid for a KPI row.

bestPractices.description: Pass pre-formatted strings for value and delta ("1.2M", "+12.4%"); Stat does not format numbers.
Set `sentiment` explicitly for inverted metrics where down is good, like error rate or latency.
Wrap Stat in a Card and lay out KPI rows with Grid columns={{minWidth: 240, max: 4}}.
Put a full-size chart in the media slot; it is meant for compact sparklines or trend glyphs.
Rely on delta color alone to convey meaning; the direction glyph and screen-reader text carry it too.

propDescriptions.label: Metric name above the value.
propDescriptions.delta: Direction glyph + colored change text; sentiment overrides direction colors.
propDescriptions.description: Muted supporting line under the value.
propDescriptions.media: Trend slot below the text (sparkline/mini chart).
propDescriptions.xstyle: StyleX layout styles; must be stylex.create() value.

props.name: label
props.description: 显示在数值上方的指标名称，例如 "Total requests"。

props.name: value
props.description: 大号显示的核心指标，使用等宽数字。请传入预先格式化的字符串，如 "1.2M"。

props.name: delta
props.description: 数值旁的变化指示：上升/下降/持平图标加彩色文本。sentiment 可覆盖默认的方向颜色映射（up=positive、down=negative、flat=neutral），用于错误率等反向指标。

props.name: description
props.description: 数值下方的弱化辅助说明，例如 "vs. previous 30 days"。

props.name: media
props.description: 渲染在文本内容下方的趋势插槽，例如迷你折线图。Stat 本身不渲染图表。

props.name: size
props.description: 控制数值字号的尺寸变体。

props.name: xstyle
props.description: 用于布局自定义的 StyleX 样式（外边距、定位、尺寸）。必须是 stylex.create() 的值，而非内联样式对象如 style={{}}。

usage.description: A KPI/metric display for dashboards and summary rows: metric name, large tabular-nums value, an optional sentiment-aware delta, a supporting description, and a media slot for a sparkline or mini chart. Compose several in a Grid for a KPI row.

bestPractices.description: Pass pre-formatted strings for value and delta ("1.2M", "+12.4%"); Stat does not format numbers.
Set `sentiment` explicitly for inverted metrics where down is good, like error rate or latency.
Wrap Stat in a Card and lay out KPI rows with Grid columns={{minWidth: 240, max: 4}}.
Put a full-size chart in the media slot; it is meant for compact sparklines or trend glyphs.
Rely on delta color alone to convey meaning; the direction glyph and screen-reader text carry it too.

docs.name: TabBar
docs.description: The bottom tab bar of a phone app, as on iOS 26: the app's top-level sections as a floating capsule above the bottom edge, with a selection lens that slides to the chosen tab. Each tab has an icon, a label and an optional badge. Under a finger, on iOS and Android alike, it behaves like iOS 26's: the lens lifts into glass as a finger lands, follows a finger dragged across the tabs and settles on the tab nearest where it lifts, while the bar flexes; under a mouse, a press is a plain button press: a click chooses a tab and the lens follows the theme's motion. With no tab selected, a held finger highlights the tab under it. Choosing the selected tab again is reported separately, so a screen can return to its root as iOS does. Experimental: lands in lab first.

components.name: TabBar
components.description: The bar. It sits fixed at the bottom of the viewport, over the page, so leave 83 px of room at the bottom of the scrolling content, and declare it on LayerProvider (inset={{blockEnd: 83}}) so menus, popovers and toasts clear it. You own the selection: pass the selected tab's value and update it in onChange.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected tab's value.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with a tab's value when a different tab is chosen: a finger lifted over it (after a tap or a drag across the bar), a click, or Enter or Space on a focused tab.

props.name: onReselect
props.description: Called with the selected tab's value when it is chosen again, for example to return the tab's navigation stack to its root, as iOS does.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the tab bar for assistive technology. Without it, or aria-label or aria-labelledby (which win over it and reach the tab list), the tab list is named "Tabs" in the reader's language.

props.name: children
props.description: The tabs: TabBarItem elements, in order, as direct children.

components.name: TabBarItem
components.description: One tab: its value, label, icon and badge. TabBar reads its props and draws it; it renders nothing on its own.

props.name: value
props.description: Identifies the tab in value, onChange and onReselect.

props.name: label
props.description: The tab's name, shown under its icon. Keep it to one short word.

props.name: icon
props.description: The tab's icon, an Icon at size lg. It is drawn in the current text colour, and in the accent colour while selected.

props.name: selectedIcon
props.description: The icon while the tab is selected, typically its filled variant. Defaults to icon.

props.name: badge
props.description: A badge over the icon's top-trailing corner: a count or a short string such as "!". It appears, changes and disappears without animating. Omit it or pass an empty string for none.

props.name: badgeLabel
props.description: What assistive technology reads for the badge after the tab's label, such as "3 unread". Defaults to the badge itself.

props.name: panelId
props.description: Id of the panel this tab controls, wired up as aria-controls. Put the same id on the section's panel element.

props.name: aria-disabled
props.description: Disables the tab, as on Core's Tab: it stays focusable but dimmed and is never chosen. A tap, a click or a key on it, or a lift over it, selects nothing, and the arrow keys skip it. A finger that lands on it lifts no lens until it drags or reaches an enabled tab, which the lift then chooses. This differs from iOS on purpose. iOS ignores a touch that starts on a disabled tab, but TabBar follows the action-group rule: the tab you lift on acts.

usage.description: Use TabBar to switch between an app's three to five top-level sections on a phone, each keeping its own state and navigation stack. Keep each section's navigation stack in the app and return it to its root in onReselect.

bestPractices.description: Keep every tab visible and the set stable; give each a short label and an outline icon with a filled selectedIcon.
Use a badge for something that needs attention in that section, such as unread items, and say what it counts in badgeLabel.
Give each tab a panelId naming its section's panel, so assistive technology can associate the two.
Disable a tab only while its section cannot open, and keep it in place, so the other tabs do not move.
Don't use it for actions, for filters within one screen (use SegmentedControl) or for tabs inside a page (use TabList).

docs.name: Tour
docs.description: A guided product tour (NUX / onboarding). Tour is a controller that steps a user through a sequence of spotlight callouts anchored to elements on the page. It renders no chrome itself; it owns the active-step state and shares it with declaratively-nested TourStep children (step order follows the children). Experimental: lands in lab first (meta/astryx#4239).

components.name: Tour
components.description: Controller for a guided tour. Coordinates the active step among its TourStep children, exposes advance / retreat / complete / dismiss, and optionally dims the page around the active step (spotlight cutout). Controlled via isActive: the consumer owns "has this user seen the tour?".

props.name: isActive
props.description: Whether the tour is running. When false nothing renders and the tour resets to the first step, so it restarts cleanly next time it becomes active.

props.name: children
props.description: The tour steps: TourStep elements. Step order follows their order here; only the active step renders its callout.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Called on every exit, with the reason ('backdrop' | 'escape' | 'close' | 'skip' | 'complete'). The consumer flips isActive to false in response, and can branch on the source to distinguish a successful finish from an early exit.

props.name: hasBackdrop
props.description: Dim the page around the active step as a spotlight cutout: the target stays lit while everything else darkens. Use for modal-style steps that demand focus; leave off for a lightweight coachmark that only rings the target.

props.name: isStepCountShown
props.description: Show the step count ("2 of 5") in each step.

components.name: TourStep
components.description: A single spotlight step. Highlights a target element with a ring drawn as a separate overlay (the target is never restyled) and renders a callout anchored to it (via the core Popover), with a heading, body, optional step progress, and back / next / close controls. Registers with the parent Tour on mount and renders its callout only while active.

props.name: targetRef
props.description: Ref to the element this step points at. The callout anchors to it like a Popover trigger; it must be a <button> or [role="button"] element (Popover's anchorRef contract).

props.name: heading
props.description: Step heading.

props.name: children
props.description: Step body content.

props.name: placement
props.description: Which side of the target the callout sits on.

props.name: alignment
props.description: How the callout aligns along the placement side (e.g. with placement="below": start left-aligns under the target, center centers, end right-aligns).

usage.description: Use a Tour to introduce a feature or onboard a user through a few key parts of the UI. Compose it from TourStep children, each pointing at an element via targetRef; the Tour advances through them with Next/Back and ends on Done. It is controlled: keep isActive in your own state and persist "has seen this tour" yourself (the component only reports dismissal via onDismiss). Built on the existing Popover/Layer anchoring and overlay tokens rather than a bespoke positioning engine.

bestPractices.description: Keep tours short: a few high-value steps. Long tours get skipped.
Persist completion yourself (from onDismiss) so a user does not see the same tour on every visit.
Point each step at a stable, visible element; ensure the target is on-screen before its step becomes active.
Gate essential, must-see information behind a tour step; users can dismiss it; put critical info inline.
Use a tour as a substitute for clear UI; fix confusing interfaces rather than narrating them.

docs.name: TransferListSelector
docs.description: A selector field for moving options between selected and available lists and optionally ordering the selected values. Changes commit immediately by default; staged commit behavior adds an internal draft and Apply/Cancel footer. TransferList remains the lower-level content primitive for custom ComplexSelector surfaces.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible field label shown outside the popover unless isLabelHidden is true.

props.name: options
props.description: Complete option pool. Each option has value and label, with optional searchable description metadata, group, an isTransferDisabled constraint, and disabledMessage. Which options keep their place is the reorderable object's isReorderable.

props.name: value
props.description: Committed selected values in display order. In staged behavior this is the applied value copied into a local draft when the selector opens.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called after every permitted list edit in immediate behavior, or once when Apply commits a changed draft in staged behavior.

props.name: commitBehavior
props.description: Controls when changes commit. Immediate updates on each list edit without a footer; staged waits for Apply and supports Cancel or dismiss.

props.name: triggerLabel
props.description: Content shown in the closed selector trigger.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting field guidance shown with the external label.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the field label while preserving its accessible name.

props.name: selectedLabel
props.description: Heading and accessible name for the selected list.

props.name: availableLabel
props.description: Heading and accessible name for the available list.

props.name: hasSearch
props.description: Shows a shared search field that filters both lists by label and description.

props.name: searchLabel
props.description: Accessible label for the shared search field.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.description: Placeholder shown in the shared search field.

props.name: reorderable
props.description: Makes the selected options reorderable: pass the object createReorderable makes. Each selected row ends with a reorder handle: on a touch screen hold the handle for a moment, then drag; a mouse drags at once; a tap, a click, Space or Enter on a handle turns on reorder mode for its row, in which each arrow key (or each move in the hint below the handle) moves it a place, and Escape, Done or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves. The object's isReorderable(value) says which values move: one it rejects has no handle, and at either end of the selected list it also keeps the others from moving past it. In immediate behavior each move goes to the object's onReorder({key, to}); in staged behavior the selector moves its draft instead, so Cancel drops the move with the draft and Apply commits it through onChange. Reordering pauses while a search filters the panel. Without it, the selected options keep their order.

props.name: hasSelectAll
props.description: Shows Add all and adds every transfer-enabled available option to the current selection.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows Clear and removes every transfer-enabled selected option from the current selection.

props.name: renderOption
props.description: Customizes row content while retaining built-in labels, actions, constraints, and reorder interaction.

props.name: selectedEmptyText
props.description: Message shown when the selected list is empty.

props.name: availableEmptyText
props.description: Message shown when every option has been selected.

props.name: noResultsText
props.description: Message shown when search has no matches in a list.

props.name: applyLabel
props.description: Label for the staged Apply action. Only valid with commitBehavior="staged".

props.name: cancelLabel
props.description: Label for the staged Cancel action. Only valid with commitBehavior="staged".

props.name: size
props.description: Trigger and field size.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field and its popup; both track this one value.

props.name: placement
props.description: Popover placement relative to the trigger.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Marks the field optional.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field required.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the selector trigger and transfer interaction.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows loading state on the trigger and disables transfer interaction while busy.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status for the field.

components.description: Lower-level controlled content primitive for advanced selector compositions that add custom headers, saved views, presets, or actions. Changes are immediate to its controlled value.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the complete transfer control.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the control label while retaining its accessible name.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting guidance shown below the control label.

props.name: options
props.description: Complete option pool with optional metadata, grouping, transfer constraints, and reorder constraints.

props.name: value
props.description: Selected option values in display order.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called immediately after a permitted option is added, removed, or bulk changed. Moves go to the reorderable object's onReorder instead.

props.name: selectedLabel
props.description: Heading and accessible name for the selected list.

props.name: availableLabel
props.description: Heading and accessible name for the available list.

props.name: hasSearch
props.description: Shows a shared search field that filters both lists by label and description.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables every transfer, reorder, Clear, Add all and search control. The row controls and the search field stay focusable.

props.name: searchLabel
props.description: Accessible label for the shared search field.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.description: Placeholder shown in the shared search field.

props.name: reorderable
props.description: Makes the selected options reorderable through a handle at the end of each row: pass the object createReorderable makes. Its isReorderable(value) decides which options move (one it rejects at either end of the list also keeps the others from moving past it), and each move goes to its onReorder({key, to}), to being the index of the value in value after the move. Without it, the selected options keep their order.

props.name: hasSelectAll
props.description: Shows Add all for transfer-enabled available options.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows Clear for transfer-enabled selected options; transfer-disabled values remain selected.

props.name: renderOption
props.description: Customizes row content without replacing built-in actions and constraints.

props.name: selectedEmptyText
props.description: Message shown when the selected list is empty.

props.name: availableEmptyText
props.description: Message shown when every option has been selected.

props.name: noResultsText
props.description: Message shown when search has no matches in a list.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the TransferList root.

usage.description: Use TransferListSelector by default for medium-to-large, inspectable sets where membership and selected order need explicit control. Immediate behavior commits each edit and renders no footer. Choose staged behavior when users must review a set of changes before Apply. Use TransferList directly only in a deliberately custom ComplexSelector surface, such as table column settings with saved views and a custom footer.

bestPractices.description: Start with immediate behavior. Add, remove, and bulk changes call onChange as they occur and moves call the reorderable object's onReorder, and closing or dismissing the popover keeps those committed changes.
Set commitBehavior="staged" when the complete selection should be reviewed or persisted as one transaction. Apply commits a changed draft; Cancel, Escape, and light dismiss discard it.

Use TransferList directly inside ComplexSelector only when the surface needs custom structure such as saved views, presets, headers, or footer actions. Keep applied and draft state separate and reset the draft whenever the surface opens.

Use isTransferDisabled and the reorderable object's isReorderable independently: isTransferDisabled pins an option to its panel, and isReorderable keeps an option in its place. Provide disabledMessage when a transfer is unavailable so the constraint is discoverable; a row that keeps its place shows no reorder handle, so say why in its content when it matters.

With no `reorderable`, TransferList no longer reorders; pass `reorderable={createReorderable(…)}`. Migrating from isReorderable: pass reorderable={createReorderable({onReorder, isReorderable})} instead. The isReorderable prop and each option's isReorderDisabled are gone; return false from the object's isReorderable(value) for an option that stays put.
Keep rows concise and single-line. Use option description as searchable metadata, or renderOption when richer visible content is necessary.

Commit add, remove, and bulk changes immediately. A drag leaves the rows still: the row dims in place, a copy of it follows the finger or pointer, and an insertion line marks where it would land; the reorderable object's onReorder runs once on release.
Use commitBehavior as a presentation or container choice. Both values render the same selector popover; use explicit composition for a different shell.
Use a transfer list for a handful of simple choices; CheckboxInput or MultiSelector is more compact.

anatomy.name: Field label and description
anatomy.description: Names and explains the selector outside the popover so placement does not change with supporting text.

anatomy.name: Selector trigger
anatomy.description: Summarizes the committed value and opens the transfer-list popover.

anatomy.name: Search
anatomy.description: Filters the selected and available lists without changing their values and uses a uniform 12px inset.

anatomy.name: Selected and available sections
anatomy.description: Places two unframed semantic lists beside one divider. Narrow containers stack the sections, use the body background behind each column header, expand both sections to their rows, and delegate overflow to one scrollable containing surface.

anatomy.name: Row actions
anatomy.description: Uses a direction-neutral X to remove and plus to add. Selected rows end with a reorder handle when reordering is enabled; a row that keeps its place has none, and transfer constraints disable the remove action.

anatomy.name: Reorder hint
anatomy.description: While a selected row is in reorder mode: the hint below its handle, whose Move up, Move down and Done are buttons.

anatomy.name: Bulk actions
anatomy.description: Optional Clear and Add all text actions that honor transfer-disabled options.

anatomy.name: Apply and Cancel footer
anatomy.description: Rendered only for staged behavior. Apply commits a changed draft; Cancel closes without changing the committed value.

anatomy.name: Live announcements
anatomy.description: Reports add, remove, bulk, and reorder results without relying on visual position alone.

docsDense.description: default-immediate transfer-list selector with optional staged commit behavior; TransferList is the advanced custom-composition primitive

usage.description: Use TransferListSelector with immediate behavior by default: each list edit commits and no footer renders. Use staged behavior to review a draft and commit from Apply. Use TransferList directly only inside a custom ComplexSelector surface with saved views, presets, or custom actions.

bestPractices.description: Default to immediate behavior; each edit calls onChange and dismiss keeps committed changes.
Use commitBehavior="staged" for review or transactional persistence; Apply commits and Cancel/Escape/light dismiss discard.
Use direct TransferList plus ComplexSelector only for custom saved views, presets, headers, or actions; reset draft from applied value on open.
Set transfer and reorder constraints independently and explain a locked transfer with disabledMessage.
Keep rows single-line; descriptions remain searchable metadata.
Use commitBehavior for presentation/container choice; both values use the selector popover.
Use for a few simple choices; prefer CheckboxInput.
